dathan_982.about: Welled; belonging to a fountain, a son of Eliab, a Reubenite, who joined Korah (q.v.) in his conspiracy, and with his accomplices was swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1; 26:9; Deut. 11:6; Ps. 106:17).

daughter_of_pharaoh_988.name: Daughter of Pharaoh
daughter_of_pharaoh_988.about: The princess who adopted the infant Moses (q.v.), Ex. 2:10. She is twice mentioned in the New Testament (Acts 7:21: Heb. 11:24). It would seem that she was alive and in some position of influence about the court when Moses was compelled to flee from Egypt, and thus for forty years he had in some way been under her influence. She was in all probability the sister of Rameses, and the daughter of Seti I. Josephus calls her Thermuthis.

daughter_of_pharaoh_989.name: Daughter of Pharaoh
daughter_of_pharaoh_989.about: The wife of Solomon (1 Kings 3:1). This is the first reference since the Exodus to any connection of Israel with Egypt.

david_994.name: David
david_994.about: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded. Some think she was the Nahash of 2 Sam. 17:25. As to his personal appearance, we only know that he was red-haired, with beautiful eyes and a fair face (1 Sam. 16:12; 17:42). His early occupation was that of tending his father’s sheep on the uplands of Judah.

debir_995.name: Debir
debir_995.about: The king of Eglon, one of the five Canaanitish kings who were hanged by Joshua (Josh. 10:3, 23) after the victory at Gibeon. These kings fled and took refuge in a cave at Makkedah. Here they were kept confined till Joshua returned from the pursuit of their discomfited armies, when he caused them to be brought forth, and “Joshua smote them, and slew them, and hanged them on five trees” (26).

deborah_997.name: Deborah
deborah_997.about: A prophetess, “wife” (woman?) of Lapidoth. Jabin, the king of Hazor, had for twenty years held Israel in degrading subjection. The spirit of patriotism seemed crushed out of the nation. In this emergency Deborah roused the people from their lethargy. Her fame spread far and wide.

dedan_998.name: Dedan (son of Raamah)
dedan_998.about: A son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7). His descendants are mentioned in Isa. 21:13, and Ezek. 27:15. They probably settled among the sons of Cush, on the north-west coast of the Persian Gulf.

dedan_999.name: Dedan (son of Jokshan)
dedan_999.about: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

delaiah_1001.name: Delaiah
delaiah_1001.about: The head of the twenty-third division of the priestly order (1 Chr. 24:18).

delaiah_1002.name: Delaiah
delaiah_1002.about: The head of one of the bands of exiles that returned under Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:60; Neh. 7:62).

delaiah_1004.name: Delaiah
delaiah_1004.about: A son of Shemaiah, and one of the courtiers to whom Jeremiah’s first roll of prophecy was read (Jer. 36:12).

delilah_1005.name: Delilah
delilah_1005.about: Languishing, a Philistine woman who dwelt in the valley of Sorek (Judg. 16:4-20). She was bribed by the “lords of the Philistines” to obtain from Samson the secret of his strength and the means of overcoming it (Judg. 16:4-18). She tried on three occasions to obtain from him this secret in vain. On the fourth occasion she wrung it from him.

demas_1006.name: Demas
demas_1006.about: A companion and fellow-labourer of Paul during his first imprisonment at Rome (Philemon 1:24; Col. 4:14). It appears, however, that the love of the world afterwards mastered him, and he deserted the apostle (2 Tim. 4:10).

demetrius_1007.name: Demetrius
demetrius_1007.about: A silversmith at Ephesus, whose chief occupation was to make “silver shrines for Diana” (q.v.), Acts 19:24, i.e., models either of the temple of Diana or of the statue of the goddess. This trade brought to him and his fellow-craftsmen “no small gain,” for these shrines found a ready sale among the countless thousands who came to this temple from all parts of Asia Minor.

diana_1008.name: Diana
diana_1008.about: So called by the Romans; called Artemis by the Greeks, the “great” goddess worshipped among heathen nations under various modifications. Her most noted temple was that at Ephesus. It was built outside the city walls, and was one of the seven wonders of the ancient world.

diblaim_1009.name: Diblaim
diblaim_1009.about: Doubled cakes, the mother of Gomer, who was Hosea’s wife (Hos. 1:3).

dinah_1012.name: Dinah
dinah_1012.about: Judged; vindicated, daughter of Jacob by Leah, and sister of Simeon and Levi (Gen. 30:21). She was seduced by Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite chief, when Jacob’s camp was in the neighbourhood of Shechem. This led to the terrible revenge of Simeon and Levi in putting the Shechemites to death (Gen. 34). Jacob makes frequent reference to this deed of blood with abhorrence and regret (Gen. 34:30; 49:5-7).

dionysius_1013.name: Dionysius
dionysius_1013.about: The Areopagite, one of Paul’s converts at Athens (Acts 17:34).

dishan_1015.name: Dishan
dishan_1015.about: Antelope, the youngest son of Seir the Horite, head of one of the tribes of Idumaea (Gen. 36:21, 28, 30).

dodanim_1018.name: Dodanim
dodanim_1018.about: Leaders, a race descended from Javan (Gen. 10:4). They are known in profane history as the Dardani, originally inhabiting Illyricum. They were a semi-Pelasgic race, and in the ethnographical table (Gen. 10) they are grouped with the Chittim (q.v.). In 1 Chr. 1:7, they are called Rodanim. The LXX. and the Samaritan Version also read Rhodii, whence some have concluded that the Rhodians, the inhabitants of the island of Rhodes, are meant.

dodo_1021.name: Dodo
dodo_1021.about: An Ahohite, father of Eleazar, who was one of David’s three heroes (2 Sam. 23:9; 1 Chr. 11:12). He was the same with Dodai mentioned in 1 Chr. 27:4.

dodo_1022.name: Dodo
dodo_1022.about: A Bethlehemite, and father of Elhanan, who was one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:24).

doeg_1023.name: Doeg
doeg_1023.about: Fearful, an Edomite, the chief overseer of Saul’s flocks (1 Sam. 21:7). At the command of Saul he slew the high priest Ahimelech (q.v.) at Nob, together with all the priests to the number of eighty-five persons. (Comp. Ps. 52, title.)

dorcas_2810.name: Dorcas
dorcas_2810.about: (in Greek called Dorcas), gazelle, a disciple at Joppa. She was distinguished for her alms-deeds and good works. Peter, who was sent for from Lydda on the occasion of her death, prayed over the dead body, and said, “Tabitha, arise.” And she opened her eyes and sat up; and Peter “gave her his hand, and raised her up; and calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive” (Acts 9:36-43).

drusilla_1024.name: Drusilla
drusilla_1024.about: Third and youngest daughter of Herod Agrippa I. (Acts 12:1-4, 20-23). Felix, the Roman procurator of Judea, induced her to leave her husband, Azizus, the king of Emesa, and become his wife. She was present with Felix when Paul reasoned of “righteousness, temperance, and judgment to come” (Acts 24:24). She and her son perished in the eruption of Mount Vesuvius, A.D. 79.

ebal_1026.name: Ebal (son of Shobal)
ebal_1026.about: A descendant of Seir the Horite (Gen. 36:23).

ebal_2227.name: Ebal (son of Joktan)
ebal_2227.about: A descendant of Eber (1 Chr. 1:22), called also Obal (Gen. 10:28).

ebed_1027.name: Ebed
ebed_1027.about: Slave, the father of Gaal, in whom the men of Shechem “put confidence” in their conspiracy against Abimelech (Judg. 9:26, 26, 30, 31).

eber_1030.name: Eber (Heber)
eber_1030.about: The third post-duluvian patriach after Shem (Gen. 10:24; 11:14). He is regarded as the founder of the Hebrew race (10:21; Num. 24:24). In Luke 3:35 he is called Heber.

eber_1031.name: Eber (a Benjamite)
eber_1031.about: The oldest of the three sons of Elpaal the Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:12).

eber_1032.name: Eber (Amok Family Head)
eber_1032.about: The head of the priestly family of Amok in the time of Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:20).

ebiasaph_19.name: Ebiasaph
ebiasaph_19.about: Father of gathering; the gatherer, the youngest of the three sons of Korah the Levite, head of a family of Korhites (Ex. 6:24); called Ebisaph (1 Chr. 6:37).

eden_1033.name: Eden
eden_1033.about: Son of Joah, and one of the Levites who assisted in reforming the public worship of the sanctuary in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

eder_1035.name: Eder
eder_1035.about: The second of the three sons of Mushi, of the family of Merari, appointed to the Levitical office (1 Chr. 23:23; 24:30).

eglah_1036.name: Eglah
eglah_1036.about: A heifer, one of David’s wives, and mother of Ithream (2 Sam. 3:5; 1 Chr. 3:3). According to a Jewish tradition she was Michal.

eglon_1037.name: Eglon
eglon_1037.about: Chieftain or king of one of the Moabite tribes (Judg. 3:12-14). Having entered into an alliance with Ammon and Amalek, he overran the trans-Jordanic region, and then crossing the Jordan, seized on Jericho, the “city of palm trees,” which had been by this time rebuilt, but not as a fortress. He made this city his capital, and kept Israel in subjection for eighteen years.

ehud_1039.name: Ehud
ehud_1039.about: The son of Gera, of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 3:15). After the death of Othniel the people again fell into idolatry, and Eglon, the king of Moab, uniting his bands with those of the Ammonites and the Amalekites, crossed the Jordan and took the city of Jericho, and for eighteen years held that whole district in subjection, exacting from it an annual tribute.

ehud_1040.name: Ehud
ehud_1040.about: A descendant of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10), his great-grandson.

elah_1043.name: Elah
elah_1043.about: One of the Edomite chiefs or “dukes” of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:41).

elah_1045.name: Elah
elah_1045.about: The son and successor of Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 16:8-10). He was killed while drunk by Zimri, one of the captains of his chariots, and was the last king of the line of Baasha. Thus was fullfilled the prophecy of Jehu (6, 7, 11-14).

elah_1046.name: Elah
elah_1046.about: The father of Hoshea, the last king of Israel (2 Kings 15:30; 17:1).

elah_1047.name: Elah
elah_1047.about: The second of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

elam_1049.name: Elam (son of Shem)
elam_1049.about: Highland, the son of Shem (Gen. 10:22), and the name of the country inhabited by his descendants (14:1, 9; Isa. 11:11; 21:2, etc.) lying to the east of Babylonia, and extending to the shore of the Mediterranean, a distance in a direct line of about 1,000 miles. The name Elam is an Assyrian word meaning “high.” “The inhabitants of Elam, or ‘the Highlands,’ to the east of Babylon, were called Elamites.

elasah_1056.name: Elasah
elasah_1056.about: The son of Shaphan, one of the two who were sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and also took charge of Jeremiah’s letter to the captives in Babylon (Jer. 29:3).

eldad_1058.name: Eldad
eldad_1058.about: Whom God has loved, one of the seventy elders whom Moses appointed (Num. 11:26, 27) to administer justice among the people. He, with Medad, prophesied in the camp instead of going with the rest to the tabernacle, as Moses had commanded. This incident was announced to Moses by Joshua, who thought their conduct in this respect irregular.

eleasah_1060.name: Eleasah
eleasah_1060.about: One of the descendants of Judah, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:39, “Eleasah”).

eleasah_1061.name: Eleasah
eleasah_1061.about: A descendant of king Saul (1 Chr. 8:37; 9:43).

eleazar_1062.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1062.about: The third son of Aaron (Ex. 6:23). His wife, a daughter of Putiel, bore him Phinehas (Ex. 6:25). After the death of Nadab and Abihu (Lev. 10:12; Num. 3:4) he was appointed to the charge of the sanctuary (Num. 3:32). On Mount Hor he was clothed with the sacred vestments, which Moses took from off his brother Aaron and put upon him as successor to his father in the high priest’s office, which he held for more than twenty years (Num. 20:25-29).

eleazar_1063.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1063.about: An inhabitant of Kirjath-jearim who was “sanctified” to take charge of the ark, although not allowed to touch it, while it remained in the house of his father Abinadab (1 Sam. 7:1, 2; comp. Num. 3:31; 4:15).

eleazar_1064.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1064.about: The son of Dodo the Ahohite, of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the three most eminent of David’s thirty-seven heroes (1 Chr. 11:12) who broke through the Philistine host and brought him water from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:9, 16).

eleazar_1065.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1065.about: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21, 22).

eleazar_1066.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1066.about: A son of Phinehas associated with the priests in taking charge of the sacred vessels brought back to Jerusalem after the Exile (Ezra 8:33).

elhanan_1070.name: Elhanan
elhanan_1070.about: A warrior of the time of David famed for his exploits.

elhanan_1071.name: Elhanan
elhanan_1071.about: The son of Dodo, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:24).

eli_1072.name: Eli
eli_1072.about: Ascent, the high priest when the ark was at Shiloh (1 Sam. 1:3, 9). He was the first of the line of Ithamar, Aaron’s fourth son (1 Chr. 24:3; comp. 2 Sam. 8:17), who held that office. The office remained in his family till the time of Abiathar (1 Kings 2:26, 27), whom Solomon deposed, and appointed Zadok, of the family of Eleazar, in his stead (35).

eliab_1073.name: Eliab
eliab_1073.about: A son of Helon, and chief of the tribe of Zebulun at the time of the census in the wilderness (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

eliab_1074.name: Eliab
eliab_1074.about: A Reubenite, son of Pallu (Num. 16:1, 12; 26:8, 9; Deut. 11:6).

eliab_1076.name: Eliab
eliab_1076.about: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in his stronghold in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:9).

eliada_1078.name: Eliada
eliada_1078.about: One of David’s sons born after his establishment in Jerusalem (2 Sam. 5:16).

eliada_1079.name: Eliada
eliada_1079.about: A mighty man of war, a Benjamite (2 Chr. 17:17).

eliadah_1080.name: Eliadah
eliadah_1080.about: An Aramite of Zobah, captain of a marauding band that troubled Solomon (1 Kings 11:23).

eliakim_1084.name: Eliakim
eliakim_1084.about: The son of Hilkiah, who was sent to receive the message of the invading Assyrians and report it to Isaiah (2 Kings 18:18; 19:2; Isa. 36:3; 37:2). In his office as governor of the palace of Hezekiah he succeeded Shebna (Isa. 22:15-25). He was a good man (Isa. 22:20; 2 Kings 18:37), and had a splendid and honourable career.

eliakim_1087.name: Eliakim
eliakim_1087.about: The son of Abiud, of the posterity of Zerubbabel (Matt. 1:13).

eliakim_1088.name: Eliakim
eliakim_1088.about: The son of Melea (Luke 3:30), and probably grandson of Nathan.

eliam_1089.name: Eliam
eliam_1089.about: The father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:3). In 1 Chr. 3:5 his name is Ammiel.

eliam_1090.name: Eliam
eliam_1090.about: This name also occurs as that of a Gilonite, the son of Ahithophel, and one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:34). perhaps these two were the same person.

eliashib_1094.name: Eliashib
eliashib_1094.about: A priest, head of one of the courses of the priests of the time of David (1 Chr. 24:12).

eliashib_1100.name: Eliashib
eliashib_1100.about: A high priest in the time of Ezra and Nehemiah (Neh. 12:22, 23). He rebuilt the eastern city wall (3:1), his own mansion being in that quarter, on the ridge Ophel (3:20, 21). His indulgence of Tobiah the Ammonite provoked the indignation of Nehemiah (13:4, 7).

eliathah_1102.name: Eliathah
eliathah_1102.about: To whom God will come, one of the foureen sons of the Levite Heman, and musician of the temple in the time of David (1 Chr. 25:4).

elidad_1103.name: Elidad
elidad_1103.about: Whom God has loved, son of Chislon, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin; one of those who were appointed to divide the Promised Land among the tribes (Num. 34:21).

eliel_1104.name: Eliel
eliel_1104.about: A chief of Manasseh, on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

eliel_1109.name: Eliel
eliel_1109.about: A Gadite who joined David in the hold at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:11).

eliel_1111.name: Eliel
eliel_1111.about: One of the overseers of the offerings in the reign of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 31:13).

eliezer_1113.name: Eliezer (Abraham's Steward)
eliezer_1113.about: “Of Damascus,” the “steward” (R.V., “possessor”) of Abraham’s house (Gen. 15:2, 3). It was probably he who headed the embassy sent by Abraham to the old home of his family in Padan-aram to seek a wife for his son Isaac. The account of this embassy is given at length in Gen. 24.

eliezer_1114.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1114.about: One of the two sons of Moses, born during his sojourn in Midian (Ex. 18:4; 1 Chr. 23:15, 17). He remained with his mother and brother Gershom with Jethro when Moses returned to Egypt. (Ex. 18:4). They were restored to Moses when Jethro heard of his departure out of Egypt.

eliezer_1115.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1115.about: The son of Becher, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:8).

eliezer_1116.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1116.about: One of the priests who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

eliezer_1117.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1117.about: Son of Zichri, and chief of the Reubenites under David (1 Chr. 27:16).

eliezer_1118.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1118.about: A prophet in the time of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 20:37). Others of this name are mentioned Luke 3:29; Ezra 8:16; 10:18, 23, 31.

elihu_1126.name: Elihu
elihu_1126.about: The son of Tohu, and grandfather of Elkanah (1 Sam. 1:1). He is called also Eliel (1 Chr. 6:34) and Eliab (6:27).

elihu_1127.name: Elihu
elihu_1127.about: One of the captains of thousands of Manasseh who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

elihu_1128.name: Elihu
elihu_1128.about: One of the family of Obed-edom, who were appointed porters of the temple under David (1 Chr. 26:7).

elihu_1130.name: Elihu
elihu_1130.about: “The son of Barachel, a Buzite” (Job 32:2), one of Job’s friends. When the debate between Job and his friends is brought to a close, Elihu for the first time makes his appearance, and delivers his opinion on the points at issue (Job 32-37).

elijah_1131.name: Elijah
elijah_1131.about: “The Tishbite,” the “Elias” of the New Testament, is suddenly introduced to our notice in 1 Kings 17:1 as delivering a message from the Lord to Ahab. There is mention made of a town called Thisbe, south of Kadesh, but it is impossible to say whether this was the place referred to in the name given to the prophet.

elika_1133.name: Elika
elika_1133.about: God is his rejector, one of David’s thirty-seven distinguished heros (2 Sam. 23:25).

elimelech_1134.name: Elimelech
elimelech_1134.about: God his king, a man of the tribe of Judah, of the family of the Hezronites, and kinsman of Boaz, who dwelt in Bethlehem in the days of the judges. In consequence of a great dearth he, with his wife Naomi and his two sons, went to dwell in the land of Moab. There he and his sons died (Ruth 1:2, 3; 2:1, 3; 4:3, 9). Naomi afterwards returned to Palestine with her daughter Ruth.

eliphalet_1143.name: Eliphalet
eliphalet_1143.about: God his deliverance, one of David’s sons (2 Sam. 5:16); called also Eliphelet (1 Chr. 3:8).

eliphaz_1144.name: Eliphaz
eliphaz_1144.about: The son of Esau by his wife Adah, and father of several Edomitish tribes (Gen. 36:4, 10, 11, 16).

elipheleh_1146.name: Elipheleh
elipheleh_1146.about: God will distinguish him, one of the porters appointed to play “on the Sheminith” on the occasion of the bringing up of the ark to the city of David (1 Chr. 15:18, 21).

eliphelet_1147.name: Eliphelet
eliphelet_1147.about: One of David’s distinguished warriors (2 Sam. 23:34); called also Eliphal in 1 Chr. 11:35.

eliphelet_1149.name: Eliphelet
eliphelet_1149.about: A descendant of king Saul through Jonathan (1 Chr. 8:39).

elisabeth_1152.name: Elisabeth
elisabeth_1152.about: God her oath, the mother of John the Baptist (Luke 1:5). She was a descendant of Aaron. She and her husband Zacharias (q.v.) “were both righteous before God” (Luke 1:5, 13). Mary’s visit to Elisabeth is described in 1:39-63.

elisha_1153.name: Elisha
elisha_1153.about: God his salvation, the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah, who became the attendant and disciple of Elijah (1 Kings 19:16-19). His name first occurs in the command given to Elijah to anoint him as his successor (1 Kings 19:16). This was the only one of the three commands then given to Elijah which he accomplished.

elishah_1154.name: Elishah
elishah_1154.about: The oldest of the four sons of Javan (Gen. 10:4), whose descendants peopled Greece. It has been supposed that Elishah’s descendants peopled the Peloponnesus, which was known by the name of Elis. This may be meant by “the isles of Elishah” (Ezek. 27:7).

elishama_1155.name: Elishama
elishama_1155.about: A prince of Benjamin, grandfather of Joshua (Num. 1:10; 1 Chr. 7:26).

elishama_1159.name: Elishama
elishama_1159.about: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the people the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

elishaphat_1161.name: Elishaphat
elishaphat_1161.about: Whom God has judged, one of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in the league to overthrow the usurpation of Athaliah (2 Chr. 23:1).

elisheba_1162.name: Elisheba
elisheba_1162.about: God is her oath, the daughter of Amminadab and the wife of Aaron (Ex. 6:23).

elishua_1163.name: Elishua
elishua_1163.about: God his salvation, a son of David, 2 Sam. 5:15 = Elishama, 1 Chr. 3:6.

elkanah_1167.name: Elkanah
elkanah_1167.about: The second son of Korah (Ex. 6:24), or, according to 1 Chr. 6:22, 23, more correctly his grandson.

elkanah_1168.name: Elkanah
elkanah_1168.about: Another Levite of the line of Heman the singer, although he does not seem to have performed any of the usual Levitical offices. He was father of Samuel the prophet (1 Chr. 6:27, 34). He was “an Ephrathite” (1 Sam. 1:1, 4, 8), but lived at Ramah, a man of wealth and high position. He had two wives, Hannah, who was the mother of Samuel, and Peninnah.

elon_1182.name: Elon
elon_1182.about: A Hittite, father of Bashemath, Esau’s wife (Gen. 26:34).

elon_1183.name: Elon
elon_1183.about: One of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

elon_1184.name: Elon
elon_1184.about: The eleventh of the Hebrew judges. He held office for ten years (Judg. 12:11, 12). He is called the Zebulonite.

elymas_403.name: Elymas
elymas_403.about: Magician or sorcerer, the Arabic name of the Jew Bar-jesus, who withstood Paul and Barnabas in Cyprus. He was miraculously struck with blindness (Acts 13:11).

enoch_1191.name: Enoch (son of Cain)
enoch_1191.about: The eldest son of Cain (Gen. 4:17), who built a city east of Eden in the land of Nod, and called it “after the name of his son Enoch.” This is the first “city” mentioned in Scripture.

enoch_1192.name: Enoch (father of Methuselah)
enoch_1192.about: The son of Jared, and father of Methuselah (Gen. 5:21; Luke 3:37). His father was one hundred and sixty-two years old when he was born. After the birth of Methuselah, Enoch “walked with God three hundred years” (Gen. 5:22-24), when he was translated without tasting death. His whole life on earth was three hundred and sixty-five years. He was the “seventh from Adam” (Jude 1:14), as distinguished from the son of Cain, the third from Adam.

enos_1193.name: Enos
enos_1193.about: Man the son of Seth, and grandson of Adam (Gen. 5:6-11; Luke 3:38). He lived nine hundred and five years. In his time “men began to call upon the name of the Lord” (Gen. 4:26), meaning either (1) then began men to call themselves by the name of the Lord (marg.) i.e., to distinguish themselves thereby from idolaters; or (2) then men in some public and earnest way began to call upon the Lord, indicating a time of spiritual revival.

epaenetus_1194.name: Epaenetus
epaenetus_1194.about: Commendable, a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutation (Rom. 16:5). He is spoken of as “the first fruits of Achaia” (R.V., “of Asia”, i.e., of proconsular Asia, which is probably the correct reading). As being the first convert in that region, he was peculiarly dear to the apostle. He calls him his “well beloved.”

epaphras_1195.name: Epaphras
epaphras_1195.about: Lovely, spoken of by Paul (Col. 1:7; 4:12) as “his dear fellow-servant,” and “a faithful minister of Christ.” He was thus evidently with him at Rome when he wrote to the Colossians. He was a distinguished disciple, and probably the founder of the Colossian church. He is also mentioned in the Epistle to Philemon (1:23), where he is called by Paul his “fellow-prisoner.”

ephah_1199.name: Ephah
ephah_1199.about: 1 Chr. 2:47, a descendant of Judah. Ephah, a word of Egyptian origin, meaning measure; a grain measure containing “three seahs or ten omers,” and equivalent to the bath for liquids (Ex. 16:36; 1 Sam. 17:17; Zech. 5:6). The double ephah in Prov. 20:10 (marg., “an ephah and an ephah”), Deut. 25:14, means two ephahs, the one false and the other just.

epher_1201.name: Epher
epher_1201.about: One of the sons of Midian, who was Abraham’s son by Keturah (Gen. 25:4).

epher_1203.name: Epher
epher_1203.about: The head of one of the families of trans-Jordanic Manasseh who were carried captive by Tiglath-pileser (1 Chr. 5:24).

ephraim_1206.name: Ephraim
ephraim_1206.about: Double fruitfulness (“for God had made him fruitful in the land of his affliction”). The second son of Joseph, born in Egypt (Gen. 41:52; 46:20). The first incident recorded regarding him is his being placed, along with his brother Manasseh, before their grandfather, Jacob, that he might bless them (48:10; comp. 27:1).

ephratah_1207.name: Ephratah
ephratah_1207.about: The second wife of Caleb, the son of Hezron, mother of Hur, and grandmother of Caleb, who was one of those that were sent to spy the land (1 Chr. 2:19, 50).

ephron_1208.name: Ephron
ephron_1208.about: The son of Zohar a Hittite, the owner of the field and cave of Machpelah (q.v.), which Abraham bought for 400 shekels of silver (Gen. 23:8-17; 25:9; 49:29, 30).

erastus_1213.name: Erastus
erastus_1213.about: A companion of Paul at Ephesus, who was sent by him along with Timothy into Macedonia (Acts 19:22). Corinth was his usual place of abode (2 Tim. 4:20); but probably he may have been the same as the preceding.

esau_1216.name: Esau (Edom)
esau_1216.about: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31). The circumstances connected with his birth foreshadowed the enmity which afterwards subsisted between the twin brothers and the nations they founded (25:22, 23, 26).

eshcol_1218.name: Eshcol
eshcol_1218.about: A young Amoritish chief who joined Abraham in the recovery of Lot from the hands of Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:13, 24).

esther_1343.name: Esther
esther_1343.about: The queen of Ahasuerus, and heroine of the book that bears her name. She was a Jewess named Hadas’sah (the myrtle), but when she entered the royal harem she received the name by which she henceforth became known (Esther 2:7). It is a Syro-Arabian modification of the Persian word satarah, which means a star. She was the daughter of Abihail, a Benjamite.

ethan_1222.name: Ethan
ethan_1222.about: “The Ezrahite,” distinguished for his wisdom (1 Kings 4:31). He is named as the author of the 89th Psalm. He was of the tribe of Levi.

ethan_1622.name: Ethan
ethan_1622.about: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 6:21), probably the same as Ethan (42).

ethbaal_1225.name: Ethbaal
ethbaal_1225.about: With Baal, a king of Sidon (B.C. 940-908), father of Jezebel, who was the wife of Ahab (1 Kings 16:31). He is said to have been also a priest of Astarte, whose worship was closely allied to that of Baal, and this may account for his daughter’s zeal in promoting idolatry in Israel. This marriage of Ahab was most fatal to both Israel and Judah. Dido, the founder of Carthage, was his granddaughter.

euodias_1229.name: Euodias
euodias_1229.about: A good journey, a female member of the church at Philippi. She was one who laboured much with Paul in the gospel. He exhorts her to be of one mind with Syntyche (Phil. 4:2). From this it seems they had been at variance with each other.

eutychus_1230.name: Eutychus
eutychus_1230.about: Fortunate, (Acts 20:9-12), a young man of Troas who fell through drowsiness from the open window of the third floor of the house where Paul was preaching, and was “taken up dead.” The lattice-work of the window being open to admit the air, the lad fell out and down to the court below. Paul restored him to life again. (Comp. 1 Kings 17:21; 2 Kings 4:34.)

eve_1231.name: Eve
eve_1231.about: Life; living, the name given by Adam to his wife (Gen. 3:20; 4:1). The account of her creation is given in Gen. 2:21, 22. The Creator, by declaring that it was not good for man to be alone, and by creating for him a suitable companion, gave sanction to monogamy. The commentator Matthew Henry says: “This companion was taken from his side to signify that she was to be dear unto him as his own flesh.

evil-merodach_1233.name: Evil-merodach
evil-merodach_1233.about: Merodach’s man, the son and successor of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (2 Kings 25:27; Jer. 52:31, 34). He seems to have reigned but two years (B.C. 562-560). Influenced probably by Daniel, he showed kindness to Jehoiachin, who had been a prisoner in Babylon for thirty-seven years. He released him, and “spoke kindly to him.” He was murdered by Nergal-sharezer=Neriglissar, his brother-in-law, who succeeded him (Jer. 39:3, 13).

ezekiel_1237.name: Ezekiel
ezekiel_1237.about: One of the great prophets, the son of Buzi the priest (Ezek. 1:3). He was one of the Jewish exiles who settled at Tel-Abib, on the banks of the Chebar, “in the land of the Chaldeans.” He was probably carried away captive with Jehoiachin (1:2; 2 Kings 24:14-16) about B.C. 597. His prophetic call came to him “in the fifth year of Jehoiachin’s captivity” (B.C. 594).

ezer_1238.name: Ezer
ezer_1238.about: One of the sons of Seir, the native princes, “dukes,” of Mount Hor (Gen. 36:21, 27).

ezra_1245.name: Ezra
ezra_1245.about: The “scribe” who led the second body of exiles that returned from Babylon to Jerusalem B.C. 459, and author of the book of Scripture which bears his name. He was the son, or perhaps grandson, of Seraiah (2 Kings 25:18-21), and a lineal descendant of Phinehas, the son of Aaron (Ezra 7:1-5). All we know of his personal history is contained in the last four chapters of his book, and in Neh. 8 and 12:26.

ezra_1246.name: Ezra
ezra_1246.about: A priest among those that returned to Jerusalem under Zerubabel (Neh. 12:1).

ezri_1247.name: Ezri
ezri_1247.about: Help of Jehovah, the son of Chelub. He superintended, under David, those who “did the work of the field for tillage” (1 Chr. 27:26).

felix_1257.name: Felix
felix_1257.about: Happy, the Roman procurator of Judea before whom Paul “reasoned” (Acts 24:25). He appears to have expected a bribe from Paul, and therefore had several interviews with him. The “worthy deeds” referred to in 24:2 was his clearing the country of banditti and impostors.

fortunatus_1258.name: Fortunatus
fortunatus_1258.about: Fortunate, a disciple of Corinth who visited Paul at Ephesus, and returned with Stephanas and Achaicus, the bearers of the apostle’s first letter to the Corinthians (1 Cor. 16:17).

gaal_1259.name: Gaal
gaal_1259.about: Loathing, the son of Ebed, in whom the Shechemites “placed their confidence” when they became discontented with Abimelech. He headed the revolution, and led out the men of Shechem against Abimelech; but was defeated, and fled to his own home (Judg. 9:26-46). We hear no more of him after this battle.

gabriel_1261.name: Gabriel
gabriel_1261.about: Champion of God, used as a proper name to designate the angel who was sent to Daniel (8:16) to explain the vision of the ram and the he-goat, and to communicate the prediction of the seventy weeks (Dan. 9:21-27). He announced also the birth of John the Baptist (Luke 1:11), and of the Messiah (26). He describes himself in the words, “I am Gabriel, who stand in the presence of God” (1:19).

gad_1262.name: Gad
gad_1262.about: Jacob’s seventh son, by Zilpah, Leah’s handmaid, and the brother of Asher (Gen. 30:11-13; 46:16, 18). In the Authorized Version of 30:11 the words, “A troop cometh: and she called,” etc., should rather be rendered, “In fortune [R.V., ‘Fortunate’]: and she called,” etc., or “Fortune cometh,” etc. The tribe of Gad during the march through the wilderness had their place with Simeon and Reuben on the south side of the tabernacle (Num. 2:14).

gad_1263.name: Gad
gad_1263.about: A prophet who joined David in the “hold,” and at whose advice he quitted it for the forest of Hareth (1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr. 29:25; 1 Sam. 22:5). Many years after we find mention made of him in connection with the punishment inflicted for numbering the people (2 Sam. 24:11-19; 1 Chr. 21:9-19). He wrote a book called the “Acts of David” (1 Chr. 29:29), and assisted in the arrangements for the musical services of the “house of God” (2 Chr. 29:25).

gaddi_1264.name: Gaddi
gaddi_1264.about: Fortunate, the representative of the tribe of Manasseh among the twelve “spies” sent by Moses to spy the land (Num. 13:11).

gaddiel_1265.name: Gaddiel
gaddiel_1265.about: Fortune (i.e., sent) of God, the representative of the tribe of Zebulum among the twelve spies (Num. 13:10).

gahar_1268.name: Gahar
gahar_1268.about: Lurking-place, one of the chief of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:47).

gaius_1269.name: Gaius (of Macedonia)
gaius_1269.about: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into the theatre. Some have identified this Gaius with No. (2).

gaius_1270.name: Gaius (of Derbe)
gaius_1270.about: A man of Derbe who accompanied Paul into Asia on his last journey to Jerusalem

gaius_1271.name: Gaius
gaius_1271.about: A Macedonian, Paul’s fellow-traveller, and his host at Corinth when he wrote his Epistle to the Romans (16:23). He with his household were baptized by Paul (1 Cor. 1:14). During a heathen outbreak against Paul at Ephesus the mob seized Gaius and Aristarchus because they could not find Paul, and rushed with them into the theatre. Some have identified this Gaius with No. (2).

gaius_1272.name: Gaius
gaius_1272.about: A Christain of Asia Minor to whom John addressed his third epistle (3 John 1:1).

gallio_1275.name: Gallio
gallio_1275.about: The elder brother of Seneca the philosopher, who was tutor and for some time minister of the emperor Nero. He was “deputy”, i.e., proconsul, as in Revised Version, of Achaia, under the emperor Claudius, when Paul visited Corinth (Acts 18:12). The word used here by Luke in describing the rank of Gallio shows his accuracy.

gamaliel_1276.name: Gamaliel
gamaliel_1276.about: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh at the census at Sinai (Num. 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59).

gamaliel_1277.name: Gamaliel
gamaliel_1277.about: The son of rabbi Simeon, and grandson of the famous rabbi Hillel. He was a Pharisse, and therefore the opponent of the party of the Sadducees. He was noted for his learning, and was president of the Sanhedrim during the regins of Tiberius, Caligula, and Claudius, and died, it is said, about eighteen years before the destruction of Jerusalem.

gamul_1278.name: Gamul
gamul_1278.about: Weaned the leader of one of the priestly courses (1 Chr. 24:17).

gareb_1279.name: Gareb
gareb_1279.about: One of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:38), an Ithrite.

geber_1286.name: Geber
geber_1286.about: A valiant man, (1 Kings 4:19), one of Solomon’s purveyors, having jurisdiction over a part of Gilead, comprising all the kingdom of Sihon and part of the kingdom of Og (Deut. 2; 31).

gedaliah_1287.name: Gedaliah
gedaliah_1287.about: The son of Ahikam, and grandson of Shaphan, secretary of king Josiah (Jer. 26:24). After the destruction of Jerusalem (see ZEDEKIAH), Nebuchadnezzar left him to govern the country as tributary to him (2 Kings 25:22; Jer. 40:5; 52:16).

gedaliah_1290.name: Gedaliah
gedaliah_1290.about: One of the Jewish nobles who conspired against Jeremiah (Jer. 38:1).

gehazi_1293.name: Gehazi
gehazi_1293.about: Valley of vision, Elisha’s trusted servant (2 Kings 4:31; 5:25; 8:4, 5). He appears in connection with the history of the Shunammite (2 Kings 4:14, 31) and of Naaman the Syrian. On this latter occasion he was guilty of duplicity and dishonesty of conduct, causing Elisha to denounce his crime with righteous sternness, and pass on him the terrible doom that the leprosy of Naaman would cleave to him and his for ever (5:20-27).

gemariah_1295.name: Gemariah
gemariah_1295.about: The son of Hilkiah, who accompanied Shaphan with the tribute-money from Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar, and was the bearer at the same time of a letter from Jeremiah to the Jewish captives at Babylon (Jer. 29:3, 4).

gemariah_1296.name: Gemariah
gemariah_1296.about: The son of Shaphan, and one of the Levites of the temple in the time of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:10; 2 Kings 22:12). Baruch read aloud to the people from Gemariah’s chamber, and again in the hearing of Gemariah and other scribes, the prophecies of Jeremiah (Jer. 36:11-20), which filled him with terror. He joined with others in entreating the king not to destroy the roll of the prophecies which Baruch had read (21-25).

genubath_1297.name: Genubath
genubath_1297.about: Theft, the son of Hadad, of the Edomitish royal family. He was brought up in Pharaoh’s household. His mother was a sister of Tahpenes, the king of Egypt’s wife, mentioned in 1 Kings 11:20.

gera_1298.name: Gera
gera_1298.about: The father of Ehud the judge (Judg. 3:15).

gera_1299.name: Gera
gera_1299.about: The father of Shimei, who so grossly abused David (2 Sam. 16:5; 19:16, 18).

gershom_1302.name: Gershom
gershom_1302.about: The elder of the two sons of Moses born to him in Midian (Ex. 2:22; 18:3). On his way to Egypt with his family, in obedience to the command of the Lord, Moses was attacked by a sudden and dangerous illness (4:24-26), which Zipporah his wife believed to have been sent because he had neglected to circumcise his son.

gershom_1303.name: Gershom
gershom_1303.about: The son of Manasseh (Judg. 18:30), in R.V. “of Moses.”

gershom_1304.name: Gershom
gershom_1304.about: A descendant of Phinehas who returned with Ezra from Babylon (Ezra 8:2).

gershon_1305.name: Gershon
gershon_1305.about: '=Ger’shom expulsion, the eldest of Levi’s three sons (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16). In the wilderness the sons of Gershon had charge of the fabrics of the tabernacle when it was moved from place to place, the curtains, veils, tent-hangings (Num. 3: 21-26). Thirteen Levitical cities fell to the lot of the Gershonites (Josh. 21:27-33).

geshem_1307.name: Geshem
geshem_1307.about: Or Gashmu, firmness, probably chief of the Arabs south of Palestine, one of the enemies of the Jews after the return from Babylon (Neh. 2:19; 6:1, 2). He united with Sanballat and Tobiah in opposing the rebuilding of the wall of Jerusalem.

gideon_1314.name: Gideon
gideon_1314.about: Called also Jerubbaal (Judg. 6:29, 32), was the first of the judges whose history is circumstantially narrated (Judg. 6-8). His calling is the commencement of the second period in the history of the judges.

girgasite_1322.name: Girgasite
girgasite_1322.about: Dwelling in clayey soil, the descendants of the fifth son of Canaan (Gen. 10:16), one of the original tribes inhabiting the land of Canaan before the time of the Israelites (Gen. 15:21; Deut. 7:1). They were a branch of the great family of the Hivites. Of their geographical position nothing is certainly known. Probably they lived somewhere in the central part of Western Palestine.

god_1324.name: God
god_1324.about: (A.S. and Dutch God; Dan. Gud; Ger. Gott), the name of the Divine Being. It is the rendering (1) of the Hebrew ’El, from a word meaning to be strong; (2) of ’Eloah_, plural _’Elohim. The singular form, Eloah, is used only in poetry.

gog_1325.name: Gog
gog_1325.about: A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:4), the father of Shimei.

goliath_1327.name: Goliath
goliath_1327.about: A famous giant of Gath, who for forty days openly defied the armies of Israel, but was at length slain by David with a stone from a sling (1 Sam. 17:4). He was probably descended from the Rephaim who found refuge among the Philistines after they were dispersed by the Ammonites (Deut. 2:20, 21). His height was “six cubits and a span,” which, taking the cubit at 21 inches, is equal to 10 1/2 feet.

gomer_1328.name: Gomer (son of Japheth)
gomer_1328.about: The eldest son of Japheth, and father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah (Gen. 10:2, 3), whose descendants formed the principal branch of the population of South-eastern Europe. He is generally regarded as the ancestor of the Celtae and the Cimmerii, who in early times settled to the north of the Black Sea, and gave their name to the Crimea, the ancient Chersonesus Taurica.

hadad_1338.name: Hadad
hadad_1338.about: An Edomite king who defeated the Midianites (Gen. 36:35; 1 Chr. 1:46).

hadad_1339.name: Hadad
hadad_1339.about: One of “the king’s seed in Edom.” He fled into Egypt, where he married the sister of Pharaoh’s wife (1 Kings 11:14-22). He became one of Solomon’s adversaries. Hadad, sharp, (a different name in Hebrew from the preceding), one of the sons of Ishmael (1 Chr. 1:30). Called also Hadar (Gen. 25:15).

hadad_1342.name: Hadad
hadad_1342.about: One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul. Called also Hadad (1 Chr. 1:50, 51). It is probable that in these cases Hadar may be an error simply of transcription for Hadad.

hadar_1341.name: Hadar
hadar_1341.about: A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad.

hadarezer_1340.name: Hadarezer
hadarezer_1340.about: Hadad is help; called also Hadarezer, Adod is his help, the king of Zobah. Hanun, the king of the Ammonites, hired among others the army of Hadadezer to assist him in his war against David. Joab, who was sent against this confederate host, found them in double battle array, the Ammonities toward their capital of Rabbah, and the Syrian mercenaries near Medeba.

hadlai_1344.name: Hadlai
hadlai_1344.about: Resting, an Ephraimite; the father of Amasa, mentioned in 2 Chr. 28:12.

hadoram_1345.name: Hadoram
hadoram_1345.about: The fifth son of Joktan, the founder of an Arab tribe (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21).

hagar_1348.name: Hagar
hagar_1348.about: Flight, or, according to others, stranger, an Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid (Gen. 16:1; 21:9, 10), whom she gave to Abraham (q.v.) as a secondary wife (16:2). When she was about to become a mother she fled from the cruelty of her mistress, intending apparently to return to her relatives in Egypt, through the desert of Shur, which lay between.

haggai_1349.name: Haggai
haggai_1349.about: Festive, one of the twelve so-called minor prophets. He was the first of the three (Zechariah, his contemporary, and Malachi, who was about one hundred years later, being the other two) whose ministry belonged to the period of Jewish history which began after the return from captivity in Babylon. Scarcely anything is known of his personal history. He may have been one of the captives taken to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.

haggith_1353.name: Haggith
haggith_1353.about: Festive; the dancer, a wife of David and the mother of Adonijah (2 Sam. 3:4; 1 Kings 1:5, 11; 2:13; 1 Chr. 3:2), who, like Absalom, was famed for his beauty.

hakkoz_1355.name: Hakkoz
hakkoz_1355.about: The thorn, the head of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:10).

ham_1359.name: Ham
ham_1359.about: Warm, hot, and hence the south; also an Egyptian word meaning “black”, the youngest son of Noah (Gen. 5:32; comp. 9:22, 24). The curse pronounced by Noah against Ham, properly against Canaan his fourth son, was accomplished when the Jews subsequently exterminated the Canaanites. One of the most important facts recorded in Gen. 10 is the foundation of the earliest monarchy in Babylonia by Nimrod the grandson of Ham (6, 8, 10).

haman_1360.name: Haman
haman_1360.about: (of Persian origin), magnificent, the name of the vizier (i.e., the prime minister) of the Persian king Ahasuerus (Esther 3:1, etc.). He is called an “Agagite,” which seems to denote that he was descended from the royal family of the Amalekites, the bitterest enemies of the Jews, as Agag was one of the titles of the Amalekite kings. He or his parents were brought to Persia as captives taken in war.

hammedatha_1362.name: Hammedatha
hammedatha_1362.about: Father of Haman, designated usually “the Agagite” (Esther 3:1, 10; 8:5).

hammelech_1363.name: Hammelech
hammelech_1363.about: The king’s, the father of Jerahmeel, mentioned in Jer. 36:26. Some take this word as a common noun, “the king”, and understand that Jerahmeel was Jehoiakim’s son. Probably, however, it is to be taken as a proper name.

hammoleketh_1364.name: Hammoleketh
hammoleketh_1364.about: The queen, the daughter of Machir and sister of Gilead (1 Chr. 7:17, 18). Abiezer was one of her three children.

hamor_1365.name: Hamor
hamor_1365.about: He-ass, a Hivite from whom Jacob purchased the plot of ground in which Joseph was afterwards buried (Gen. 33:19). He is called “Emmor” in Acts 7:16. His son Shechem founded the city of that name which Simeon and Levi destroyed because of his crime in the matter of Dinah, Jacob’s daughter (Gen. 34:20). Hamor and Shechem were also slain (ver. 26).

hamul_1367.name: Hamul
hamul_1367.about: Spared, one of the sons of Pharez, son of Judah (1 Chr. 2:5). His descendants are called Hamulites (Num. 26:21).

hamutal_1368.name: Hamutal
hamutal_1368.about: Kinsman of the dew, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, wife of king Josiah, and mother of king Jehoahaz (2 Kings 23:31), also of king Zedekiah (2 Kings 24:18).

hanameel_1369.name: Hanameel
hanameel_1369.about: Whom God has graciously given, the cousin of Jeremiah, to whom he sold the field he possessed in Anathoth, before the siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 32:6-12).

hanan_1374.name: Hanan
hanan_1374.about: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra (Neh. 8:7).

hanan_1375.name: Hanan
hanan_1375.about: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:22).

hanani_1379.name: Hanani
hanani_1379.about: A prophet who was sent to rebuke king Asa for entering into a league with Benhadad I., king of Syria, against Judah (2 Chr. 16:1-10). He was probably the father of the prophet Jehu (1 Kings 16:7).

hanani_1380.name: Hanani
hanani_1380.about: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 25).

hanani_1382.name: Hanani
hanani_1382.about: Probably a brother of Nehemiah (Neh. 1:2; 7:2), who reported to him the melancholy condition of Jerusalem. Nehemiah afterwards appointed him to have charge of the city gates.

hananiah_1385.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1385.about: A chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:24).

hananiah_1386.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1386.about: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4, 23).

hananiah_1387.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1387.about: One of Uzziah’s military officers (2 Chr. 26:11).

hananiah_1391.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1391.about: The “ruler of the palace; he was a faithful man, and feared God above many” (Neh. 7:2).

hananiah_1397.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1397.about: Grandfather of the captain who arrested Jeremiah (Jer. 37:13).

haniel_1399.name: Haniel
haniel_1399.about: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:39).

hannah_1400.name: Hannah
hannah_1400.about: Favour, grace, one of the wives of Elkanah the Levite, and the mother of Samuel (1 Sam. 1; 2). Her home was at Ramathaim-zophim, whence she was wont every year to go to Shiloh, where the tabernacle had been pitched by Joshua, to attend the offering of sacrifices there according to the law (Ex. 23:15; 34:18; Deut. 16:16), probably at the feast of the Passover (comp. Ex. 13:10).

hanniel_1401.name: Hanniel
hanniel_1401.about: A chief of the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 34:23).

hanun_1404.name: Hanun
hanun_1404.about: The son and successor of Nahash, king of Moab. David’s messengers, sent on an embassy of condolence to him to Rabbah Ammon, his capital, were so grossly insulted that he proclaimed war against Hanun. David’s army, under the command of Joab, forthwith crossed the Jordan, and gained a complete victory over the Moabites and their allies (2 Sam. 10:1-14) at Medeba (q.v.).

haran_1407.name: Haran (brother of Abraham)
haran_1407.about: Heb. haran; i.e., “mountaineer.” The eldest son of Terah, brother of Abraham and Nahor, and father of Lot, Milcah, and Iscah. He died before his father (Gen. 11:27), in Ur of the Chaldees.

haran_1408.name: Haran (son of Caleb)
haran_1408.about: The son of Caleb of Judah (1 Chr. 2:46) by his concubine Ephah.

harbona_1410.name: Harbona
harbona_1410.about: (a Persian word meaning “ass-driver”), one of the seven eunuchs or chamberlains of king Ahasuerus (Esther 1:10; 7:9).

harhaiah_1413.name: Harhaiah
harhaiah_1413.about: Zeal of Jehovah, (Neh. 3:8) “of the goldsmiths,” one whose son helped to repair the wall of Jerusalem.

harim_1416.name: Harim
harim_1416.about: The head of the second course of priests (1 Chr. 24:8).

harnepher_1420.name: Harnepher
harnepher_1420.about: A chief of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:36).

harsha_1422.name: Harsha
harsha_1422.about: Worker or enchanter, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:52; Neh. 7:54).

harum_1423.name: Harum
harum_1423.about: Elevated, (1 Chr. 4:8), a descendant of Judah.

haruz_1425.name: Haruz
haruz_1425.about: Eager, the father of Meshullemeth, the wife of king Manasseh (2 Kings 21:19) and mother of king Amon.

hasadiah_1426.name: Hasadiah
hasadiah_1426.about: Favoured by Jehovah, one of the sons of Pedaiah (1 Chr. 3:20), of the royal line of David.

hasenuah_1427.name: Hasenuah
hasenuah_1427.about: Bristling or hated, a Benjamite (1 Chr. 9:7).

hashabiah_1433.name: Hashabiah
hashabiah_1433.about: One of the chief Levites (2 Chr. 35:9).

hashabiah_1434.name: Hashabiah
hashabiah_1434.about: One of the chief priests in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:24).

hashabniah_1440.name: Hashabniah
hashabniah_1440.about: One of the Levites whom Ezra appointed to interpret the law to the people (Neh. 9:5).

hashbadana_1441.name: Hashbadana
hashbadana_1441.about: Consideration in judging, stood at Ezra’s left hand when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

hashubah_1445.name: Hashubah
hashubah_1445.about: Ibid., a descendant of David (1 Chr. 3:20).

hashum_1447.name: Hashum
hashum_1447.about: Stood on Ezra’s left hand while he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

hasrah_1414.name: Hasrah
hasrah_1414.about: Poverty, “keeper of the wardrobe,” i.e., of the sacerdotal vestments (2 Chr. 34:22); called Harhas 2 Kings 22:14. He was husband of the prophetess Huldah.

hasshub_1450.name: Hasshub
hasshub_1450.about: A Levite of the family of Merari (Neh. 11:15; 1 Chr. 9:14).

hasupha_1451.name: Hasupha
hasupha_1451.about: Uncovered, one of the Nethinim (Ezra 2:43; Neh. 7:46).

hatach_1452.name: Hatach
hatach_1452.about: Verity, one of the eunuchs or chamberlains in the palace of Ahasuerus (Esther 4:5, 6, 9, 10).

hatita_1455.name: Hatita
hatita_1455.about: Exploration, one of the temple porters or janitors (Ezra 2:42). He returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel.

hattush_1460.name: Hattush
hattush_1460.about: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:2).

havilah_1461.name: Havilah (son of Cush)
havilah_1461.about: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

hazael_1463.name: Hazael
hazael_1463.about: Whom God beholds, an officer of Ben-hadad II., king of Syria, who ultimately came to the throne, according to the word of the Lord to Elijah (1 Kings 19:15), after he had put the king to death (2 Kings 8:15). His interview with Elisha is mentioned in 2 Kings 8.

hazarmaveth_1465.name: Hazarmaveth
hazarmaveth_1465.about: Court of death, the third son of Joktan, and a region in Arabia-Felix settled by him (Gen. 10:26; 1 Chr. 1:20). It is probably the modern province of Hadramaut, situated on the Indian Ocean east of the modern Yemen.

hazo_1468.name: Hazo
hazo_1468.about: Vision, one of the sons of Nahor (Gen. 22:22).

heber_1469.name: Heber
heber_1469.about: Son of Beriah and grandson of Asher (Gen. 46:17; 1 Chr. 7:31, 32).

heber_1470.name: Heber
heber_1470.about: The Kenite (Judg. 4:11, 17; 5:24), a descendant of Hobab. His wife Jael received Sisera (q.v.) into her tent and then killed him.

heber_1472.name: Heber
heber_1472.about: One of the seven heads of the families of the Gadites (1 Chr. 5:13).

hebron_1475.name: Hebron
hebron_1475.about: The third son of Kohath the Levite (Ex. 6:18; 1 Chr. 6:2, 18).

hegai_1477.name: Hegai
hegai_1477.about: Eunuch, had charge of the harem of Ahasuerus (Esther 2:8).

helah_1478.name: Helah
helah_1478.about: Rust, (1 Chr. 4:5, 7), one of the wives of Ashur.

heleb_1480.name: Heleb
heleb_1480.about: Fatness, one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:29).

helem_1479.name: Helem
helem_1479.about: Zech. 6:10, one who returned from Babylon.

heli_1484.name: Heli
heli_1484.about: Elevation, father of Joseph in the line of our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:23).

helkai_1485.name: Helkai
helkai_1485.about: Smooth-tongued, one of the chief priests in the time of Joiakim (Neh. 12:15).

helon_1486.name: Helon
helon_1486.about: Strong, father of Eliab, who was “captain of the children of Zebulun” (Num. 1:9; 2:7).

heman_1488.name: Heman
heman_1488.about: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

heman_1489.name: Heman
heman_1489.about: 1 Kings 4:31; 1 Chr. 2:6, a son of Zerah, noted for his wisdom.

heman_1490.name: Heman
heman_1490.about: Grandson of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:33; 15:17), to whom the 88th Psalm probably was inscribed. He was one of the “seers” named in 2 Chr. 29:14, 30, and took a leading part in the administration of the sacred services.

henadad_1493.name: Henadad
henadad_1493.about: Favour of Hadad, the name of a Levite after the Captivity (Ezra 3:9).

hepher_1497.name: Hepher
hepher_1497.about: The second son of Asher (1 Chr. 4:6).

hermogenes_1503.name: Hermogenes
hermogenes_1503.about: Mercury-born, at one time Paul’s fellow-labourer in Asia Minor, who, however, afterwards abandoned him, along with one Phygellus, probably on account of the perils by which they were beset (2 Tim. 1:15).

herod_1505.name: Herod Antipas
herod_1505.about: Herod’s son by Malthace (Matt. 14:1; Luke 3:1, 19; 9:7; Acts 13:1).

herod_1506.name: Herod Agrippa I
herod_1506.about: Son of Aristobulus and Bernice, and grandson of Herod the Great. He was made tetrarch of the provinces formerly held by Lysanias II., and ultimately possessed the entire kingdom of his grandfather, Herod the Great, with the title of king. He put the apostle James the elder to death, and cast Peter into prison (Luke 3:1; Acts 12:1-19).

herodias_1507.name: Herodias
herodias_1507.about: (Matt. 14:3-11; Mark 6:17-28; Luke 3:19), the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice. While residing at Rome with her husband Herod Philip I. and her daughter, Herod Antipas fell in with her during one of his journeys to that city. She consented to leave her husband and become his wife. Some time after, Herod met John the Baptist, who boldly declared the marriage to be unlawful.

herodion_1508.name: Herodion
herodion_1508.about: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes and calls his “kinsman” (Rom. 16:11).

heth_1510.name: Heth
heth_1510.about: Dread, a descendant of Canaan, and the ancestor of the Hittites (Gen. 10:18; Deut. 7:1), who dwelt in the vicinity of Hebron (Gen. 23:3, 7). The Hittites were a Hamitic race. They are called “the sons of Heth” (Gen. 23:3, 5, 7, 10, 16, 18, 20).

hezekiah_1512.name: Hezekiah
hezekiah_1512.about: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697). The history of this king is contained in 2 Kings 18:20, Isa. 36-39, and 2 Chr. 29-32. He is spoken of as a great and good king. In public life he followed the example of his great-granfather Uzziah.

hezion_1515.name: Hezion
hezion_1515.about: Vision, the father of Tabrimon, and grandfather of Ben-hadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

hezir_1516.name: Hezir
hezir_1516.about: The head of the seventeenth course of the priests (1 Chr. 24:15).

hezir_1517.name: Hezir
hezir_1517.about: Neh. 10:20, one who sealed Nehemiah’s covenant.

hezrai_1518.name: Hezrai
hezrai_1518.about: A Carmelite, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:37).

hezron_1519.name: Hezron
hezron_1519.about: One of the sons of Reuben (Gen. 46:9; Ex. 6:14).

hezron_1520.name: Hezron
hezron_1520.about: The older of the two sons of Pharez (Gen. 46:12).

hiel_1522.name: Hiel
hiel_1522.about: Life of (i.e., from) God, a native of Bethel, who built (i.e., fortified) Jericho some seven hundred years after its destruction by the Israelites. There fell on him for such an act the imprecation of Joshua (6:26). He laid the foundation in his first-born, and set up the gates in his youngest son (1 Kings 16:34), i.e., during the progress of the work all his children died.

hilkiah_1524.name: Hilkiah
hilkiah_1524.about: The high priest in the reign of Josiah (1 Chr. 6:13; Ezra 7:1). To him and his deputy (2 Kings 23:5), along with the ordinary priests and the Levites who had charge of the gates, was entrusted the purification of the temple in Jerusalem. While this was in progress, he discovered in some hidden corner of the building a book called the “book of the law” (2 Kings 22:8) and the “book of the covenant” (23:2).

hillel_1530.name: Hillel
hillel_1530.about: Praising, a Pirathonite, father of the judge Abdon (Judg. 12:13, 15).

hiram_1532.name: Hiram
hiram_1532.about: Also “Huram” and “Horam,” king of Tyre. He entered into an alliance with David, and assisted him in building his palace by sending him able workmen, and also cedar-trees and fir-trees from Lebanon (2 Sam. 5:11; 1 Chr. 14:1). After the death of David he entered into a similar alliance with Solomon, and assisted him greatly in building the temple (1 Kings 5:1; 9:11; 2 Chr. 2:3).

hiram_1533.name: Hiram
hiram_1533.about: The “master workman” whom Hiram sent to Solomon. He was the son of a widow of Dan, and of a Tyrian father.

hivite_1534.name: Hivite
hivite_1534.about: One of the original tribes scattered over Palestine, from Hermon to Gibeon in the south. The name is interpreted as “midlanders” or “villagers” (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15). They were probably a branch of the Hittites. At the time of Jacob’s return to Canaan, Hamor the Hivite was the “prince of the land” (Gen. 24:2-28). They are next mentioned during the Conquest (Josh. 9:7; 11:19).

hobab_1537.name: Hobab
hobab_1537.about: Beloved, the Kenite, has been usually identified with Jethro (q.v.), Ex. 18:5, 27; comp. Num. 10:29, 30. In Judg. 4:11, the word rendered “father-in-law” means properly any male relative by marriage (comp. Gen. 19:14, “son-in-law,” A.V.), and should be rendered “brother-in-law,” as in the R.V.

hodijah_1545.name: Hodijah
hodijah_1545.about: One of the Levites who assisted Ezra in expounding the law (Neh. 8:7; 9:5).

hodijah_1547.name: Hodijah
hodijah_1547.about: Neh. 10:18, a Levite who sealed the covenant.

hoglah_1548.name: Hoglah
hoglah_1548.about: Partridge, one of the daughters of Zelophehad the Gileadite, to whom portions were assigned by Moses (Num. 26:33; 27:1; 36:11).

hoham_1549.name: Hoham
hoham_1549.about: Jehovah impels, the king of Hebron who joined the league against Gibeon. He and his allies were defeated (Josh. 10:3, 5, 16-27).

holy_spirit_7400.name: Holy Spirit
holy_spirit_7400.about: The third Person of the adorable Trinity. His personality is proved (1) from the fact that the attributes of personality, as intelligence and volition, are ascribed to him (John 14:17, 26; 15:26; 1 Cor. 2:10, 11; 12:11). He reproves, helps, glorifies, intercedes (John 16:7-13; Rom. 8:26). (2) He executes the offices peculiar only to a person.

hophni_1550.name: Hophni
hophni_1550.about: Pugilist or client, one of the two sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:34), who, because he was “very old,” resigned to them the active duties of his office. By their scandalous conduct they brought down a curse on their father’s house (2:22, 12-27, 27-36; 3:11-14). For their wickedness they were called “sons of Belial,” i.e., worthless men (2:12). They both perished in the disastrous battle with the Philistines at Aphek (4:11).

hosah_1554.name: Hosah
hosah_1554.about: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 16:38).

hosea_1555.name: Hosea
hosea_1555.about: Salvation, the son of Beeri, and author of the book of prophecies bearing his name. He belonged to the kingdom of Israel.

hoshea_1559.name: Hoshea
hoshea_1559.about: The last king of Israel. He conspired against and slew his predecessor, Pekah (Isa. 7:16), but did not ascend the throne till after an interregnum of warfare of eight years (2 Kings 17:1, 2). Soon after this he submitted to Shalmaneser, the Assyrian king, who a second time invaded the land to punish Hoshea, because of his withholding tribute which he had promised to pay.

hoshea_1560.name: Hoshea
hoshea_1560.about: 1 Chr. 27:20. The ruler of Ephraim in David’s time.

hotham_1562.name: Hotham
hotham_1562.about: A stroke, great-grandson of Asher (1 Chr. 7:35).

hul_1566.name: Hul
hul_1566.about: Circle, the second son of Aram (Gen. 10:23), and grandson of Shem.

huldah_1567.name: Huldah
huldah_1567.about: Weasel, a prophetess; the wife of Shallum. She was consulted regarding the “book of the law” discovered by the high priest Hilkiah (2 Kings 22:14-20; 2 Chr. 34:22-28). She resided in that part of Jerusalem called the Mishneh (A.V., “the college;” R.V., “the second quarter”), supposed by some to be the suburb between the inner and the outer wall, the second or lower city, Akra.

hur_1571.name: Hur
hur_1571.about: The husband of Miriam, Moses’ sister (Ex. 17:10-12). He was associated with Aaron in charge of the people when Moses was absent on Sinai (Ex. 24:14). He was probably of the tribe of Judah, and grandfather of Bezaleel (Ex. 31:2; 35:30; 1 Chr. 2:19).

hur_1572.name: Hur
hur_1572.about: One of the five princes of Midian who were defeated and slain by the Israelites under the command of Phinehas (Num. 31:8).

hurai_1521.name: Hurai
hurai_1521.about: Linen-worker, one of David’s heroes, a native of the valley of Mount Gaash (1 Chr. 11:32).

huram_1569.name: Huram
huram_1569.about: Generally “Huram,” one of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 8:5).

hushai_1577.name: Hushai
hushai_1577.about: Quick, “the Archite,” “the king’s friend” (1 Chr. 27:33). When David fled from Jerusalem, on account of the rebellion of Absalom, and had reached the summit of Olivet, he there met Hushai, whom he sent back to Jerusalem for the purpose of counteracting the influence of Ahithophel, who had joined the ranks of Absalom (2 Sam. 15:32, 37; 16:16-18). It was by his advice that Absalom refrained from immediately pursuing after David.

ibhar_1584.name: Ibhar
ibhar_1584.about: Chosen, one of David’s sons (1 Chr. 3:6; 2 Sam. 5:15).

ibzan_1588.name: Ibzan
ibzan_1588.about: Illustrious, the tenth judge of Israel (Judg. 12:8-10). He ruled seven years.

iddo_1591.name: Iddo
iddo_1591.about: Timely. The father of Ahinadab, who was one of Solomon’s purveyors (1 Kings 4:14).

iddo_1593.name: Iddo
iddo_1593.about: Lovely. The son of Zechariah (1 Chr. 27:21), the ruler of Manasseh in David’s time.

iddo_1594.name: Iddo
iddo_1594.about: Lovely. A prophet of Judah who wrote the history of Rehoboam and Abijah (2 Chr. 12:15). He has been identified with Oded (2 Chr. 15:1).

igal_1598.name: Igal
igal_1598.about: Num. 13:7, one of the spies of the tribe of Issachar.

igal_1599.name: Igal
igal_1599.about: Son of Nathan of Zobah, and one of David’s warriors (2 Sam. 23:36).

ilai_2982.name: Ilai
ilai_2982.about: An Ahohite, one of David’s chief warriors (1 Chr. 11:29); called also Zalmon (2 Sam. 23:28).

imla_597.name: Imla
imla_597.about: Replenisher, the father of Micaiah the prophet (2 Chr. 18:7, 8).

immer_599.name: Immer
immer_599.about: The head of the sixteenth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:14).

iphedeiah_606.name: Iphedeiah
iphedeiah_606.about: Set free by Jehovah, a chief of the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:25).

ira_608.name: Ira
ira_608.about: A Jairite and priest, a royal chaplain (2 Sam. 20:26) or confidential adviser (comp. 2 Sam. 8:18; 1 Chr. 18:17).

ira_609.name: Ira
ira_609.about: A Tekoite, one of David’s thirty warriors (2 Sam. 23:26).

ira_610.name: Ira
ira_610.about: An Ithrite, also one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:38).

irad_611.name: Irad
irad_611.about: Runner; wild ass, one of the antediluvian patriarchs, the father of Mehujael (Gen. 4:18), and grandson of Cain.

iram_612.name: Iram
iram_612.about: Citizen, chief of an Edomite tribe in Mount Seir (Gen. 36:43).

isaac_616.name: Isaac
isaac_616.about: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3). He was circumcised when eight days old (4-7); and when he was probably two years old a great feast was held in connection with his being weaned. The next memorable event in his life is that connected with the command of God given to Abraham to offer him up as a sacrifice on a mountain in the land of Moriah (Gen. 22).

isaiah_617.name: Isaiah
isaiah_617.about: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1). He had two sons, who bore symbolical names.

iscah_618.name: Iscah
iscah_618.about: Spy, the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot (Gen. 11:29, 31).

ish-bosheth_622.name: Ish-bosheth
ish-bosheth_622.about: Man of shame or humiliation, the youngest of Saul’s four sons, and the only one who survived him (2 Sam. 2-4). His name was originally Eshbaal (1 Chr. 8:33; 9:39). He was about forty years of age when his father and three brothers fell at the battle of Gilboa.

ishbak_620.name: Ishbak
ishbak_620.about: Leaving, one of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2).

ishbi-benob_621.name: Ishbi-benob
ishbi-benob_621.about: My seat at Nob, one of the Rephaim, whose spear was three hundred shekels in weight. He was slain by Abishai (2 Sam. 21:16, 17).

ishmael_630.name: Ishmael (Son of Hagar)
ishmael_630.about: Abraham’s eldest son, by Hagar the concubine (Gen. 16:15; 17:23). He was born at Mamre, when Abraham was eighty-six years of age, eleven years after his arrival in Canaan (16:3; 21:5). At the age of thirteen he was circumcised (17:25). He grew up a true child of the desert, wild and wayward.

ishmael_631.name: Ishmael
ishmael_631.about: The son of Nethaniah, “of the seed royal” (Jer. 40:8, 15). He plotted against Gedaliah, and treacherously put him and others to death. He carried off many captives, “and departed to go over to the Ammonites.”

ishmaiah_636.name: Ishmaiah
ishmaiah_636.about: Son of Obadiah, and viceroy of Zebulun under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:19).

ismaiah_643.name: Ismaiah
ismaiah_643.about: A Gibeonite who joined David at Ziklag, “a hero among the thirty and over the thirty” (1 Chr. 12:4).

israel_682.name: Jacob (Israel)
israel_682.about: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old. Like his father, he was of a quiet and gentle disposition, and when he grew up followed the life of a shepherd, while his brother Esau became an enterprising hunter.

issachar_645.name: Issachar
issachar_645.about: Hired (Gen. 30:18). “God hath given me,” said Leah, “my hire (Heb. sekhari)...and she called his name Issachar.” He was Jacob’s ninth son, and was born in Padan-aram (comp. 28:2). He had four sons at the going down into Egypt (46:13; Num. 26:23, 25). Issachar, Tribe of, during the journey through the wilderness, along with Judah and Zebulun (Num. 2:5), marched on the east of the tabernacle.

ithamar_649.name: Ithamar
ithamar_649.about: Palm isle, the fourth and youngest son of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:3). He was consecrated to the priesthood along with his brothers (Ex. 6:23); and after the death of Nadab and Abihu, he and Eleazar alone discharged the functions of that office (Lev. 10:6, 12; Num. 3:4). He and his family occupied the position of common priest till the high priesthood passed into his family in the person of Eli (1 Kings 2:27), the reasons for which are not recorded.

ittai_656.name: Ittai
ittai_656.about: A native of Gath, a Philistine, who had apparently the command of the six hundred heroes who formed David’s band during his wanderings (2 Sam. 15:19-22; comp. 1 Sam. 23:13; 27:2; 30:9, 10). He is afterwards with David at Mahanaim, holding in the army equal rank with Joab and Abishai (2 Sam. 18:2, 5, 12). He then passes from view.

ittai_657.name: Ittai
ittai_657.about: A Benjamite, one of David’s thirty heroes (2 Sam. 23:29).

izhar_658.name: Izhar
izhar_658.about: Oil, one of the sons of Kohath, and grandson of Levi (Ex. 6:18, 21; Num. 16:1).

jaakobah_660.name: Jaakobah
jaakobah_660.about: Heel-catcher, a form of the name Jacob, one of the descendants of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:36).

jaala_661.name: Jaala
jaala_661.about: A wild she-goat, one of the Nethinim, whose descendants returned from the Captivity (Neh. 7:58).

jaalam_662.name: Jaalam
jaalam_662.about: Concealer, the second of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14).

jaanai_663.name: Jaanai
jaanai_663.about: Mourner, one of the chief Gadites (1 Chr. 5:12).

jaasiel_666.name: Jaasiel
jaasiel_666.about: Made by God, one of David’s body-guard, the son of Abner (1 Chr. 27:21), called Jasiel in 1 Chr. 11:47.

jaazaniah_668.name: Jaazaniah
jaazaniah_668.about: The son of Jeremiah, and one of the chief Rechabites (Jer. 35:3).

jaaziah_671.name: Jaaziah
jaaziah_671.about: Comforted by Jehovah, a descendant of Merari the Levite (1 Chr. 24:26, 27).

jaaziel_672.name: Jaaziel
jaaziel_672.about: Comforted by God, a Levitical musician (1 Chr. 15:18).

jabal_673.name: Jabal
jabal_673.about: A stream, a descendant of Cain, and brother of Jubal; “the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle” (Gen. 4:20). This description indicates that he led a wandering life.

jabesh_674.name: Jabesh
jabesh_674.about: The father of Shallum (2 Kings 15:10, 13, 14), who usurped the throne of Israel on the death of Zachariah.

jabez_675.name: Jabez
jabez_675.about: A descendant of Judah, of whom it is recorded that “God granted him that which he requested” (1 Chr. 4:9, 10).

jabin_676.name: Jabin
jabin_676.about: A king of Hazor, at the time of the entrance of Israel into Canaan (Josh. 11:1-14), whose overthrow and that of the northern chief with whom he had entered into a confederacy against Joshua was the crowning act in the conquest of the land (11:21-23; comp. 14:6-15). This great battle, fought at Lake Merom, was the last of Joshua’s battles of which we have any record.

jabin_677.name: Jabin (king of Hazor)
jabin_677.about: Another king of Hazor, called “the king of Canaan,” who overpowered the Israelites of the north one hundred and sixty years after Joshua’s death, and for twenty years held them in painful subjection.

jachan_678.name: Jachan
jachan_678.about: Mourner, one of the chief Gadite “brothers” in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

jachin_679.name: Jachin
jachin_679.about: The fourth son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10), called also Jarib (1 Chr. 4:24).

jachin_680.name: Jachin
jachin_680.about: One of the priests who returned from the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

jachin_681.name: Jachin
jachin_681.about: The head of one of the courses (the twenty-first) of priests (1 Chr. 24:17).

jaddua_686.name: Jaddua
jaddua_686.about: One of the chiefs who subscribed the covenant (Neh. 10:21).

jaddua_687.name: Jaddua
jaddua_687.about: The last high priest mentioned in the Old Testament (Neh. 12:11, 22), sons of Jonathan.

jadon_688.name: Jadon
jadon_688.about: Judge, a Meronothite who assisted in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:7).

jael_689.name: Jael
jael_689.about: Mountain-goat, the wife of Heber the Kenite (Judg. 4:17-22). When the Canaanites were defeated by Barak, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, fled and sought refuge with the friendly tribe of Heber, beneath the oaks of Zaanaim. As he drew near, Jael invited him to enter her tent. He did so, and as he lay wearied on the floor he fell into a deep sleep.

jahath_692.name: Jahath
jahath_692.about: A son of Shimei, and grandson of Gershom (1 Chr. 23:10).

jahath_693.name: Jahath
jahath_693.about: One of the sons of Shelomoth, of the family of Kohath (1 Chr. 24:22).

jahath_694.name: Jahath
jahath_694.about: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the overseers of the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

jahaziel_697.name: Jahaziel
jahaziel_697.about: A priest who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:6).

jahaziel_698.name: Jahaziel
jahaziel_698.about: The third son of Hebron (1 Chr. 23:19).

jahaziel_699.name: Jahaziel
jahaziel_699.about: The son of Zechariah, a Levite of the family of Asaph (2 Chr. 20:14-17). He encouraged Jehoshaphat against the Moabites and Ammonites.

jahdai_701.name: Jahdai
jahdai_701.about: Grasper, a descendant of Caleb, of the family of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:47).

jahzeel_706.name: Jahzeel
jahzeel_706.about: Allotted by God, the first of the sons of Naphtali (Gen. 46:24).

jahzerah_707.name: Jahzerah
jahzerah_707.about: Returner, the son of Meshullam, and father of Adiel (1 Chr. 9:12).

jair_664.name: Jair
jair_664.about: The father of Elhanan, who slew Lahmi, the brother of Goliath (1 Chr. 20:5).

jair_710.name: Jair
jair_710.about: A Benjamite, the father of Mordecai, Esther’s uncle (Esther 2:5).

jairus_711.name: Jairus
jairus_711.about: A ruler of the synagogue at Capernaum, whose only daughter Jesus restored to life (Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41).

jakeh_712.name: Jakeh
jakeh_712.about: Pious, the father of Agur (Prov. 30:1). Nothing is known of him.

jakim_714.name: Jakim
jakim_714.about: Chief of the twelfth priestly order (1 Chr. 24:12).

jalon_715.name: Jalon
jalon_715.about: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

jambres_716.name: Jambres
jambres_716.about: One of those who opposed Moses in Egypt (2 Tim. 3:8).

james_717.name: James (Son of Zebedee)
james_717.about: The son of Zebedee and Salome; an elder brother of John the apostle. He was one of the twelve. He was by trade a fisherman, in partnership with Peter (Matt. 20:20; 27:56). With John and Peter he was present at the transfiguration (Matt. 17:1; Mark 9:2), at the raising of Jairus’s daughter (Mark 5:37-43), and in the garden with our Lord (14:33).

james_718.name: James (Son of Alphaeus)
james_718.about: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature. He is mentioned along with the other apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15). He had a separate interview with our Lord after his resurrection (1 Cor. 15:7), and is mentioned as one of the apostles of the circumcision (Acts 1:13).

james_719.name: James (Brother of Jesus)
james_719.about: The son of Alphaeus, or Cleopas, “the brother” or near kinsman or cousin of our Lord (Gal. 1:18, 19), called James “the Less,” or “the Little,” probably because he was of low stature. He is mentioned along with the other apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15). He had a separate interview with our Lord after his resurrection (1 Cor. 15:7), and is mentioned as one of the apostles of the circumcision (Acts 1:13).

jannes_725.name: Jannes
jannes_725.about: One of the Egyptians who “withstood Moses” (2 Tim. 3:8).

japheth_726.name: Japheth
japheth_726.about: Wide spreading: “God shall enlarge Japheth” (Heb. Yaphat Elohim le-Yephet, Gen. 9:27. Some, however, derive the name from yaphah, “to be beautiful;” hence white), one of the sons of Noah, mentioned last in order (Gen. 5:32; 6:10; 7:13), perhaps first by birth (10:21; comp. 9:24). He and his wife were two of the eight saved in the ark (1 Pet. 3:20).

japhia_727.name: Japhia
japhia_727.about: The king of Lachish, who joined in the confederacy against Joshua (Josh. 10:3), and was defeated and slain. In one of the Amarna tablets he speaks of himself as king of Gezer. Called also Horam (Josh. 10:33).

japhia_728.name: Japhia
japhia_728.about: One of the sons of David (2 Sam. 5:15), born in Jerusalem.

jared_730.name: Jared
jared_730.about: The fourth antediluvian patriarch in descent from Seth (Gen. 5:15-20; Luke 3:37), the father of Enoch; called Jered in 1 Chr. 1:2.

jarib_733.name: Jarib
jarib_733.about: One of the chiefs sent by Ezra to bring up the priests to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:16).

jashen_736.name: Jashen
jashen_736.about: Sleeping, called also Hashem (1 Chr. 11:34); a person, several of whose sons were in David’s body-guard (2 Sam. 23:32).

jasher_737.name: Jasher
jasher_737.about: Upright. “The Book of Jasher,” rendered in the LXX. “the Book of the Upright One,” by the Vulgate “the Book of Just Ones,” was probably a kind of national sacred song-book, a collection of songs in praise of the heroes of Israel, a “book of golden deeds,” a national anthology.

jashobeam_738.name: Jashobeam
jashobeam_738.about: Dweller among the people; or to whom the people turn, the Hachmonite (1 Chr. 11:11), one of David’s chief heroes who joined him at Ziklag (12:6). He was the first of the three who broke through the host of the Philistines to fetch water to David from the well of Bethlehem (2 Sam. 23:13-17). He is also called Adino the Eznite (8).

jashub_1638.name: Jashub
jashub_1638.about: The third of Issachar’s four sons (1 Chr. 7:1); called also Job (Gen. 46:13).

jason_742.name: Jason
jason_742.about: He that will cure, the host of Paul and Silas in Thessalonica. The Jews assaulted his house in order to seize Paul, but failing to find him, they dragged Jason before the ruler of the city (Acts 17:5-9). He was apparently one of the kinsmen of Paul (Rom. 16:21), and accompanied him from Thessalonica to Corinth.

javan_744.name: Javan
javan_744.about: The fourth “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), whose descendants settled in Greece, i.e., Ionia, which bears the name of Javan in Hebrew. Alexander the Great is called the “king of Javan” (rendered “Grecia,” Dan. 8:21; 10:20; comp. 11:2; Zech. 9:13). This word was universally used by the nations of the East as the generic name of the Greek race.

jebusite_748.name: Jebusite
jebusite_748.about: The name of the original inhabitants of Jebus, mentioned frequently among the seven nations doomed to destruction (Gen. 10:16; 15:21; Ex. 3:8, 17; 13:5, etc.). At the time of the arrival of the Israelites in Palestine they were ruled by Adonizedek (Josh. 10:1, 23). They were defeated by Joshua, and their king was slain; but they were not entirely driven out of Jebus till the time of David, who made it the capital of his kingdom instead of Hebron.

jecoliah_750.name: Jecoliah
jecoliah_750.about: Able through Jehovah, the wife of King Amaziah, and mother of King Uzziah (2 Chr. 26:3).

jedaiah_751.name: Jedaiah
jedaiah_751.about: Invoker of Jehovah. The son of Shimri, a chief Simeonite (1 Chr. 4:37).
