jedaiah_752.name: Jedaiah
jedaiah_752.about: A priest in Jerusalem after the Exile (1 Chr. 9:10).

jedaiah_753.name: Jedaiah
jedaiah_753.about: Knowing Jehovah. The chief of one of the courses of the priests (1 Chr. 24:7).

jedaiah_754.name: Jedaiah
jedaiah_754.about: One of those who repaired the walls of Jerusalem after the return from Babylon (Neh. 3:10).

jediael_757.name: Jediael
jediael_757.about: One of the sons of Benjamin, whose descendants numbered 17,200 warriors (1 Chr. 7:6, 10, 11).

jediael_758.name: Jediael
jediael_758.about: A Shimrite, one of David’s bodyguard (1 Chr. 11:45). Probably same as in 12:20.

jediael_760.name: Jediael
jediael_760.about: A Korhite of the family of Ebiasaph, and one of the gate-keepers to the temple (1 Chr. 26:2).

jeduthun_1224.name: Jeduthun (Ethan)
jeduthun_1224.about: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the leaders of the temple music (1 Chr. 6:44; 15:17, 19). He was probably the same as Jeduthun. He is supposed by some to be the same also as (1).

jehalelel_765.name: Jehalelel
jehalelel_765.about: A Levite of the family of Merari (2 Chr. 29:12).

jehdeiah_766.name: Jehdeiah
jehdeiah_766.about: One of the Levitical attendants at the temple, a descendant of Shubael (1 Chr. 24:20).

jehdeiah_767.name: Jehdeiah
jehdeiah_767.about: A Meronothite, herdsman of the asses under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:30).

jehiel_770.name: Jehiel
jehiel_770.about: One of the Levites “of the second degree,” appointed to conduct the music on the occasion of the ark’s being removed to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

jehiel_772.name: Jehiel
jehiel_772.about: A Hachmonite, a tutor in the family of David toward the close of his reign (1 Chr. 27:32).

jehiel_773.name: Jehiel
jehiel_773.about: The second of Jehoshaphat’s six sons (2 Chr. 21:2).

jehiel_774.name: Jehiel
jehiel_774.about: One of the Levites of the family of Heman who assisted Hezekiah in his work of reformation (2 Chr. 29:14).

jehiel_776.name: Jehiel
jehiel_776.about: A “prince” and “ruler of the house of God” who contributed liberally to the renewal of the temple sacrifices under Josiah (2 Chr. 35:8).

jehizkiah_781.name: Jehizkiah
jehizkiah_781.about: Jehovah strengthens, one of the chiefs of Ephraim (2 Chr. 28:12).

jehoaddan_783.name: Jehoaddan
jehoaddan_783.about: Jehovah his ornament, the wife of King Jehoash, and mother of King Amaziah (2 Kings 14:2).

jehoahaz_784.name: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz_784.about: The son and successor of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 10:35). He reigned seventeen years, and followed the evil ways of the house of Jeroboam. The Syrians, under Hazael and Benhadad, prevailed over him, but were at length driven out of the land by his son Jehoash (13:1-9, 25).

jehoahaz_2516.name: Jehoahaz
jehoahaz_2516.about: A son of king Josiah (1 Chr. 3:15; Jer. 22:11), who was elected to succeed his father on the throne, although he was two years younger than his brother Eliakim. He assumed the crown under the name of Jehoahaz (q.v.). He did not imitate the example of his father (2 Kings 23:32), but was “a young lion, and it learned to catch the prey; it devoured men” (Ezek. 19:3). His policy was anti-Egyptian therefore.

jehohanan_785.name: Jehohanan
jehohanan_785.about: A Korhite, the head of one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:3).

jehoiachin_791.name: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin_791.about: Succeeded his father Jehoiakin (B.C. 599) when only eight years of age, and reigned for one hundred days (2 Chr. 36:9). He is also called Jeconiah (Jer. 24:1; 27:20, etc.), and Coniah (22:24; 37:1). He was succeeded by his uncle, Mattaniah = Zedekiah (q.v.). He was the last direct heir to the Jewish crown.

jehoiada_792.name: Jehoiada
jehoiada_792.about: The father of Benaiah, who was one of David’s chief warriors (2 Sam. 8:18; 20:23).

jehoiada_793.name: Jehoiada
jehoiada_793.about: The high priest at the time of Athaliah’s usurpation of the throne of Judah. He married Jehosheba, or Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram (2 Chr. 22:11), and took an active part along with his wife in the preservation and training of Jehoash when Athaliah slew all the royal family of Judah. The plans he adopted in replacing Jehoash on the throne of his ancestors are described in 2 Kings 11:2; 12:2; 2 Chr. 22:11; 23:24.

jehoiakim_1085.name: Jehoiakim
jehoiakim_1085.about: He whom Jehovah has set up, the second son of Josiah, and eighteenth king of Judah, which he ruled over for eleven years (B.C. 610-599). His original name was Eliakim (q.v.).

jehoiarib_798.name: Jehoiarib
jehoiarib_798.about: Jehovah defends, a priest at Jerusalem, head of one of the sacerdotal courses (1 Chr. 9:10; 24:7). His “course” went up from Babylon after the Exile (Ezra 2:36-39; Neh. 7:39-42).

jehonathan_800.name: Jehonathan
jehonathan_800.about: One of the stewards of David’s store-houses (1 Chr. 27:25).

jehonathan_801.name: Jehonathan
jehonathan_801.about: A Levite who taught the law to the people of Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

jehoram_803.name: Jehoram
jehoram_803.about: The eldest son and successor of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah. He reigned eight years (B.C. 892-885) alone as king of Judah, having been previously for some years associated with his father (2 Chr. 21:5, 20; 2 Kings 8:16). His wife was Athaliah, the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel. His daughter Jehosheba was married to the high priest Jehoiada. He sank into gross idolatry, and brought upon himself and his kingdom the anger of Jehovah.

jehoram_805.name: Jehoram
jehoram_805.about: A priest sent by Jehoshaphat to instructruct the people in Judah (2 Chr. 17:8).

jehoshabeath_811.name: Jehoshabeath
jehoshabeath_811.about: Jehovah-swearing, the daughter of Jehoram, the king of Israel. She is called Jehoshabeath in 2 Chr. 22:11. She was the only princess of the royal house who was married to a high priest, Jehoiada (2 Chr. 22:11).

jehoshaphat_806.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_806.about: Son of Ahilud, “recorder” or annalist under David and Solomon (2 Sam. 8:16), a state officer of high rank, chancellor or vizier of the kingdom.

jehoshaphat_808.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_808.about: The son and successor of Asa, king of Judah. After fortifying his kingdom against Israel (2 Chr. 17:1, 2), he set himself to cleanse the land of idolatry (1 Kings 22:43). In the third year of his reign he sent out priests and Levites over the land to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7-9).

jehoshaphat_809.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_809.about: The son of Nimshi, and father of Jehu, king of Israel (2 Kings 9:2, 14).

jehoshaphat_810.name: Jehoshaphat
jehoshaphat_810.about: One of the priests who accompanied the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

jehozabad_812.name: Jehozabad
jehozabad_812.about: The son of Shomer, one of the two conspirators who put king Jehoash to death in Millo in Jerusalem (2 Kings 12:21).

jehozabad_813.name: Jehozabad
jehozabad_813.about: The son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), one of the Levite porters.

jehu_816.name: Jehu
jehu_816.about: The son of Hanani, a prophet of Judah (1 Kings 16:1, 7; 2 Chr. 19:2; 20:34), who pronounced the sentence of God against Baasha, the king of Israel.

jehu_817.name: Jehu
jehu_817.about: King of Israel, the son of Jehoshaphat (2 Kings 9:2), and grandson of Nimshi. The story of his exaltation to the throne is deeply interesting.

jehu_818.name: Jehu
jehu_818.about: The son of Obed, and father of Azariah (1 Chr. 2:38).

jehu_820.name: Jehu
jehu_820.about: One of the Benjamite slingers that joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

jehudi_823.name: Jehudi
jehudi_823.about: A Jew, son of Nethaniah. He was sent by the princes to invite Baruch to read Jeremiah’s roll to them (Jer. 36:14, 21).

jeiel_827.name: Jeiel
jeiel_827.about: One of the Levites who took part in praising God on the removal of the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 16:5).

jeiel_830.name: Jeiel
jeiel_830.about: 2 Chr. 29:13. A Levite of the sons of Asaph.

jeiel_831.name: Jeiel
jeiel_831.about: One of the chief Levites, who made an offering for the restoration of the Passover by Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

jemima_837.name: Jemima
jemima_837.about: Dove, the eldest of Job’s three daughters born after his time of trial (Job 42:14).

jemuel_838.name: Jemuel
jemuel_838.about: One of Simeon’s five sons (1 Chr. 4:24), called also Jemuel (Gen. 46:10).

jephthah_839.name: Jephthah
jephthah_839.about: Whom God sets free, or the breaker through, a “mighty man of valour” who delivered Israel from the oppression of the Ammonites (Judg. 11:1-33), and judged Israel six years (12:7). He has been described as “a wild, daring, Gilead mountaineer, a sort of warrior Elijah.” After forty-five years of comparative quiet Israel again apostatized, and in “process of time the children of Ammon made war against Israel” (11:5).

jephunneh_840.name: Jephunneh
jephunneh_840.about: The father of Caleb, who was Joshua’s companion in exploring Canaan (Num. 13:6), a Kenezite (Josh. 14:14).

jephunneh_841.name: Jephunneh
jephunneh_841.about: One of the descendants of Asher (1 Chr. 7:38).

jerahmeel_843.name: Jerahmeel
jerahmeel_843.about: The son of Hezron, the brother of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:9, 25, 26, etc.).

jerahmeel_844.name: Jerahmeel
jerahmeel_844.about: The son of Kish, a Levite (1 Chr. 24:29).

jered_846.name: Jered
jered_846.about: A son of Ezra probably (1 Chr. 4:18).

jeremiah_848.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_848.about: The father of Hamutal (2 Kings 23:31), the wife of Josiah.

jeremiah_849.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_849.about: One of the chiefs of the tribe of Manasseh on the east of Jordan (1 Chr. 5:24).

jeremiah_850.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_850.about: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

jeremiah_851.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_851.about: A Gadite who joined David in the wilderness (1 Chr. 12:10).

jeremiah_853.name: Jeremiah
jeremiah_853.about: One of the “greater prophets” of the Old Testament, son of Hilkiah (q.v.), a priest of Anathoth (Jer. 1:1; 32:6). He was called to the prophetical office when still young (1:6), in the thirteenth year of Josiah (B.C. 628). He left his native place, and went to reside in Jerusalem, where he greatly assisted Josiah in his work of reformation (2 Kings 23:1-25).

jerimoth_864.name: Jerimoth
jerimoth_864.about: One of the sons of Bela (1 Chr. 7:7).

jerimoth_866.name: Jerimoth
jerimoth_866.about: A Benjamite slinger who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

jerimoth_867.name: Jerimoth
jerimoth_867.about: A Levitical musician under Heman his father (1 Chr. 25:4).

jerimoth_870.name: Jerimoth
jerimoth_870.about: A Levite, one of the overseers of the temple offerings (2 Chr. 31:13) in the reign of Hezekiah.

jeroboam_872.name: Jeroboam
jeroboam_872.about: The son of Nebat (1 Kings 11:26-39), “an Ephrathite,” the first king of the ten tribes, over whom he reigned twenty-two years (B.C. 976-945). He was the son of a widow of Zereda, and while still young was promoted by Solomon to be chief superintendent of the “burnden”, i.e., of the bands of forced labourers.

jeroboam_873.name: Jeroboam
jeroboam_873.about: Jeroboam II., the son and successor of Jehoash, and the fourteenth king of Israel, over which he ruled for forty-one years, B.C. 825-784 (2 Kings 14:23). He followed the example of the first Jeroboam in keeping up the worship of the golden calves (2 Kings 14:24). His reign was contemporary with those of Amaziah (2 Kings 14:23) and Uzziah (15:1), kings of Judah.

jeroham_874.name: Jeroham
jeroham_874.about: Father of Elkanah, and grandfather of the prophet Samuel (1 Sam. 1:1).

jeroham_877.name: Jeroham
jeroham_877.about: 1 Chr. 9:12; a priest, perhaps the same as in Neh. 11:12.

jeroham_879.name: Jeroham
jeroham_879.about: The father of Azareel, the “captain” of the tribe of Dan (1 Chr. 27:22).

jeroham_880.name: Jeroham
jeroham_880.about: 2 Chr. 23:1; one whose son assisted in placing Joash on the throne.

jerubbesheth_881.name: Jerubbesheth
jerubbesheth_881.about: Contender with the shame; i.e., idol, a surname also of Gideon (2 Sam. 11:21).

jerushah_882.name: Jerushah
jerushah_882.about: Possession, or possessed; i.e., “by a husband”, the wife of Uzziah, and mother of king Jotham (2 Kings 15:33).

jesaiah_883.name: Jesaiah
jesaiah_883.about: One of the three sons of Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:21).

jeshaiah_647.name: Jeshaiah
jeshaiah_647.about: A Kohathite Levite, the father of Joram, of the family of Eliezer (1 Chr. 26:25); called also Isshiah (24:21).

jeshaiah_885.name: Jeshaiah
jeshaiah_885.about: One of the sons of Jeduthum (1 Chr. 25:3, 15).

jesharelah_334.name: Jesharelah
jesharelah_334.about: Upright towards God, the head of the seventh division of Levitical musicians (1 Chr. 25:14).

jeshebeab_888.name: Jeshebeab
jeshebeab_888.about: Seat of his father, the head of the fourteenth division of priests (1 Chr. 24:13).

jesher_889.name: Jesher
jesher_889.about: Uprightness, the first of the three sons of Caleb by Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

jeshua_892.name: Jeshua
jeshua_892.about: A Levite appointed by Hezekiah to distribute offerings in the priestly cities (2 Chr. 31:15).

jeshua_899.name: Jeshua
jeshua_899.about: Head of the ninth priestly order (Ezra 2:36); called also Jeshuah (1 Chr. 24:11).

jesse_903.name: Jesse
jesse_903.about: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12). The phrase “stem of Jesse” is used for the family of David (Isa. 11:1), and “root of Jesse” for the Messiah (Isa. 11:10; Rev. 5:5). Jesse was a man apparently of wealth and position at Bethlehem (1 Sam. 17:17, 18, 20; Ps. 78:71).

jesus_904.name: Jesus
jesus_904.about: A Jewish Christian surnamed Justus (Col. 4:11). Je’sus, the proper, as Christ is the official, name of our Lord. To distinguish him from others so called, he is spoken of as “Jesus of Nazareth” (John 18:7), and “Jesus the son of Joseph” (John 6:42). This is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Joshua, which was originally Hoshea (Num. 13:8, 16), but changed by Moses into Jehoshua (Num. 13:16; 1 Chr. 7:27), or Joshua.

jesus_905.name: Jesus Christ
jesus_905.about: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah” (q.v.), the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament. It denotes that he was anointed or consecrated to his great redemptive work as Prophet, Priest, and King of his people. He is Jesus the Christ (Acts 17:3; 18:5; Matt. 22:42), the Anointed One.

jether_906.name: Jether
jether_906.about: The oldest of Gideon’s seventy sons (Judg. 8:20).

jether_907.name: Jether
jether_907.about: The father of Amasa, David’s general (1 Kings 2:5, 32); called Ithra (2 Sam. 17:25).

jetheth_910.name: Jetheth
jetheth_910.about: A peg, or a prince, one of the Edomitish kings of Mount Seir (Gen. 36:40).

jethro_2431.name: Jethro
jethro_2431.about: “The priest of Midian,” Moses’ father-in-law (Ex. 2:18)=Raguel (Num. 10:29). If he be identified with Jethro (q.v.), then this may be regarded as his proper name, and Jether or Jethro (i.e., “excellency”) as his official title.

jetur_911.name: Jetur
jetur_911.about: An enclosure, one of the twelve sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

jeuel_912.name: Jeuel
jeuel_912.about: Snatched away by God, a descendant of Zerah (1 Chr. 9:6).

jeush_913.name: Jeush
jeush_913.about: The oldest of Esau’s three sons by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:5, 14, 18).

jeush_1601.name: Jeush
jeush_1601.about: A son of Bilhan, grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:10).

jeush_1602.name: Jeush
jeush_1602.about: A Levite, one of the sons of Shimei (1 Chr. 23:10, 11).

jeush_1603.name: Jeush
jeush_1603.about: One of the three sons of Rehoboam (2 Chr. 11:19).

jezaniah_667.name: Jezaniah
jezaniah_667.about: A Maachathite (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8; 42:1). He is also called Azariah (Jer. 43:2).

jezebel_1605.name: Jezebel
jezebel_1605.about: Chaste, the daughter of Ethbaal, the king of the Zidonians, and the wife of Ahab, the king of Israel (1 Kings 16:31). This was the “first time that a king of Israel had allied himself by marriage with a heathen princess; and the alliance was in this case of a peculiarly disastrous kind. Jezebel has stamped her name on history as the representative of all that is designing, crafty, malicious, revengeful, and cruel.

jeziel_1608.name: Jeziel
jeziel_1608.about: Assembled by God, a son of Azmaveth. He was one of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

joab_1617.name: Joab
joab_1617.about: One of the three sons of Zeruiah, David’s sister, and “captain of the host” during the whole of David’s reign (2 Sam. 2:13; 10:7; 11:1; 1 Kings 11:15). His father’s name is nowhere mentioned, although his sepulchre at Bethlehem is mentioned (2 Sam. 2:32). His two brothers were Abishai and Asahel, the swift of foot, who was killed by Abner (2 Sam. 2:13-32), whom Joab afterwards treacherously murdered (3:22-27).

joah_1621.name: Joah
joah_1621.about: The son of Asaph, and “recorder” (q.v.) or chronicler to King Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:18, 26, 37).

joah_1623.name: Joah
joah_1623.about: One of the sons of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4), a Korhite porter.

joah_1626.name: Joah
joah_1626.about: Son of Joahaz, and “recorder” (q.v.) or keeper of the state archives under King Josiah (2 Chr. 34:8).

joahaz_1627.name: Joahaz
joahaz_1627.about: (2 Chr. 34:8), a contracted form of Jehoahaz (q.v.).

joanna_1628.name: Joanna
joanna_1628.about: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ (Luke 3:27); the same as Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:19).

joanna_1629.name: Joanna
joanna_1629.about: The wife of Chuza, the steward of Herod Antipas, tetrarch of Galilee (Luke 8:3). She was one of the women who ministered to our Lord, and to whom he appeared after his resurrection (Luke 8:3; 24:10).

joash_1630.name: Joash
joash_1630.about: A contracted form of Jehoash, the father of Gideon (Judg. 6:11, 29; 8:13, 29, 32).

joash_1631.name: Joash
joash_1631.about: One of King Ahab’s sons (1 Kings 22:26).

joash_1632.name: Joash
joash_1632.about: The son of King Ahaziah. While yet an infant, he was saved from the general massacre of the family by his aunt Jehosheba, and was apparently the only surviving descendant of Solomon (2 Chr. 21:4, 17). His uncle, the high priest Jehoiada, brought him forth to public notice when he was eight years of age, and crowned and anointed him king of Judah with the usual ceremonies.

joash_1633.name: Joash
joash_1633.about: The son and successor of Jehoahaz, king of Israel (2 Kings 14:1; comp. 12:1; 13:10). When he ascended the throne the kingdom was suffering from the invasion of the Syrians. Hazael “was cutting Israel short.” He tolerated the worship of the golden calves, yet seems to have manifested a character of sincere devotion to the God of his fathers.

joash_1636.name: Joash
joash_1636.about: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

joash_1637.name: Joash
joash_1637.about: One who had charge of the royal stores of oil under David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:28).

job_1639.name: Job
job_1639.about: Persecuted, an Arabian patriarch who resided in the land of Uz (q.v.). While living in the midst of great prosperity, he was suddenly overwhelmed by a series of sore trials that fell upon him. Amid all his sufferings he maintained his integrity. Once more God visited him with the rich tokens of his goodness and even greater prosperity than he had enjoyed before.

jobab_1640.name: Jobab (son of Joktan)
jobab_1640.about: One of the sons of Joktan, and founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 10:29).

jobab_1642.name: Jobab
jobab_1642.about: A Canaanitish king (Josh. 11:1) who joined the confederacy against Joshua.

jochebed_1645.name: Jochebed
jochebed_1645.about: Jehovah is her glory, the wife of Amram, and the mother of Miriam, Aaron, and Moses (Num. 26:59). She is spoken of as the sister of Kohath, Amram’s father (Ex. 6:20; comp. 16, 18; 2:1-10).

joel_1647.name: Joel
joel_1647.about: The oldest of Samuel’s two sons appointed by him as judges in Beersheba (1 Sam. 8:2).

joel_1653.name: Joel
joel_1653.about: One of David’s famous warriors (1 Chr. 11:38).

joel_1654.name: Joel
joel_1654.about: A Levite of the family of Gershom (1 Chr. 15:7, 11).

joel_1660.name: Joel
joel_1660.about: The second of the twelve minor prophets. He was the son of Pethuel. His personal history is only known from his book.

joelah_1661.name: Joelah
joelah_1661.about: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:7).

joezer_1662.name: Joezer
joezer_1662.about: Jehovah is his help, one of the Korhites who became part of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 12:6).

johanan_1666.name: Johanan
johanan_1666.about: Son of Careah, one of the Jewish chiefs who rallied round Gedaliah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had made governor in Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8). He warned Gedaliah of the plans of Ishmael against him, a warning which was unheeded (Jer. 40:13, 16). He afterwards pursued the murderer of the governor, and rescued the captives (41:8, 13, 15, 16). He and his associates subsequently fled to Tahpanhes in Egypt (43:2, 4, 5), taking Jeremiah with them.

johanan_1667.name: Johanan
johanan_1667.about: The oldest of King Josiah’s sons (1 Chr. 3:15).

johanan_1671.name: Johanan
johanan_1671.about: One of the Gadite heroes who joined David in the desert of Judah (1 Chr. 12:12).

john_1676.name: John the Baptist
john_1676.about: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent. His father, Zacharias, was a priest of the course of Abia (1 Chr. 24:10), and his mother, Elisabeth, was of the daughters of Aaron (Luke 1:5). The mission of John was the subject of prophecy (Matt. 3:3; Isa. 40:3; Mal. 3:1). His birth, which took place six months before that of Jesus, was foretold by an angel.

john_1677.name: John the Apostle
john_1677.about: THE APOSTLE, brother of James the “Greater” (Matt. 4:21; 10:2; Mark 1:19; 3:17; 10:35). He was one, probably the younger, of the sons of Zebedee (Matt. 4:21) and Salome (Matt. 27:56; comp. Mark 15:40), and was born at Bethsaida. His father was apparently a man of some wealth (comp. Mark 1:20; Luke 5:3; John 19:27). He was doubtless trained in all that constituted the ordinary education of Jewish youth.

john_1678.name: John (Relative of the High Priest)
john_1678.about: One who, with Annas and Caiaphas, sat in judgment on the apostles Peter and John (Acts 4:6). He was of the kindred of the high priest; otherwise unknown.

joiakim_1681.name: Joiakim
joiakim_1681.about: (whom Jehovah has set up) = Jehoiakim, a high priest, the son and successor of Jeshua (Neh. 12:10, 12, 26).

joiarib_797.name: Joiarib
joiarib_797.about: The founder of one of the courses of the priests (Neh. 11:10).

joiarib_1682.name: Joiarib
joiarib_1682.about: Ezra 8:16, a “man of understanding” whom Ezra sent to “bring ministers for the house of God.”

jokim_1684.name: Jokim
jokim_1684.about: Whom Jehovah has set up, one of the descendants of Shelah (1 Chr. 4:22).

jokshan_1685.name: Jokshan
jokshan_1685.about: Snarer, the second son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen. 25:2, 3; 1 Chr. 1:32).

joktan_1686.name: Joktan
joktan_1686.about: Little, the second of the two sons of Eber (Gen. 10:25; 1 Chr. 1:19). There is an Arab tradition that Joktan (Arab. Kahtan) was the progenitor of all the purest tribes of Central and Southern Arabia.

jonadab_799.name: Jonadab
jonadab_799.about: A son of Rechab, the founder of a tribe who bound themselves by a vow to abstain from wine (Jer. 35:6-19). There were different settlements of Rechabites (Judg. 1:16; 4:11; 1 Chr. 2:55). His interview and alliance with Jehu are mentioned in 2 Kings 10:15-23. He went with Jehu in his chariot to Samaria.

jonadab_1688.name: Jonadab
jonadab_1688.about: Son of Shammah, and David’s nephew, and also one of his chief warriors (2 Sam. 21:21). He slew a giant in Gath.

jonah_1689.name: Jonah
jonah_1689.about: A dove, the son of Amittai of Gath-hepher. He was a prophet of Israel, and predicted the restoration of the ancient boundaries (2 Kings 14:25-27) of the kingdom. He exercised his ministry very early in the reign of Jeroboam II., and thus was contemporary with Hosea and Amos; or possibly he preceded them, and consequently may have been the very oldest of all the prophets whose writings we possess.

jonas_1687.name: Jonas
jonas_1687.about: The father of the apostles Peter (John 21:15-17) and Andrew; but the reading should be (also in 1:42), as in the Revised Version, “John,” instead of Jonas.

jonathan_1691.name: Jonathan
jonathan_1691.about: A Levite descended from Gershom (Judg. 18:30). His history is recorded in 17:7-13 and 18:30. The Rabbins changed this name into Manasseh “to screen the memory of the great lawgiver from the stain of having so unworthy an apostate among his near descendants.” He became priest of the idol image at Dan, and this office continued in his family till the Captivity.

jonathan_1692.name: Jonathan
jonathan_1692.about: The eldest son of king Saul, and the bosom friend of David. He is first mentioned when he was about thirty years of age, some time after his father’s accession to the throne (1 Sam. 13:2). Like his father, he was a man of great strength and activity (2 Sam. 1:23), and excelled in archery and slinging (1 Chr. 12:2;2 Sam. 1:22). The affection that evidently subsisted between him and his father was interrupted by the growth of Saul’s insanity.

jonathan_1693.name: Jonathan
jonathan_1693.about: Son of the high priest Abiathar, and one who adhered to David at the time of Absalom’s rebellion (2 Sam. 15:27, 36). He is the last descendant of Eli of whom there is any record.

joram_804.name: Joram
joram_804.about: The son of Ahab and Jezebel, and successor to his brother Ahaziah on the throne of Israel. He reigned twelve years, B.C. 896-884 (2 Kings 1:17; 3:1). His first work was to reduce to subjection the Moabites, who had asserted their independence in the reign of his brother. Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, assisted Jehoram in this effort. He was further helped by his ally the king of Edom.

joram_1705.name: Joram
joram_1705.about: The son of Tou, king of Hamath, sent by his father to congratulate David on his victory over Hadarezer, king of Syria (1 Chr. 18:10; called Joram 2 Sam. 8:10).

josabad_1708.name: Josabad
josabad_1708.about: One of the Benjamite archers who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:4).

josedech_815.name: Josedech
josedech_815.about: Jehovah-justified, the son of the high priest Seraiah at the time of the Babylonian exile (1 Chr. 6:14, 15). He was carried into captivity by Nebuchadnezzar, and probably died in Babylon. He was the father of Jeshua, or Joshua, who returned with Zerubbabel.

joseph_1710.name: Joseph (son of Jacob)
joseph_1710.about: The elder of the two sons of Jacob by Rachel (Gen. 30:23, 24), who, on the occasion of his birth, said, “God hath taken away [Heb. ‘asaph] my reproach.” “The Lord shall add [Heb. yoseph] to me another son” (Gen. 30:24). He was a child of probably six years of age when his father returned from Haran to Canaan and took up his residence in the old patriarchal town of Hebron.

joseph_1712.name: Joseph (son of Asaph)
joseph_1712.about: One of the sons of Asaph, head of the first division of sacred musicians (1 Chr. 25:2, 9).

joseph_1715.name: Joseph (Mary's Husband)
joseph_1715.about: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.” He was by trade a carpenter (Matt. 13:55). He is last mentioned in connection with the journey to Jerusalem, when Jesus was twelve years old. It is probable that he died before Jesus entered on his public ministry. This is concluded from the fact that Mary only was present at the marriage feast in Cana of Galilee.

joseph_1716.name: Joseph (of Arimathea)
joseph_1716.about: A native of Arimathea, probably the Ramah of the Old Testament (1 Sam. 1:19), a man of wealth, and a member of the Sanhedrim (Matt. 27:57; Luke 23:50), an “honourable counsellor, who waited for the kingdom of God.” As soon as he heard the tidings of Christ’s death, he “went in boldly” (lit.

joseph_1718.name: Joseph (son of Judah)
joseph_1718.about: The son of Judah, and father of Semei (Luke 3:26). Other two of the same name in the ancestry of Christ are also mentioned (3:24, 30).

joshua_893.name: Joshua
joshua_893.about: The son of Jozadak, and high priest of the Jews under Zerubbabel (Neh. 7:7; 12:1, 7, 10, 26); called Joshua (Hag. 1:1, 12; 2:2, 4; Zech. 3:1, 3, 6, 8, 9).

joshua_1727.name: Joshua
joshua_1727.about: Jehovah is his help, or Jehovah the Saviour. The son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, the successor of Moses as the leader of Israel. He is called Jehoshua in Num. 13:16 (A.V.), and Jesus in Acts 7:45 and Heb. 4:8 (R.V., Joshua). He was born in Egypt, and was probably of the age of Caleb, with whom he is generally associated.

josiah_1730.name: Josiah
josiah_1730.about: Healed by Jehovah, or Jehovah will support. The son of Amon, and his successor on the throne of Judah (2 Kings 22:1; 2 Chr. 34:1). His history is contained in 2 Kings 22, 23. He stands foremost among all the kings of the line of David for unswerving loyalty to Jehovah (23:25).

josiah_1731.name: Josiah
josiah_1731.about: Common in later times among the Jews in Palestine (Matt. 23:37; Luke 13:34). It is noticeable that this familiar bird is only mentioned in these passages in connection with our Lord’s lamentation over the impenitence of Jerusalem.

jotham_1734.name: Jotham
jotham_1734.about: The youngest of Gideon’s seventy sons. He escaped when the rest were put to death by the order of Abimelech (Judg. 9:5). When “the citizens of Shechem and the whole house of Millo” were gathered together “by the plain of the pillar” (i.e., the stone set up by Joshua, 24:26; comp.

jotham_1735.name: Jotham
jotham_1735.about: The son and successor of Uzziah on the throne of Judah. As during his last years Uzziah was excluded from public life on account of his leprosy, his son, then twenty-five years of age, administered for seven years the affairs of the kingdom in his father’s stead (2 Chr. 26:21, 23; 27:1). After his father’s death he became sole monarch, and reigned for sixteen years (B.C. 759-743). He ruled in the fear of God, and his reign was prosperous.

jubal_1748.name: Jubal
jubal_1748.about: Jubilee, music, Lamech’s second son by Adah, of the line of Cain. He was the inventor of “the harp” (Heb. kinnor, properly “lyre”) and “the organ” (Heb. ‘ugab, properly “mouth-organ” or Pan’s pipe), Gen. 4:21.

jucal_822.name: Jucal
jucal_822.about: Able, the son of Shelemiah. He is also called Jucal (Jer. 38:1). He was one of the two persons whom Zedekiah sent to request the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the kingdom (Jer. 37:3) during the time of its final siege by Nebuchadnezzar. He was accompanied by Zephaniah (q.v.).

juda_1750.name: Juda
juda_1750.about: The father of Simeon in Christ’s maternal ancestry (Luke 3:30).

judah_1751.name: Judah (patriarch)
judah_1751.about: Praise, the fourth son of Jacob by Leah. The name originated in Leah’s words of praise to the Lord on account of his birth: “Now will I praise [Heb. odeh] Jehovah, and she called his name Yehudah” (Gen. 29:35). It was Judah that interposed in behalf of Joseph, so that his life was spared (Gen. 37:26, 27). He took a lead in the affairs of the family, and “prevailed above his brethren” (Gen. 43:3-10; 44:14, 16-34; 46:28; 1 Chr. 5:2).

judas_1758.name: Judas (Jew of Damascus)
judas_1758.about: A Jew of Damascus (Acts 9:11), to whose house Ananias was sent. The street called “Straight” in which it was situated is identified with the modern “street of bazaars,” where is still pointed out the so-called “house of Judas.”

judas_1759.name: Judas Barsabas
judas_1759.about: A Christian teacher, surnamed Barsabas. He was sent from Jerusalem to Antioch along with Paul and Barnabas with the decision of the council (Acts 15:22, 27, 32). He was a “prophet” and a “chief man among the brethren.”

judas_1760.name: Judas Iscariot
judas_1760.about: Son of Simon (John 6:71; 13:2, 26), surnamed Iscariot, i.e., a man of Kerioth (Josh. 15:25). His name is uniformly the last in the list of the apostles, as given in the synoptic (i.e., the first three) Gospels. The evil of his nature probably gradually unfolded itself till “Satan entered into him” (John 13:27), and he betrayed our Lord (18:3).

jude_1756.name: Jude
jude_1756.about: '= Judas. Among the apostles there were two who bore this name, (1) Judas (Jude 1:1; Matt. 13:55; John 14:22; Acts 1:13), called also Lebbaeus or Thaddaeus (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18); and (2) Judas Iscariot (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:19). He who is called “the brother of James” (Luke 6:16), may be the same with the Judas surnamed Lebbaeus. The only thing recorded regarding him is in John 14:22.

julia_1762.name: Julia
julia_1762.about: A Christian woman at Rome to whom Paul sent his salutations (Rom. 16:15), supposed to be the wife of Philologus.

julius_1763.name: Julius
julius_1763.about: The centurion of the Augustan cohort, or the emperor’s body-guard, in whose charge Paul was sent prisoner to Rome (Acts 27:1, 3, 43). He entreated Paul “courteously,” showing in many ways a friendly regard for him.

junia_1764.name: Junia
junia_1764.about: (Rom. 16:7), a Christian at Rome to whom Paul sends salutations along with Andronicus.

justus_1766.name: Justus
justus_1766.about: A Jewish proselyte at Corinth, in whose house, next door to the synagogue, Paul held meetings and preached after he left the synagogue (Acts 18:7).

kadmiel_1767.name: Kadmiel
kadmiel_1767.about: Before God; i.e., his servant, one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 9:4; 10:9; 12:8).

kareah_919.name: Kareah
kareah_919.about: Bald, the father of Johanan and Jonathan, who for a time were loyal to Gedaliah, the Babylonian governor of Jerusalem (Jer. 40:8, 13, 15, 16).

kedar_1769.name: Kedar
kedar_1769.about: Dark-skinned, the second son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:13). It is the name for the nomadic tribes of Arabs, the Bedouins generally (Isa. 21:16; 42:11; 60:7; Jer. 2:10; Ezek. 27:21), who dwelt in the north-west of Arabia. They lived in black hair-tents (Cant. 1:5). To “dwell in the tents of Kedar” was to be cut off from the worship of the true God (Ps. 120:5). The Kedarites suffered at the hands of Nebuchadnezzar (Jer. 49:28, 29).

kedemah_1770.name: Kedemah
kedemah_1770.about: Eastward, the last-named of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15).

kelita_1772.name: Kelita
kelita_1772.about: Dwarf, a Levite who assisted Ezra in expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:7; 10:10).

kemuel_1774.name: Kemuel
kemuel_1774.about: Son of Shiphtan, appointed on behalf of the tribe of Ephraim to partition the land of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

kenaz_1778.name: Kenaz
kenaz_1778.about: Caleb’s younger brother, and father of Othniel (Josh. 15:17), whose family was of importance in Israel down to the time of David (1 Chr. 27:15). Some think that Othniel (Judg. 1:13), and not Kenaz, was Caleb’s brother.

keren-happuch_1780.name: Keren-happuch
keren-happuch_1780.about: Horn of the face-paint = cosmetic-box, the name of Job’s third daughter (Job. 42:14), born after prosperity had returned to him.

keturah_1782.name: Keturah
keturah_1782.about: Incense, the wife of Abraham, whom he married probably after Sarah’s death (Gen. 25:1-6), by whom he had six sons, whom he sent away into the east country. Her nationality is unknown. She is styled “Abraham’s concubine” (1 Chr. 1:32). Through the offshoots of the Keturah line Abraham became the “father of many nations.”

kish_1784.name: Kish
kish_1784.about: A Benjamite, the son of Abiel, and father of king Saul (1 Sam. 9:1, 3; 10:11, 21; 14:51; 2 Sam. 21:14). All that is recorded of him is that he sent his son Saul in search of his asses that had strayed, and that he was buried in Zelah. Called Cis, Acts 13:21 (R.V., Kish).

kish_1785.name: Kish
kish_1785.about: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 23:21; 24:29).

kish_1786.name: Kish
kish_1786.about: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

kohath_1790.name: Kohath
kohath_1790.about: Assembly, the second son of Levi, and father of Amram (Gen. 46:11). He came down to Egypt with Jacob, and lived to the age of one hundred and thirty-three years (Ex. 6:18).

korah_1793.name: Korah
korah_1793.about: The third son of Esau, by Aholibamah (Gen. 36:14; 1 Chr. 1:35).

korah_1795.name: Korah (Levite)
korah_1795.about: A Levite, the son of Izhar, the brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 6:21). The institution of the Aaronic priesthood and the Levitical service at Sinai was a great religious revolution. The old priesthood of the heads of families passed away.

kore_1797.name: Kore
kore_1797.about: A Levite and temple-warder of the Korahites, the son of Asaph. He was father of Shallum and Meshelemiah, temple-porters (1 Chr. 9:19; 26:1).

kore_1798.name: Kore
kore_1798.about: A Levitical porter at the east gate of the temple (2 Chr. 31:14).

laadan_1823.name: Laadan
laadan_1823.about: White, one of the two sons of Gershon, the son of Levi (Ex. 6:17; Num. 3:18, 21).

laban_1803.name: Laban
laban_1803.about: The son of Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. He lived at Haran in Mesopotamia. His sister Rebekah was Isaac’s wife (Gen. 24). Jacob, one of the sons of this marriage, fled to the house of Laban, whose daughters Leah and Rachel (ch. 29) he eventually married.

lamech_1808.name: Lamech (descendant of Cain)
lamech_1808.about: The fifth in descent from Cain. He was the first to violate the primeval ordinance of marriage (Gen. 4:18-24). His address to his two wives, Adah and Zillah (4:23, 24), is the only extant example of antediluvian poetry. It has been called “Lamech’s sword-song.” He was “rude and ruffianly,” fearing neither God nor man. With him the curtain falls on the race of Cain. We know nothing of his descendants.

lamech_1809.name: Lamech (father of Noah)
lamech_1809.about: The seventh in descent from Seth, being the only son of Methuselah. Noah was the oldest of his several sons (Gen. 5:25-31; Luke 3:36).

lapidoth_1810.name: Lapidoth
lapidoth_1810.about: Torches. Deborah is called “the wife of Lapidoth” (Judg. 4:4). Some have rendered the expression “a woman of a fiery spirit,” under the supposition that Lapidoth is not a proper name, a woman of a torch-like spirit.

lazarus_1812.name: Lazarus
lazarus_1812.about: The brother of Mary and Martha of Bethany. He was raised from the dead after he had lain four days in the tomb (John 11:1-44). This miracle so excited the wrath of the Jews that they sought to put both Jesus and Lazarus to death.

leah_1813.name: Leah
leah_1813.about: Weary, the eldest daughter of Laban, and sister of Rachel (Gen. 29:16). Jacob took her to wife through a deceit of her father (Gen. 29:23). She was “tender-eyed” (17). She bore to Jacob six sons (32-35), also one daughter, Dinah (30:21). She accompanied Jacob into Canaan, and died there before the time of the going down into Egypt (Gen. 31), and was buried in the cave of Machpelah (49:31).

lebbaeus_1815.name: Lebbaeus Thaddaeus
lebbaeus_1815.about: Breast, the name of one of the apostles (Mark 3:18), called “Lebbaeus” in Matt. 10:3, and in Luke 6:16, “Judas the brother of James;” while John (14:22), probably referring to the same person, speaks of “Judas, not Iscariot.” These different names all designate the same person, viz., Jude or Judas, the author of the epistle.

lemuel_1817.name: Lemuel
lemuel_1817.about: Dedicated to God, a king whom his mother instructed (Prov. 31:1-9). Nothing is certainly known concerning him. The rabbis identified him with Solomon.

leummim_1819.name: Leummim
leummim_1819.about: Peoples; nations, the last mentioned of the three sons of Dedan, and head of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:3).

levi_1820.name: Levi (patriarch)
levi_1820.about: The third son of Jacob by Leah. The origin of the name is found in Leah’s words (Gen. 29:34), “This time will my husband be joined [Heb. yillaveh] unto me.” He is mentioned as taking a prominent part in avenging his sister Dinah (Gen. 34:25-31). He and his three sons went down with Jacob (46:11) into Egypt, where he died at the age of one hundred and thirty-seven years (Ex. 6:16).

levi_1822.name: Levi
levi_1822.about: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ (Luke 3:29).

lo-ammi_1827.name: Lo-ammi
lo-ammi_1827.about: Not my people, a symbolical name given by God’s command to Hosea’s second son in token of Jehovah’s rejection of his people (Hos. 1:9, 10), his treatment of them as a foreign people. This Hebrew word is rendered by “not my people” in ver. 10; 2:23.

lo-ruhamah_1829.name: Lo-ruhamah
lo-ruhamah_1829.about: Not pitied, the name of the prophet Hosea’s first daughter, a type of Jehovah’s temporary rejection of his people (Hos. 1:6; 2:23).

lois_1828.name: Lois
lois_1828.about: The maternal grandmother of Timothy. She is commended by Paul for her faith (2 Tim. 1:5).

lot_1830.name: Lot
lot_1830.about: (Heb. goral, a “pebble”), a small stone used in casting lots (Num. 33:54; Jonah 1:7). The lot was always resorted to by the Hebrews with strictest reference to the interposition of God, and as a method of ascertaining the divine will (Prov. 16:33), and in serious cases of doubt (Esther 3:7).

lotan_1831.name: Lotan
lotan_1831.about: Coverer, one of the sons of Seir, the Horite (Gen. 36:20, 29).

lucifer_1832.name: Lucifer
lucifer_1832.about: Brilliant star, a title given to the king of Babylon (Isa. 14:12) to denote his glory.

lucius_1833.name: Lucius
lucius_1833.about: Of Cyrene, a Christian teacher at Antioch (Acts 13:1), and Paul’s kinsman (Rom. 16:21). His name is Latin, but his birthplace seems to indicate that he was one of the Jews of Cyrene, in North Africa.

lud_1834.name: Lud
lud_1834.about: The fourth son of Shem (Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17), ancestor of the Lydians probably.

ludim_1835.name: Ludim
ludim_1835.about: Probably the same as Lud (2) (comp. Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11). They are associated (Jer. 46:9) with African nations as mercenaries of the king of Egypt.

luke_1836.name: Luke
luke_1836.about: The evangelist, was a Gentile. The date and circumstances of his conversion are unknown. According to his own statement (Luke 1:2), he was not an “eye-witness and minister of the word from the beginning.” It is probable that he was a physician in Troas, and was there converted by Paul, to whom he attached himself.

lydia_1837.name: Lydia
lydia_1837.about: A woman of Thyatira, a “seller of purple,” who dwelt in Philippi (Acts 16:14, 15). She was not a Jewess but a proselyte. The Lord opened her heart as she heard the gospel from the lips of Paul (16:13). She thus became the first in Europe who embraced Christianity. She was a person apparently of considerable wealth, for she could afford to give a home to Paul and his companions.

lysanias_1838.name: Lysanias
lysanias_1838.about: Tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

maacah_1839.name: Maacah
maacah_1839.about: A daughter of Talmai, king of the old native population of Geshur. She became one of David’s wives, and was the mother of Absalom (2 Sam. 3:3).

maachah_1841.name: Maachah
maachah_1841.about: The daughter of Abishalom (called Absalom, 2 Chr. 11:20-22), the third wife of Rehoboam, and mother of Abijam (1 Kings 15:2). She is called “Michaiah the daughter of Uriel,” who was the husband of Absalom’s daughter Tamar (2 Chr. 13:2). Her son Abijah or Abijam was heir to the throne.

maachah_1845.name: Maachah
maachah_1845.about: The father of Hanan, who was one of David’s body-guard (1 Chr. 11:43).

maachah_1934.name: Maachah
maachah_1934.about: The father of Achish, the king of Gath (1 Kings 2:39), called also Maoch (1 Sam. 27:2).

maaseiah_1849.name: Maaseiah
maaseiah_1849.about: One of the Levites whom David appointed as porter for the ark (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

maaseiah_1850.name: Maaseiah
maaseiah_1850.about: One of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in restoring king Jehoash to the throne (2 Chr. 23:1).

maaseiah_1853.name: Maaseiah
maaseiah_1853.about: One who was sent by king Josiah to repair the temple (2 Chr. 34:8). He was governor (Heb. sar, rendered elsewhere in the Authorized Version “prince,” “chief captain,” chief ruler”) of Jerusalem.

maaseiah_1866.name: Maaseiah
maaseiah_1866.about: The father of the priest Zephaniah (Jer. 21:1; 37:3).

maasiai_1870.name: Maasiai
maasiai_1870.about: Work of Jehovah, one of the priests resident at Jerusalem at the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:12).

maath_1871.name: Maath
maath_1871.about: Small, a person named in our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:26).

maaziah_1873.name: Maaziah
maaziah_1873.about: The head of the twenty-fourth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:18) in David’s reign.

machir_1877.name: Machir
machir_1877.about: Manasseh’s oldest son (Josh. 17:1), or probably his only son (see 1 Chr. 7:14, 15; comp. Num. 26:29-33; Josh. 13:31). His descendants are referred to under the name of Machirites, being the offspring of Gilead (Num. 26:29). They settled in land taken from the Amorites (Num. 32:39, 40; Deut. 3:15) by a special enactment (Num. 36:1-3; Josh. 17:3, 4). He is once mentioned as the representative of the tribe of Manasseh east of Jordan (Judg. 5:14).

machir_1878.name: Machir
machir_1878.about: A descendant of the preceding, residing at Lo-debar, where he maintained Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth till he was taken under the care of David (2 Sam. 9:4), and where he afterwards gave shelter to David himself when he was a fugitive (17:27).

madai_1880.name: Madai
madai_1880.about: Middle land, the third “son” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the name by which the Medes are known on the Assyrian monuments.

magog_1882.name: Magog
magog_1882.about: Region of Gog, the second of the “sons” of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5). In Ezekiel (38:2; 39:6) it is the name of a nation, probably some Scythian or Tartar tribe descended from Japheth. They are described as skilled horsemen, and expert in the use of the bow.

mahalaleel_1885.name: Mahalaleel (line of Seth)
mahalaleel_1885.about: The son of Cainan, of the line of Seth (Gen. 5:12-17); called Maleleel (Luke 3:37).

mahalath_1888.name: Mahalath
mahalath_1888.about: The daughter of Jerimoth, who was one of David’s sons. She was one of Rehoboam’s wives (2 Chr. 11:18).

mahath_150.name: Mahath
mahath_150.about: A Kohathite Levite, father of Elkanah (1 Chr. 6:35).

mahath_1891.name: Mahath
mahath_1891.about: Another Kohathite Levite, of the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

mahazioth_1893.name: Mahazioth
mahazioth_1893.about: Visions, a Kohathite Levite, chief of the twenty-third course of musicians (1 Chr. 25:4, 30).

maher-shalal-hash-baz_1894.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
maher-shalal-hash-baz_1894.about: Plunder speedeth; spoil hasteth, (Isa. 8:1-3; comp. Zeph. 1:14), a name Isaiah was commanded first to write in large characters on a tablet, and afterwards to give as a symbolical name to a son that was to be born to him (Isa. 8:1, 3), as denoting the sudden attack on Damascus and Syria by the Assyrian army.

mahlah_1895.name: Mahlah
mahlah_1895.about: Disease, one of the five daughters of Zelophehad (Num. 27:1-11) who had their father’s inheritance, the law of inheritance having been altered in their favour.

mahlon_1897.name: Mahlon
mahlon_1897.about: Sickly, the elder of Elimelech the Bethlehemite’s two sons by Naomi. He married Ruth and died childless (Ruth 1:2, 5; 4:9, 10), in the land of Moab.

mahol_1898.name: Mahol
mahol_1898.about: Dance, the father of four sons (1 Kings 4:31) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

malachi_1899.name: Malachi
malachi_1899.about: Messenger or angel, the last of the minor prophets, and the writer of the last book of the Old Testament canon (Mal. 4:4, 5, 6). Nothing is known of him beyond what is contained in his book of prophecies. Some have supposed that the name is simply a title descriptive of his character as a messenger of Jehovah, and not a proper name. There is reason, however, to conclude that Malachi was the ordinary name of the prophet.

malcham_1900.name: Malcham
malcham_1900.about: (2 Sam. 12:30, Heb., R.V., “their king;” Jer. 49:1, 3, R.V.; Zeph. 1:5), the national idol of the Ammonites. When Rabbah was taken by David, the crown of this idol was among the spoils. The weight is said to have been “a talent of gold” (above 100 lbs.). The expression probably denotes its value rather than its weight. It was adorned with precious stones.

malchi-shua_1990.name: Malchi-shua
malchi-shua_1990.about: King of help, one of the four sons of Saul (1 Chr. 8:33). He perished along with his father in the battle of Gilboa (1 Sam. 31:2).

malchiah_1906.name: Malchiah
malchiah_1906.about: A priest who stood by Ezra when he “read in the book of the law of God” (Neh. 8:4).

malchijah_1910.name: Malchijah
malchijah_1910.about: The head of the fifth division of the priests in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:9).

malchijah_1914.name: Malchijah
malchijah_1914.about: One of the priests appointed as musicians to celebrate the completion of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

malchus_1916.name: Malchus
malchus_1916.about: Reigning, the personal servant or slave of the high priest Caiaphas. He is mentioned only by John. Peter cut off his right ear in the garden of Gethsemane (John 18:10). But our Lord cured it with a touch (Matt. 26:51; Mark 14:47; Luke 22:51). This was the last miracle of bodily cure wrought by our Lord. It is not mentioned by John.

mallothi_1917.name: Mallothi
mallothi_1917.about: My fulness, a Kohathite Levite, one of the sons of Heman the Levite (1 Chr. 25:4), and chief of the nineteenth division of the temple musicians (26).

malluch_1918.name: Malluch
malluch_1918.about: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:44).

malluch_1921.name: Malluch
malluch_1921.about: A priest who returned from Babylon (Neh. 12:2).

mamre_1923.name: Mamre
mamre_1923.about: An Amoritish chief in alliance with Abraham (Gen. 14:13, 24).

manaen_1926.name: Manaen
manaen_1926.about: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch. Nothing else is known of him beyond what is stated in Acts 13:1, where he is spoken of as having been brought up with (Gr. syntrophos; rendered in R.V. “foster brother” of) Herod, i.e., Herod Antipas, the tetrach, who, with his brother Archelaus, was educated at Rome.

manasseh_1928.name: Manasseh (son of Joseph)
manasseh_1928.about: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1). There is an account of his marriage to a Syrian (1 Chr. 7:14); and the only thing afterwards recorded of him is, that his grandchildren were “brought up upon Joseph’s knees” (Gen. 50:23; R.V., “born upon Joseph’s knees”) i.e., were from their birth adopted by Joseph as his own children.

manasseh_1930.name: Manasseh (son of Hezekiah)
manasseh_1930.about: The elder of the two sons of Joseph. He and his brother Ephraim were afterwards adopted by Jacob as his own sons (48:1). There is an account of his marriage to a Syrian (1 Chr. 7:14); and the only thing afterwards recorded of him is, that his grandchildren were “brought up upon Joseph’s knees” (Gen. 50:23; R.V., “born upon Joseph’s knees”) i.e., were from their birth adopted by Joseph as his own children.

manoah_1933.name: Manoah
manoah_1933.about: Rest, a Danite, the father of Samson (Judg. 13:1-22, and 14:2-4).

mark_1679.name: John Mark
mark_1679.about: The evangelist; “John whose surname was Mark” (Acts 12:12, 25). Mark (Marcus, Col. 4:10, etc.) was his Roman name, which gradually came to supersede his Jewish name John. He is called John in Acts 13:5, 13, and Mark in 15:39, 2 Tim. 4:11, etc. He was the son of Mary, a woman apparently of some means and influence, and was probably born in Jerusalem, where his mother resided (Acts 12:12). Of his father we know nothing.

martha_1937.name: Martha
martha_1937.about: Bitterness, the sister of Lazarus and Mary, and probably the eldest of the family, who all resided at Bethany (Luke 10:38, 40, 41; John 11:1-39). From the residence being called “her house,” some have supposed that she was a widow, and that her brother and sister lodged with her.

mary_1938.name: Mary (Mother of Jesus)
mary_1938.about: The wife of Joseph, the mother of Jesus, called the “Virgin Mary,” though never so designated in Scripture (Matt. 2:11; Acts 1:14). Little is known of her personal history. Her genealogy is given in Luke 3. She was of the tribe of Judah and the lineage of David (Ps. 132:11; Luke 1:32). She was connected by marriage with Elisabeth, who was of the lineage of Aaron (Luke 1:36).

mary_1939.name: Mary (sister of Lazarus)
mary_1939.about: Mary the sister of Lazarus is brought to our notice in connection with the visits of our Lord to Bethany. She is contrasted with her sister Martha, who was “cumbered about many things” while Jesus was their guest, while Mary had chosen “the good part.” Her character also appears in connection with the death of her brother (John 11:20, 31, 33).

mary_1941.name: Mary (Mother of John Mark)
mary_1941.about: Mary the mother of John Mark was one of the earliest of our Lord’s disciples. She was the sister of Barnabas (Col. 4:10), and joined with him in disposing of their land and giving the proceeds of the sale into the treasury of the Church (Acts 4:37; 12:12). Her house in Jerusalem was the common meeting-place for the disciples there.

mary_1942.name: Mary (of Rome)
mary_1942.about: A Christian at Rome who treated Paul with special kindness (Rom. 16:6).

mary_1943.name: Mary Magdalene
mary_1943.about: A surname derived from Magdala, the place of her nativity, given to one of the Marys of the Gospels to distinguish her from the other Marys (Matt. 27:56, 61; 28:1, etc.). A mistaken notion has prevailed that this Mary was a woman of bad character, that she was the woman who is emphatically called “a sinner” (Luke 7:36-50).

mash_1944.name: Mash
mash_1944.about: (= Meshech 1 Chr. 1:17), one of the four sons of Aram, and the name of a tribe descended from him (Gen. 10:23) inhabiting some part probably of Mesopotamia. Some have supposed that they were the inhabitants of Mount Masius, the present Karja Baghlar, which forms part of the chain of Taurus.

massa_1945.name: Massa
massa_1945.about: A lifting up, gift, one of the sons of Ishmael, the founder of an Arabian tribe (Gen. 25:14); a nomad tribe inhabiting the Arabian desert toward Babylonia.

mattan_1948.name: Mattan
mattan_1948.about: A priest of Baal, slain before his altar during the reformation under Jehoiada (2 Kings 11:18).

mattaniah_1952.name: Mattaniah
mattaniah_1952.about: A Levite, son of Heman, the chief of the ninth class of temple singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 16).

mattaniah_1954.name: Mattaniah
mattaniah_1954.about: A Levite who assisted in purifying the temple at the reformation under Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

mattathias_1963.name: Mattathias
mattathias_1963.about: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:25).

mattathias_1964.name: Mattathias
mattathias_1964.about: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy (Luke 3:26).

matthan_1968.name: Matthan
matthan_1968.about: The son of Eleazar, and father of Jacob, who was the father of Joseph, the husband of the Virgin Mary (Matt. 1:15).

matthat_1969.name: Matthat
matthat_1969.about: The son of Levi, and father of Heli (Luke 3:24).

matthew_1971.name: Matthew
matthew_1971.about: Gift of God, a common Jewish name after the Exile. He was the son of Alphaeus, and was a publican or tax-gatherer at Capernaum. On one occasion Jesus, coming up from the side of the lake, passed the custom-house where Matthew was seated, and said to him, “Follow me.” Matthew arose and followed him, and became his disciple (Matt. 9:9).

mattithiah_1973.name: Mattithiah
mattithiah_1973.about: The eldest son of Shallum, of the family of Korah (1 Chr. 9:31).

mattithiah_1974.name: Mattithiah
mattithiah_1974.about: One of the sons of Jeduthun (1 Chr. 25:3, 21).

mattithiah_1976.name: Mattithiah
mattithiah_1976.about: One who stood by Ezra while reading the law (Neh. 8:4).

medan_1978.name: Medan
medan_1978.about: A son of Jokshan, Abraham’s son by Keturah (1 Chr. 1:32). His descendants settled on the Syrian borders about the territory of Edom. They probably led a pastoral life.

mehetabeel_1979.name: Mehetabeel
mehetabeel_1979.about: Whose benefactor is God, the father of Delaiah, and grandfather of Shemaiah, who joined Sanballat against Nehemiah (Neh. 6:10).

mehetabel_1980.name: Mehetabel
mehetabel_1980.about: Wife of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom (Gen. 36:39).

mehujael_1983.name: Mehujael
mehujael_1983.about: Smitten by God, the son of Irad, and father of Methusael (Gen. 4:18).

mehuman_1984.name: Mehuman
mehuman_1984.about: Faithful, one of the eunchs whom Ahasuerus (Xerxes) commanded to bring in Vashti (Esther 1:10).

mehunim_1985.name: Mehunim
mehunim_1985.about: Habitations, (2 Chr. 26:7; R.V. “Meunim,” Vulg. Ammonitae), a people against whom Uzziah waged a successful war. This word is in Hebrew the plural of Ma’on, and thus denotes the Maonites who inhabited the country on the eastern side of the Wady el-Arabah. They are again mentioned in 1 Chr. 4:41 (R.V.), in the reign of King Hezekiah, as a Hamite people, settled in the eastern end of the valley of Gedor, in the wilderness south of Palestine.

melchi_1988.name: Melchi
melchi_1988.about: The son of Addi, and father of Neri (Luke 3:28).

melchisedec_1991.name: Melchisedec
melchisedec_1991.about: King of righteousness, the king of Salem (q.v.). All we know of him is recorded in Gen. 14:18-20. He is subsequently mentioned only once in the Old Testament, in Ps. 110:4. The typical significance of his history is set forth in detail in the Epistle to the Hebrews, ch. 7.

melea_1992.name: Melea
melea_1992.about: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

melech_1993.name: Melech
melech_1993.about: King, the second of Micah’s four sons (1 Chr. 8:35), and thus grandson of Mephibosheth.

melzar_1994.name: Melzar
melzar_1994.about: Probably a Persian word meaning master of wine, i.e., chief butler; the title of an officer at the Babylonian court (Dan. 1:11, 16) who had charge of the diet of the Hebrew youths.

memucan_1995.name: Memucan
memucan_1995.about: Dignified, one of the royal counsellors at the court of Ahasuerus, by whose suggestion Vashti was divorced (Esther 1:14, 16, 21).

menahem_1996.name: Menahem
menahem_1996.about: Conforting, the son of Gadi, and successor of Shallum, king of Israel, whom he slew. After a reign of about ten years (B.C. 771-760) he died, leaving the throne to his son Pekahiah. His reign was one of cruelty and oppression (2 Kings 15:14-22). During his reign, Pul (q.v.), king of Assyria, came with a powerful force against Israel, but was induced to retire by a gift from Menahem of 1,000 talents of silver.

mephibosheth_1999.name: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth_1999.about: The son of Jonathan, and grandson of Saul (2 Sam. 4:4). He was but five years old when his father and grandfather fell on Mount Gilboa. The child’s nurse hearing of this calamity, fled with him from Gibeah, the royal residence, and stumbling in her haste, the child was thrown to the ground and maimed in both his feet, and ever after was unable to walk (19:26).

mephibosheth_2000.name: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth_2000.about: The name of Saul’s son by the concubine Rizpah (q.v.), the daughter of Aiah. He and his brother Armoni were with five others “hanged on a hill before the Lord” by the Gibeonites, and their bodies exposed in the sun for five months (2 Sam. 21:8-10).

merab_2001.name: Merab
merab_2001.about: Increase, the eldest of Saul’s two daughters (1 Sam. 14:49). She was betrothed to David after his victory over Goliath, but does not seem to have entered heartily into this arrangement (18:2, 17, 19). She was at length, however, married to Adriel of Abel-Meholah, a town in the Jordan valley, about 10 miles south of Bethshean, with whom the house of Saul maintained alliance.

meraiah_2002.name: Meraiah
meraiah_2002.about: Resistance, a chief priest, a contemporary of the high priest Joiakim (Neh. 12:12).

meraioth_2003.name: Meraioth
meraioth_2003.about: Father of Amariah, a high priest of the line of Eleazar (1 Chr. 6:6, 7, 52).

merari_2004.name: Merari
merari_2004.about: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16). He became the head of one of the great divisions of the Levites (Ex. 6:19).

mered_2005.name: Mered
mered_2005.about: Rebellion, one of the sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

meremoth_2006.name: Meremoth
meremoth_2006.about: Exaltations, heights, a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3), to whom were sent the sacred vessels (Ezra 8:33) belonging to the temple. He took part in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:4).

merodach-baladan_483.name: Merodach-baladan
merodach-baladan_483.about: Merodach has given a son, (Isa. 39:1), “the hereditary chief of the Chaldeans, a small tribe at that time settled in the marshes at the mouth of the Euphrates, but in consequence of his conquest of Babylon afterwards, they became the dominant caste in Babylonia itself.” One bearing this name sent ambassadors to Hezekiah (B.C. 721). He is also called Berodach-baladan (2 Kings 20:12; 2 Chr. 20:31).

mesha_2009.name: Mesha
mesha_2009.about: Heb. id, a king of Moab, the son of Chemosh-Gad, a man of great wealth in flocks and herds (2 Kings 3:4). After the death of Ahab at Ramoth-Gilead, Mesha shook off the yoke of Israel; but on the ascension of Jehoram to the throne of Israel, that king sought the help of Jehoshaphat in an attempt to reduce the Moabites again to their former condition.

mesha_2010.name: Mesha
mesha_2010.about: Heb. meysh’a, “deliverance,” the eldest son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:42), and brother of Jerahmeel.

meshach_2092.name: Meshach
meshach_2092.about: One of the three Hebrew youths who were trained with Daniel in Babylon (Dan. 1:11, 19), and promoted to the rank of Magi. He and his companions were afterwards cast into the burning fiery furnace for refusing to worship the idol the king had set up, from which they were miraculously delivered (3:13-30). His Chaldean name was Meshach (q.v.).

meshech_2012.name: Meshech
meshech_2012.about: Drawing out, the sixth son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2), the founder of a tribe (1 Chr. 1:5; Ezek. 27:13; 38:2, 3). They were in all probability the Moschi, a people inhabiting the Moschian Mountains, between the Black and the Caspian Seas. In Ps. 120:5 the name occurs as simply a synonym for foreigners or barbarians.

meshelemiah_2013.name: Meshelemiah
meshelemiah_2013.about: Friendship of Jehovah, a Levite of the family of the Korhites, called also Shelemiah (1 Chr. 9:21; 26:1, 2, 9, 14). He was a temple gate-keeper in the time of David.

meshillemith_2017.name: Meshillemith
meshillemith_2017.about: A priest, the son of Immer (Neh. 11:13).

meshullam_2020.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2020.about: Grandfather of Shaphan, “the scribe,” in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:3).

meshullam_2022.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2022.about: One of the chief Gadites in Bashan in the time of Jotham (1 Chr. 5:13).

meshullam_2033.name: Meshullam
meshullam_2033.about: One of the principal Israelites who supported Ezra when expounding the law to the people (Neh. 8:4).

meshullemeth_2040.name: Meshullemeth
meshullemeth_2040.about: Friend, the wife of Manasseh, and the mother of Amon (2 Kings 21:19), Kings of Judah.

methusael_2041.name: Methusael
methusael_2041.about: Champion of El; man of God, a descendant of Cain (Gen. 4:18), so called, perhaps, to denote that even among the descendants of Cain God had not left himself without a witness.

methuselah_2042.name: Methuselah
methuselah_2042.about: Man of the dart, the son of Enoch, and grandfather of Noah. He was the oldest man of whom we have any record, dying at the age of nine hundred and sixty-nine years, in the year of the Flood (Gen. 5:21-27; 1 Chr. 1:3).

mezahab_2043.name: Mezahab
mezahab_2043.about: Water of gold, the father of Matred (Gen. 36:39; 1 Chr. 1:50), and grandfather of Mehetabel, wife of Hadar, the last king of Edom.

mibhar_2045.name: Mibhar
mibhar_2045.about: Choice, a Hagarene, one of David’s warriors (1 Chr. 11:38); called also Bani the Gadite (2 Sam. 23:36).

mibsam_2046.name: Mibsam
mibsam_2046.about: One of Ishmael’s twelve sons, and head of an Arab tribe (Gen. 25:13).

mibzar_2048.name: Mibzar
mibzar_2048.about: Fortress, one of the Edomitish “dukes” descended from Esau (Gen. 36:42; 1 Chr. 1:53).

micah_2049.name: Micah
micah_2049.about: A man of Mount Ephraim, whose history so far is introduced in Judg. 17, apparently for the purpose of leading to an account of the settlement of the tribe of Dan in Northern Palestine, and for the purpose also of illustrating the lawlessness of the times in which he lived (Judg. 18; 19:1-29; 21:25).

micah_2050.name: Micah
micah_2050.about: A descendant of Joel the Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:5).

micah_2053.name: Micah
micah_2053.about: “The Morasthite,” so called to distinguish him from Micaiah, the son of Imlah (1 Kings 22:8). He was a prophet of Judah, a contemporary of Isaiah (Micah 1:1), a native of Moresheth of Gath (1:14, 15). Very little is known of the circumstances of his life (comp. Jer. 26:18, 19).

micaiah_2054.name: Micaiah
micaiah_2054.about: Who is like Jehovah?, the son of Imlah, a faithful prophet of Samaria (1 Kings 22:8-28). Three years after the great battle with Ben-hadad (20:29-34), Ahab proposed to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, that they should go up against Ramoth-Gilead to do battle again with Ben-hadad.

micha_2051.name: Micha
micha_2051.about: The son of Zabdi, a Levite of the family of Asaph (Neh. 11:17, 22).

michael_2058.name: Michael
michael_2058.about: The father of Sethur, the spy selected to represent Asher (Num. 13:13).

michael_2059.name: Michael
michael_2059.about: A chief Gadite in Bashan (1 Chr. 5:13).

michael_2062.name: Michael
michael_2062.about: 1 Chr. 7:3, a chief of the tribe of Issachar.

michael_2064.name: Michael
michael_2064.about: A Manassite, “a captain of thousands” who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:20).

michael_2066.name: Michael
michael_2066.about: One of the sons of king Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 21:2, 4). He was murdered by his brother Jehoram.

michael_2068.name: Michael
michael_2068.about: The title given to one of the chief angels (Dan. 10:13, 21; 12:1). He had special charge of Israel as a nation. He disputed with Satan (Jude 1:9) about the body of Moses. He is also represented as warning against “that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world” (Rev. 12:7-9).

michah_2052.name: Michah
michah_2052.about: The first in rank of the priests of the family of Kohathites (1 Chr. 23:20).

michaiah_2070.name: Michaiah
michaiah_2070.about: One of those sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

michaiah_2072.name: Michaiah
michaiah_2072.about: The son of Gemariah. He reported to the king’s officers Jeremiah’s prediction, which he had heard Baruch read (Jer. 36:11, 13) from his father Gemariah’s chamber in the temple.

michal_2073.name: Michal
michal_2073.about: Rivulet, or who as God?, the younger of Saul’s two daughters by his wife Ahinoam (1 Sam. 14:49, 50). “Attracted by the graces of his person and the gallantry of his conduct, she fell in love with David and became his wife” (18:20-28). She showed her affection for him by promoting his escape to Naioth when Saul sought his life (1 Sam. 19:12-17. Comp. Ps. 59. See TERAPHIM). After this she did not see David for many years.

michri_2074.name: Michri
michri_2074.about: Prize of Jehovah, a Benjamite, the father of Uzzi (1 Chr. 9:8).

midian_2075.name: Midian
midian_2075.about: Strife, the fourth son of Abraham by Keturah, the father of the Midianites (Gen. 25:2; 1 Chr. 1:32).

mikloth_2079.name: Mikloth
mikloth_2079.about: An officer under Dodai, in the time of David and Solomon (1 Chr. 27:4).

milalai_2081.name: Milalai
milalai_2081.about: Eloquent, a Levitical musician (Neh. 12:36) who took part in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem.

miniamin_2077.name: Miniamin
miniamin_2077.about: A chief priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:5), called Mijamin (10:7) and Miniamin (12:17).

miriam_2087.name: Miriam
miriam_2087.about: The sister of Moses and Aaron (Ex. 2:4-10; 1 Chr. 6:3). Her name is prominent in the history of the Exodus. She is called “the prophetess” (Ex. 15:20). She took the lead in the song of triumph after the passage of the Red Sea. She died at Kadesh during the second encampment at that place, toward the close of the wanderings in the wilderness, and was buried there (Num. 20:1).

miriam_2088.name: Miriam
miriam_2088.about: 1 Chr. 4:17, one of the descendants of Judah.

mishael_2090.name: Mishael
mishael_2090.about: A Levite; the eldest of the three sons of Uzziel (Ex. 6:22).

misham_2093.name: Misham
misham_2093.about: Their cleansing or their beholding, a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal (1 Chr. 8:12).

mishma_2094.name: Mishma
mishma_2094.about: One of the sons of Ishmael (Gen. 25:14), and founder of an Arab tribe.

mishmannah_2096.name: Mishmannah
mishmannah_2096.about: Fatness, one of the Gadite heroes who gathered to David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:10).

mispereth_2099.name: Mispereth
mispereth_2099.about: Number, one of the Jews who accompanied Zerubbabel from Babylon (Ezra 2:2); called also Mispereth (Neh. 7:7).

mizraim_2100.name: Mizraim
mizraim_2100.about: The dual form of matzor, meaning a “mound” or “fortress,” the name of a people descended from Ham (Gen. 10:6, 13; 1 Chr. 1:8, 11). It was the name generally given by the Hebrews to the land of Egypt (q.v.), and may denote the two Egypts, the Upper and the Lower. The modern Arabic name for Egypt is Muzr.

mnason_2102.name: Mnason
mnason_2102.about: Reminding, or remembrancer, a Christian of Jerusalem with whom Paul lodged (Acts 21:16). He was apparently a native of Cyprus, like Barnabas (11:19, 20), and was well known to the Christians of Caesarea (4:36). He was an “old disciple” (R.V., “early disciple”), i.e., he had become a Christian in the beginning of the formation of the Church in Jerusalem.

moab_2103.name: Moab
moab_2103.about: Used to denote the people of Moab (Num. 22:3-14; Judg. 3:30; 2 Sam. 8:2; Jer. 48:11, 13).

molech_2104.name: Molech
molech_2104.about: King, the name of the national god of the Ammonites, to whom children were sacrificed by fire. He was the consuming and destroying and also at the same time the purifying fire. In Amos 5:26, “your Moloch” of the Authorized Version is “your king” in the Revised Version (comp. Acts 7:43).

mordecai_2107.name: Mordecai
mordecai_2107.about: The son of Jair, of the tribe of Benjamin. It has been alleged that he was carried into captivity with Jeconiah, and hence that he must have been at least one hundred and twenty-nine years old in the twelfth year of Ahasuerus (Xerxes). But the words of Esther do not necessarily lead to this conclusion. It was probably Kish of whom it is said (ver. 6) that he “had been carried away with the captivity.” He resided at Susa, the metropolis of Persia.

moses_2108.name: Moses
moses_2108.about: Drawn (or Egypt. mesu, “son;” hence Rameses, royal son). On the invitation of Pharaoh (Gen. 45:17-25), Jacob and his sons went down into Egypt. This immigration took place probably about 350 years before the birth of Moses. Some centuries before Joseph, Egypt had been conquered by a pastoral Semitic race from Asia, the Hyksos, who brought into cruel subjection the native Egyptians, who were an African race.

mother_of_the_wife_of_simon_2111.name: Mother of the Wife of Simon
mother_of_the_wife_of_simon_2111.short: Mother of the Wife of Simon

moza_2113.name: Moza
moza_2113.about: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:46).

moza_2114.name: Moza
moza_2114.about: The son of Zimri, of the posterity of Saul (1 Chr. 8:36, 37; 9:42, 43).

mushi_2116.name: Mushi
mushi_2116.about: Receding, the second of the two sons of Merari (Ex. 6:19; Num. 3:20). His sons were called Mushites (Num. 3:33; 26:58).

naam_2117.name: Naam
naam_2117.about: Pleasantness, one of the three sons of Caleb, the son of Jephunneh (1 Chr. 4:15).

naamah_2118.name: Naamah (line of Cain)
naamah_2118.about: The daughter of Lamech and Zillah (Gen. 4: 22).

naamah_2119.name: Naamah
naamah_2119.about: The daughter of the king of Ammon, one of the wives of Solomon, the only one who appears to have borne him a son, viz., Rehoboam (1 Kings 14:21, 31).

naaman_2122.name: Naaman
naaman_2122.about: Pleasantness, a Syrian, the commander of the armies of Benhadad II. in the time of Joram, king of Israel. He was afflicted with leprosy; and when the little Hebrew slave-girl that waited on his wife told her of a prophet in Samaria who could cure her master, he obtained a letter from Benhadad and proceeded with it to Joram. The king of Israel suspected in this some evil design against him, and rent his clothes.

naarah_2124.name: Naarah
naarah_2124.about: A girl, the second of Ashur’s two wives, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:5, 6).

naarai_2125.name: Naarai
naarai_2125.about: Youthful, a military chief in David’s army (1 Chr. 11:37), called also Paarai (2 Sam. 23:35).

nabal_2126.name: Nabal
nabal_2126.about: Foolish, a descendant of Caleb who dwelt at Maon (1 Sam. 25), the modern Main, 7 miles south-east of Hebron.

naboth_2127.name: Naboth
naboth_2127.about: Fruits, “the Jezreelite,” was the owner of a portion of ground on the eastern slope of the hill of Jezreel (2 Kings 9:25, 26). This small “plat of ground” seems to have been all he possessed. It was a vineyard, and lay “hard by the palace of Ahab” (1 Kings 21:1, 2), who greatly coveted it. Naboth, however, refused on any terms to part with it to the king.

nadab_2128.name: Nadab
nadab_2128.about: The eldest of Aaron’s four sons (Ex. 6:23; Num. 3:2). He with his brothers and their father were consecrated as priests of Jehovah (Ex. 28:1). He afterwards perished with Abihu for the sin of offering strange fire on the altar of burnt-offering (Lev. 10:1, 2; Num. 3:4; 26:60).

nadab_2129.name: Nadab
nadab_2129.about: The son and successor of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 14:20). While engaged with all Israel in laying siege to Gibbethon, a town of southern Dan (Josh. 19:44), a conspiracy broke out in his army, and he was slain by Baasha (1 Kings 15:25-28), after a reign of two years (B.C. 955-953). The assassination of Nadab was followed by that of his whole house, and thus this great Ephraimite family became extinct (1 Kings 15:29).

nadab_2130.name: Nadab
nadab_2130.about: One of the sons of Shammai in the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 2:28, 30).

naharai_2135.name: Naharai
naharai_2135.about: Snorer, a Berothite, one of David’s heroes, and armour-bearer of Joab (1 Chr. 11:39).

nahash_2136.name: Nahash
nahash_2136.about: King of the Ammonites in the time of Saul. The inhabitants of Jabesh-Gilead having been exposed to great danger from Nahash, sent messengers to Gibeah to inform Saul of their extremity. He promptly responded to the call, and gathering together an army he marched against Nahash. “And it came to pass that they which remained were scattered, so that two of them [the Ammonites] were not left together” (1 Sam. 11:1-11).

nahash_2138.name: Nahash
nahash_2138.about: The father of Amasa, who was commander-in-chief of Abasolom’s army (2 Sam. 17:25). Jesse’s wife had apparently been first married to this man, to whom she bore Abigail and Zeruiah, who were thus David’s sisters, but only on the mother’s side (1 Chr. 2:16).

nahath_2140.name: Nahath
nahath_2140.about: A Levite, one of the overseers of the sacred offerings of the temple (2 Chr. 31:13).

nahath_2146.name: Nahath
nahath_2146.about: One of the four sons of Reuel, the son of Esau (Gen. 36:13, 17).

nahbi_2141.name: Nahbi
nahbi_2141.about: Hidden, one of the twelve spies sent out to explore the land of Canaan (Num. 13:14).

nahor_2142.name: Nahor (father of Terah)
nahor_2142.about: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham (Gen. 11:22-25; Luke 3:34).

nahor_2143.name: Nahor (brother of Abraham)
nahor_2143.about: A son of Terah, and elder brother of Abraham (Gen. 11:26, 27; Josh. 24:2, R.V.). He married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran, and remained in the land of his nativity on the east of the river Euphrates at Haran (Gen. 11:27-32). A correspondence was maintained between the family of Abraham in Canaan and the relatives in the old ancestral home at Haran till the time of Jacob.

nahshon_2144.name: Nahshon
nahshon_2144.about: Sorcerer, the son of Aminadab, and prince of the children of Judah at the time of the first numbering of the tribes in the wilderness (Ex. 6:23). His sister Elisheba was the wife of Aaron. He died in the wilderness (Num. 26:64, 65). His name occurs in the Greek form Naasson in the genealogy of Christ (Matt, 1:4; Luke 3:32).

naomi_2147.name: Naomi
naomi_2147.about: Bitter; sad, a symbolical name which Naomi gave to herself because of her misfortunes (Ruth 1:20).

naphtali_2149.name: Naphtali
naphtali_2149.about: My wrestling, the fifth son of Jacob. His mother was Bilhah, Rachel’s handmaid (Gen. 30:8). When Jacob went down into Egypt, Naphtali had four sons (Gen. 46:24). Little is known of him as an individual.

naphtuhim_2150.name: Naphtuhim
naphtuhim_2150.about: A Hamitic tribe descended from Mizraim (Gen. 10:13). Others identify this word with Napata, the name of the city and territory on the southern frontier of Mizraim, the modern Meroe, at the great bend of the Nile at Soudan. This city was the royal residence, it is said, of Queen Candace (Acts 8:27). Here there are extensive and splendid ruins.

narcissus_2151.name: Narcissus
narcissus_2151.about: Daffodil, a Roman whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:11). He is supposed to have been the private secretary of the emperor Claudius. This is, however, quite uncertain.

nathan_2152.name: Nathan
nathan_2152.about: A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

nathan_2153.name: Nathan
nathan_2153.about: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14). He was charged with the education of Solomon (12:25), at whose inauguration to the throne he took a prominent part (1 Kings 1:8, 10, 11, 22-45).

nathan_2155.name: Nathan
nathan_2155.about: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14). He was charged with the education of Solomon (12:25), at whose inauguration to the throne he took a prominent part (1 Kings 1:8, 10, 11, 22-45).

nathanael_2158.name: Nathanael
nathanael_2158.about: Given or gift of God, one of our Lord’s disciples, “of Cana in Galilee” (John 21:2). He was “an Israelite indeed, in whom was no guile” (1:47, 48). His name occurs only in the Gospel of John, who in his list of the disciples never mentions Bartholomew, with whom he has consequently been identified. He was one of those to whom the Lord showed himself alive after his resurrection, at the Sea of Tiberias.

nebajoth_2164.name: Nebajoth
