nebajoth_2164.about: Ishmael’s eldest son (Gen. 25:13), and the prince of an Israelitish tribe (16). He had a sister, Mahalath, who was one of Esau’s wives (Gen. 28:9; 36:3).

nebat_2165.name: Nebat
nebat_2165.about: Sight; aspect, the father of Jeroboam, the king of Israel (1 Kings 11:26, etc.).

nebuchadnezzar_2167.name: Nebuchadnezzar
nebuchadnezzar_2167.about: In the Babylonian orthography Nabu-kudur-uzur, which means “Nebo, protect the crown!” or the “frontiers.” In an inscription he styles himself “Nebo’s favourite.” He was the son and successor of Nabopolassar, who delivered Babylon from its dependence on Assyria and laid Nineveh in ruins. He was the greatest and most powerful of all the Babylonian kings. He married the daughter of Cyaxares, and thus the Median and Babylonian dynasties were united.

nebushasban_2168.name: Nebushasban
nebushasban_2168.about: Adorer of Nebo, or Nebo saves me, the “Rabsaris,” or chief chamberlain, of the court of Babylon. He was one of those whom the king sent to release Jeremiah from prison in Jerusalem (Jer. 39:13).

nebuzar-adan_2169.name: Nebuzar-adan
nebuzar-adan_2169.about: “the captain of the guard,” in rank next to the king, who appears prominent in directing affairs at the capture of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:8-20; Jer. 39:11; 40:2-5). He showed kindness toward Jeremiah, as commanded by Nebuchadnezzar (40:1). Five years after this he again came to Jerusalem and carried captive seven hundred and forty-five more Jews.

nedabiah_2170.name: Nedabiah
nedabiah_2170.about: Moved of Jehovah, one of the sons of Jeconiah (1 Chr. 3:18).

nehemiah_2172.name: Nehemiah
nehemiah_2172.about: The son of Hachaliah (Neh. 1:1), and probably of the tribe of Judah. His family must have belonged to Jerusalem (Neh. 2:3). He was one of the “Jews of the dispersion,” and in his youth was appointed to the important office of royal cup-bearer at the palace of Shushan. The king, Artaxerxes Longimanus, seems to have been on terms of friendly familiarity with his attendant.

nehushta_2174.name: Nehushta
nehushta_2174.about: Copper, the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, and the wife of Jehoiakin (2 Kings 24:8), king of Judah.

nemuel_2177.name: Nemuel
nemuel_2177.about: A Reubenite, a son of Eliab, and brother of Dathan and Abiram (Num. 26:9).

ner_2181.name: Ner
ner_2181.about: Light, the father of Kish (1 Chr. 8:33). 1 Sam. 14:51 should be read, “Kish, the father of Saul, and Ner, the father of Abner, were the sons of Abiel.” And hence this Kish and Ner were brothers, and Saul and Abner were first cousins (comp. 1 Chr. 9:36).

nergal-sharezer_2183.name: Nergal-sharezer
nergal-sharezer_2183.about: Another of the “princes,” who bore the title of “Rabmag.” He was one of those who were sent to release Jeremiah from prison (Jer. 39:13) by “the captain of the guard.” He was a Babylonian grandee of high rank. From profane history and the inscriptions, we are led to conclude that he was the Neriglissar who murdered Evil-merodach, the son of Nebuchadnezzar, and succeeded him on the throne of Babylon (B.C. 559-556).

nethaneel_2188.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2188.about: The son of Zuar, chief of the tribe of Issachar at the Exodus (Num. 1:8; 2:5).

nethaneel_2190.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2190.about: A priest who blew the trumpet before the ark when it was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:24).

nethaneel_2192.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2192.about: A temple porter, of the family of the Korhites (1 Chr. 26:4).

nethaneel_2193.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2193.about: One of the “princes” appointed by Jehoshaphat to teach the law through the cities of Judah (2 Chr. 17:7).

nethaneel_2194.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2194.about: A chief Levite in the time of Josiah (2 Chr. 35:9).

nethaneel_2197.name: Nethaneel
nethaneel_2197.about: A priest’s son who bore a trumpet at the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:36).

nethaniah_2200.name: Nethaniah
nethaniah_2200.about: A Levite sent by Jehoshaphat to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

nicanor_2203.name: Nicanor
nicanor_2203.about: Conqueror, one of the seven deacons appointed in the apostolic Church (Acts 6:1-6). Nothing further is known of him.

nicodemus_2204.name: Nicodemus
nicodemus_2204.about: The people is victor, a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin. He is first noticed as visiting Jesus by night (John 3:1-21) for the purpose of learning more of his doctrines, which our Lord then unfolded to him, giving prominence to the necessity of being “born again.” He is next met with in the Sanhedrin (7:50-52), where he protested against the course they were taking in plotting against Christ.

nicolas_2205.name: Nicolas
nicolas_2205.about: The victory of the people, a proselyte of Antioch, one of the seven deacons (Acts 6:5).

nimrod_2206.name: Nimrod
nimrod_2206.about: Firm, a descendant of Cush, the son of Ham. He was the first who claimed to be a “mighty one in the earth.” Babel was the beginning of his kingdom, which he gradually enlarged (Gen. 10:8-10). The “land of Nimrod” (Micah 5:6) is a designation of Assyria or of Shinar, which is a part of it.

nimshi_2207.name: Nimshi
nimshi_2207.about: Saved. Jehu was “the son of Jehoshaphat, the son of Nimshi” (2 Kings 9:2; comp. 1 Kings 19:16).

noadiah_2208.name: Noadiah
noadiah_2208.about: A Levite who returned from Babylon (Ezra 8:33).

noadiah_2209.name: Noadiah
noadiah_2209.about: A false prophetess who assisted Tobiah and Sanballat against the Jews (Neh. 6:14). Being bribed by them, she tried to stir up discontent among the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and so to embarrass Nehemiah in his great work of rebuilding the ruined walls of the city.

noah_2210.name: Noah
noah_2210.about: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second great progenitor of the human family.

noah_2211.name: Noah (daughter of Zelophehad)
noah_2211.about: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death. This patriarch is rightly regarded as the connecting link between the old and the new world. He is the second great progenitor of the human family.

nogah_2213.name: Nogah
nogah_2213.about: Splendour, one of David’s sons, born at Jerusalem (1 Chr. 3:7).

nun_2214.name: Nun
nun_2214.about: Beyond the fact that he was the father of Joshua nothing more is known of him (Ex. 33:11).

obadiah_2215.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2215.about: An Israelite who was chief in the household of King Ahab (1 Kings 18:3). Amid great spiritual degeneracy he maintained his fidelity to God, and interposed to protect The Lord’s prophets, an hundred of whom he hid at great personal risk in a cave (4, 13). Ahab seems to have held Obadiah in great honour, although he had no sympathy with his piety (5, 6, 7).

obadiah_2217.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2217.about: A chief of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:3).

obadiah_2219.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2219.about: A Levite, after the Captivity (1 Chr. 9:16).

obadiah_2220.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2220.about: A Gadite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:9).

obadiah_2221.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2221.about: A prince of Zebulun in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:19).

obadiah_2222.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2222.about: One of the princes sent by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people in the law (2 Chr. 17:7).

obadiah_2223.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2223.about: A Levite who superintended the repairs of the temple under Josiah (2 Chr. 34:12).

obadiah_2224.name: Obadiah
obadiah_2224.about: One who accompanied Ezra on the return from Babylon (Ezra 8:9).

obed_2228.name: Obed
obed_2228.about: A son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:21, 22), and the grandfather of David (Matt. 1:5).

obil_2234.name: Obil
obil_2234.about: A keeper of camels, an Ishmaelite who was “over the camels” in the time of David (1 Chr. 27:30).

oded_2237.name: Oded
oded_2237.about: A prophet in the time of Ahaz and Pekah (2 Chr. 28:9-15).

og_2238.name: Og
og_2238.about: Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons (Deut. 1:4), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 21:32-35; Deut. 3:1-13). His bedstead (or rather sarcophagus) was of iron (or ironstone), 9 cubits in length and 4 cubits in breadth. His overthrow was afterwards celebrated in song (Ps. 135:11; 136:20).

ohad_2239.name: Ohad
ohad_2239.about: United, or power, the third son of Simeon (Gen. 46:10).

ohel_2240.name: Ohel
ohel_2240.about: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:20).

olympas_2241.name: Olympas
olympas_2241.about: A Roman Christian whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:15).

omar_2242.name: Omar
omar_2242.about: Eloquent, the son of Eliphaz, who was Esau’s eldest son (Gen. 36:11-15).

omri_2243.name: Omri
omri_2243.about: Servant of Jehovah. When Elah was murdered by Zimri at Tirzah (1 Kings 16:15-27), Omri, his captain, was made king (B.C. 931). For four years there was continued opposition to his reign, Tibni, another claimant to the throne, leading the opposing party; but at the close of that period all his rivals were defeated, and he became king of Israel, “Tibni died and Omri reigned” (B.C. 927).

onan_2250.name: Onan
onan_2250.about: Strong, the second son of Judah (Gen. 38:4-10; comp. Deut. 25:5; Matt. 22:24). He died before the going down of Jacob and his family into Egypt.

onesimus_2251.name: Onesimus
onesimus_2251.about: Useful, a slave who, after robbing his master Philemon (q.v.) at Colosse, fled to Rome, where he was converted by the apostle Paul, who sent him back to his master with the epistle which bears his name. In it he beseeches Philemon to receive his slave as a “faithful and beloved brother.” Paul offers to pay to Philemon anything his slave had taken, and to bear the wrong he had done him.

onesiphorus_2252.name: Onesiphorus
onesiphorus_2252.about: Bringing profit, an Ephesian Christian who showed great kindness to Paul at Rome. He served him in many things, and had oft refreshed him. Paul expresses a warm interest in him and his household (2 Tim. 1:16-18; 4:19).

ophir_2253.name: Ophir
ophir_2253.about: One of the sons of Joktan (Gen. 10:29).

oreb_2255.name: Oreb
oreb_2255.about: Raven, a prince of Midian, who, being defeated by Gideon and put to straits, was slain along with Zeeb (Judg. 7:20-25). Many of the Midianites perished along with him (Ps. 83:9; Isa. 10:26).

oren_2256.name: Oren
oren_2256.about: Ash or pine, the son of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25).

ornan_289.name: Ornan
ornan_289.about: Agile; also called Ornan 1 Chr. 21:15, a Jebusite who dwelt in Jerusalem before it was taken by the Israelites. The destroying angel, sent to punish David for his vanity in taking a census of the people, was stayed in his work of destruction near a threshing-floor belonging to Araunah which was situated on Mount Moriah.

orpah_2257.name: Orpah
orpah_2257.about: Forelock or fawn, a Moabitess, the wife of Chilion (Ruth 1:4; 4:10). On the death of her husband she accompanied Naomi, her mother-in-law, part of the way to Bethlehem, and then returned to Moab.

othni_2258.name: Othni
othni_2258.about: A lion of Jehovah, a son of Shemaiah, and one of the temple porters in the time of David (1 Chr. 26:7). He was a “mighty man of valour.”

othniel_2259.name: Othniel
othniel_2259.about: Lion of God, the first of the judges. His wife Achsah was the daughter of Caleb (Josh. 15:16, 17; Judg. 1:13). He gained her hand as a reward for his bravery in leading a successful expedition against Debir (q.v.). Some thirty years after the death of Joshua, the Israelites fell under the subjection of Chushan-rishathaim (q.v.), the king of Mesopotamia.

ozem_2260.name: Ozem
ozem_2260.about: One of David’s brothers; the sixth son of Jesse (1 Chr. 2:15).

ozni_1235.name: Ozni
ozni_1235.about: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

paarai_2262.name: Paarai
paarai_2262.about: Opening of the Lord, “the Arbite,” one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:35); called also Naarai, 1 Chr. 11:37.

pagiel_2264.name: Pagiel
pagiel_2264.about: God allots, a prince of the tribe of Asher (Num. 1:13), in the wilderness.

pahath-moab_2265.name: Pahath-moab
pahath-moab_2265.about: Governor of Moab, a person whose descendants returned from the Captivity and assisted in rebuilding Jerusalem (Ezra 2:6; 8:4; 10:30).

pallu_2325.name: Pallu
pallu_2325.about: Separated, the second son of Reuben (1 Chr. 5:3); called Phallu, Gen. 46:9. He was the father of the Phalluites (Ex. 6:14; Num. 26:5, 8).

palti_2269.name: Palti
palti_2269.about: Deliverance from the Lord, one of the spies representing the tribe of Benjamin (Num. 13:9).

paltiel_2270.name: Paltiel
paltiel_2270.about: Deliverance of God, the prince of Issachar who assisted “to divide the land by inheritance” (Num. 34:26).

parmashta_2271.name: Parmashta
parmashta_2271.about: Strong-fisted, a son of Haman, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:9).

parshandatha_2277.name: Parshandatha
parshandatha_2277.about: An interpreter of the law, the eldest of Haman’s sons, slain in Shushan (Esther 9:7).

paruah_2278.name: Paruah
paruah_2278.about: Flourishing, the father of Jehoshaphat, appointed to provide monthly supplies for Solomon from the tribe of Issachar (1 Kings 4:17).

pasach_2279.name: Pasach
pasach_2279.about: Clearing, one of the sons of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher (1 Chr. 7:33).

patrobas_2289.name: Patrobas
patrobas_2289.about: A Christian at Rome to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

paul_2479.name: Paul
paul_2479.about: '=Saul (q.v.) was born about the same time as our Lord. His circumcision-name was Saul, and probably the name Paul was also given to him in infancy “for use in the Gentile world,” as “Saul” would be his Hebrew home-name. He was a native of Tarsus, the capital of Cilicia, a Roman province in the south-east of Asia Minor.

pedahel_2290.name: Pedahel
pedahel_2290.about: Redeemed of God, the son of Ammihud, a prince of Naphtali (Num. 34:28).

pedahzur_2291.name: Pedahzur
pedahzur_2291.about: Rock of redemption, the father of Gamaliel and prince of Manasseh at the time of the Exodus (Num. 1:10; 2:20).

pedaiah_2292.name: Pedaiah
pedaiah_2292.about: The father of Zebudah, who was the wife of Josiah and mother of king Jehoiakim (2 Kings 23:36).

pedaiah_2294.name: Pedaiah
pedaiah_2294.about: . The father of Joel, ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh (1 Chr. 27:20).

pekah_2299.name: Pekah
pekah_2299.about: Open-eyed, the son of Remaliah a captain in the army of Pekahiah, king of Israel, whom he slew, with the aid of a band of Gileadites, and succeeded (B.C. 758) on the throne (2 Kings 15:25). Seventeen years after this he entered into an alliance with Rezin, king of Syria, and took part with him in besieging Jerusalem (2 Kings 15:37; 16:5).

pekahiah_2300.name: Pekahiah
pekahiah_2300.about: The Lord opened his eyes, the son and successor of Menahem on the throne of Israel. He was murdered in the royal palace of Samaria by Pekah, one of the captains of his army (2 Kings 15:23-26), after a reign of two years (B.C. 761-759). He “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord.”

pelaiah_2302.name: Pelaiah
pelaiah_2302.about: A Levite who expounded the law (Neh. 8:7).

pelatiah_2304.name: Pelatiah
pelatiah_2304.about: A son of Hananiah and grandson of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:21).

pelatiah_2307.name: Pelatiah
pelatiah_2307.about: One of the twenty-five princes of the people against whom Ezekiel prophesied on account of their wicked counsel (Ezek. 11:1-13).

peleg_2308.name: Peleg
peleg_2308.about: Division, one of the sons of Eber; so called because “in his days was the earth divided” (Gen. 10:25). Possibly he may have lived at the time of the dispersion from Babel. But more probably the reference is to the dispersion of the two races which sprang from Eber, the one spreading towards Mesopotamia and Syria, and the other southward into Arabia.

pelet_2310.name: Pelet
pelet_2310.about: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:3).

peleth_2311.name: Peleth
peleth_2311.about: A Reubenite whose son was one of the conspirators against Moses and Aaron (Num. 16:1).

peleth_2312.name: Peleth
peleth_2312.about: One of the sons of Jonathan (1 Chr. 2:33).

perida_2318.name: Perida
perida_2318.about: One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:55); called also Perida (Neh. 7:57).

persis_2317.name: Persis
persis_2317.about: A female Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:12). She is spoken of as “beloved,” and as having “laboured much in the Lord.”

peter_2745.name: Simon Peter
peter_2745.about: Originally called Simon (=Simeon, i.e., “hearing”), a very common Jewish name in the New Testament. He was the son of Jona (Matt. 16:17). His mother is nowhere named in Scripture. He had a younger brother called Andrew, who first brought him to Jesus (John 1:40-42). His native town was Bethsaida, on the western coast of the Sea of Galilee, to which also Philip belonged.

pethahiah_2319.name: Pethahiah
pethahiah_2319.about: The chief of one of the priestly courses (the nineteenth) in the time of David (1 Chr. 24:16).

pethahiah_2322.name: Pethahiah
pethahiah_2322.about: A descendant of Judah who had some office at the court of Persia (Neh. 11:24).

pethuel_2323.name: Pethuel
pethuel_2323.about: Vision of God, the father of Joel the prophet (Joel 1:1).

peulthai_2324.name: Peulthai
peulthai_2324.about: Wages of the Lord, one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite porter (1 Chr. 26:5).

phaltiel_2326.name: Phaltiel
phaltiel_2326.about: Deliverance of the Lord, the son of Laish of Gallim (1 Sam. 25:44)= Phaltiel (2 Sam. 3:15). Michal, David’s wife, was given to him.

phanuel_2327.name: Phanuel
phanuel_2327.about: Face of God, father of the prophetess Anna (q.v.), Luke 2:36.

pharaoh_2328.name: Pharaoh (during Abraham's Journey)
pharaoh_2328.about: The Pharaoh who was on the throne when Abram went down into Egypt (Gen. 12:10-20) was probably one of the Hyksos, or “shepherd kings.” The Egyptians called the nomad tribes of Syria Shasu, “plunderers,” their king or chief Hyk, and hence the name of those invaders who conquered the native kings and established a strong government, with Zoan or Tanis as their capital. They were of Semitic origin, and of kindred blood accordingly with Abram.

pharaoh_2329.name: Pharaoh (of Joseph)
pharaoh_2329.about: The Pharaoh of Joseph’s days (Gen. 41) was probably Apopi, or Apopis, the last of the Hyksos kings. To the old native Egyptians, who were an African race, shepherds were “an abomination;” but to the Hyksos kings these Asiatic shepherds who now appeared with Jacob at their head were congenial, and being akin to their own race, had a warm welcome (Gen. 47:5, 6).

pharaoh_2330.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2330.about: The “new king who knew not Joseph” (Ex. 1:8-22) has been generally supposed to have been Aahmes I., or Amosis, as he is called by Josephus. Recent discoveries, however, have led to the conclusion that Seti was the “new king.” For about seventy years the Hebrews in Egypt were under the powerful protection of Joseph. After his death their condition was probably very slowly and gradually changed.

pharaoh_2331.name: Pharaoh (of the Exodus)
pharaoh_2331.about: The Pharaoh of the Exodus was probably Menephtah I., the fourteenth and eldest surviving son of Rameses II. He resided at Zoan, where he had the various interviews with Moses and Aaron recorded in the book of Exodus. His mummy was not among those found at Deir el-Bahari. It is still a question, however, whether Seti II. or his father Menephtah was the Pharaoh of the Exodus.

pharaoh_2333.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh_2333.about: Pharaoh, in whom Hezekiah put his trust in his war against Sennacherib (2 Kings 18:21).

pharez_2338.name: Pharez
pharez_2338.about: '=Pharez, (q.v.), breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3). Four hundred and sixty-eight of his “sons” came back from captivity with Zerubbabel, who himself was one of them (1 Chr. 9:4; Neh. 11:6).

phebe_2340.name: Phebe
phebe_2340.about: A “deaconess of the church at Cenchrea,” the port of Corinth. She was probably the bearer of Paul’s epistle to the Romans. Paul commended her to the Christians at Rome; “for she hath been,” says he, “a succourer of many, and of myself also” (Rom. 16:1, 2).

phichol_2341.name: Phichol
phichol_2341.about: Great, the chief captain of the army of Abimelech, the Philistine king of Gerar. He entered into an alliance with Abraham with reference to a certain well which, from this circumstance, was called Beersheba (q.v.), “the well of the oath” (Gen. 21:22, 32; 26:26).

philemon_2342.name: Philemon
philemon_2342.about: An inhabitant of Colosse, and apparently a person of some note among the citizens (Col. 4:9; Philemon 1:2). He was brought to a knowledge of the gospel through the instrumentality of Paul (19), and held a prominent place in the Christian community for his piety and beneficence (4-7).

philetus_2343.name: Philetus
philetus_2343.about: Amiable, with Hymenaeus, at Ephesus, said that the “resurrection was past already” (2 Tim. 2:17, 18). This was a Gnostic heresy held by the Nicolaitanes.

philip_2344.name: Phillip the Apostle
philip_2344.about: One of the twelve apostles; a native of Bethsaida, “the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44). He readily responded to the call of Jesus when first addressed to him (43), and forthwith brought Nathanael also to Jesus (45, 46). He seems to have held a prominent place among the apostles (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18; John 6:5-7; 12:21, 22; 14:8, 9; Acts 1:13). Of his later life nothing is certainly known.

philip_2345.name: Philip
philip_2345.about: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome. (See HEROD PHILIP I.)

philip_2347.name: Phillip the Evangelist
philip_2347.about: One of the “seven” (Acts 6:5), called also “the evangelist” (21:8, 9). He was one of those who were “scattered abroad” by the persecution that arose on the death of Stephen. He went first to Samaria, where he laboured as an evangelist with much success (8:5-13). While he was there he received a divine command to proceed toward the south, along the road leading from Jerusalem to Gaza. These towns were connected by two roads.

phinehas_2349.name: Phinehas (Levite)
phinehas_2349.about: Son of Eleazar, the high priest (Ex. 6:25). While yet a youth he distinguished himself at Shittim by his zeal against the immorality into which the Moabites had tempted the people (Num. 25:1-9), and thus “stayed the plague” that had broken out among the people, and by which twenty-four thousand of them perished. For his faithfulness on that occasion he received the divine approbation (10-13).

phinehas_2350.name: Phinehas
phinehas_2350.about: One of the sons of Eli, the high priest (1 Sam. 1:3; 2:12). He and his brother Hophni were guilty of great crimes, for which destruction came on the house of Eli (31). He died in battle with the Philistines (1 Sam. 4:4, 11); and his wife, on hearing of his death, gave birth to a son, whom she called “Ichabod,” and then she died (19-22).

phlegon_2352.name: Phlegon
phlegon_2352.about: Burning, a Roman Christian to whom Paul sent salutations (Rom. 16:14).

phut_2354.name: Phut
phut_2354.about: One of the sons of Ham (Gen. 10:6).

phygellus_2356.name: Phygellus
phygellus_2356.about: Fugitive, a Christian of Asia, who “turned away” from Paul during his second imprisonment at Rome (2 Tim. 1:15). Nothing more is known of him.

pilate_2365.name: Pontius Pilate
pilate_2365.about: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one. He was the sixth in the order of the Roman procurators of Judea (A.D. 26-36). His headquarters were at Caesarea, but he frequently went up to Jerusalem.

portius_2367.name: Portius Festus
portius_2367.about: The successor of Felix (A.D. 60) as procurator of Judea (Acts 24:27). A few weeks after he had entered on his office the case of Paul, then a prisoner at Caesarea, was reported to him.

potiphar_2368.name: Potiphar
potiphar_2368.about: Dedicated to Ra; i.e., to the sun-god, the Egyptian to whom the Ishmaelites sold Joseph (Gen. 39:1). He was “captain of the guard”, i.e., chief, probably, of the state police, who, while they formed part of the Egyptian army, were also largely employed in civil duties (37:36; marg., “chief of the executioners”). Joseph, though a foreigner, gradually gained his confidence, and became overseer over all his possessions.

priscilla_2370.name: Priscilla
priscilla_2370.about: The wife of Aquila (Acts 18:2), who is never mentioned without her. Her name sometimes takes the precedence of his (Rom. 16:3; 2 Tim. 4:19). She took part with Aquila (q.v.) in insturcting Apollos (Acts 18:26).

puah_2372.name: Puah
puah_2372.about: One of the two midwives who feared God, and refused to kill the Hebrew male children at their birth (Ex. 1:15-21).

publius_2374.name: Publius
publius_2374.about: “the chief man of the island” of Malta (Acts 28:7), who courteously entertained Paul and his shipwrecked companions for three days, till they found a more permanent place of residence; for they remained on the island for three months, till the stormy season had passed. The word here rendered “chief man” (protos) is supposed by some to be properly a Maltese term, the official title of the governor.

pudens_2375.name: Pudens
pudens_2375.about: Bashful, a Christian at Rome, who sent his greetings to Timothy (2 Tim. 4:21).

quartus_2378.name: Quartus
quartus_2378.about: Fourth, a Corinthian Christian who sent by Paul his salutations to friends at Rome (Rom. 16:23).

raamah_2380.name: Raamah
raamah_2380.about: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

rabsaris_2382.name: Rabsaris
rabsaris_2382.about: Chief of the Heads, one of the three officers whom Sennacherib sent from Lachish with a threatening message to Jerusalem (2 Kings 18:17; Jer. 39:3, 13).

rabshakeh_2384.name: Rabshakeh
rabshakeh_2384.about: Chief of the princes, the name given to the chief cup-bearer or the vizier of the Assyrian court; one of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah. See the speech he delivered, in the Hebrew language, in the hearing of all the people, as he stood near the wall on the north side of the city (2 Kings 18:17-37). He and the other envoys returned to their master and reported that Hezekiah and his people were obdurate, and would not submit.

rachab_2385.name: Rachab
rachab_2385.about: '=Rahab, a name found in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:5).

rachel_2386.name: Rachel
rachel_2386.about: Ewe, “the daughter”, “the somewhat petulant, peevish, and self-willed though beautiful younger daughter” of Laban, and one of Jacob’s wives (Gen. 29:6, 28). He served Laban fourteen years for her, so deep was Jacob’s affection for her. She was the mother of Joseph (Gen. 30:22-24). Afterwards, on Jacob’s departure from Mesopotamia, she took with her her father’s teraphim (31:34, 35).

rahab_2388.name: Rahab
rahab_2388.about: Insolence; pride, a poetical name applied to Egypt in Ps. 87:4; 89:10; Isa. 51:9, as “the proud one.” Rahab, (Heb. Rahab; i.e., “broad,” “large”).

raham_2389.name: Raham
raham_2389.about: Merciful, one of the descendants of Caleb, the son of Hezron (1 Chr. 2:44).

ram_2391.name: Ram
ram_2391.about: The son of Hezron, and one of the ancestors of the royal line (Ruth 4:19). The margin of 1 Chr. 2:9, also Matt. 1:3, 4 and Luke 3:33, have “Aram.”

ram_2392.name: Ram
ram_2392.about: One of the sons of Jerahmeel (1 Chr. 2:25, 27).

ram_2393.name: Ram
ram_2393.about: A person mentioned in Job 32:2 as founder of a clan to which Elihu belonged. The same as Aram of Gen. 22:21.

rapha_2447.name: Rapha
rapha_2447.about: A Benjamite, the son of Binea (1 Chr. 8:2, 37), a descendant of Saul.

raphu_2397.name: Raphu
raphu_2397.about: Healed, a Benjamite, whose son Palti was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:9).

reba_2400.name: Reba
reba_2400.about: Fourth, one of the Midianite chiefs slain by the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 31:8; Josh. 13:21).

rebekah_2401.name: Rebekah
rebekah_2401.about: A noose, the daughter of Bethuel, and the wife of Isaac (Gen. 22:23; 24:67). The circumstances under which Abraham’s “steward” found her at the “city of Nahor,” in Padan-aram, are narrated in Gen. 24-27. “She can hardly be regarded as an amiable woman.

rechab_2402.name: Rechab
rechab_2402.about: One of Ishbosheth’s “captains of bands” or leaders of predatory troops (2 Sam. 4:2).

rechab_2403.name: Rechab
rechab_2403.about: The father of Jehonadab, who was the father of the Rechabites (2 Kings 10:15, 23; Jer. 35:6-19).

reelaiah_2406.name: Reelaiah
reelaiah_2406.about: Thunder of the Lord, one of the princes who returned from the Exile (Neh. 7:7); called also Reelaiah (Ezra 2:2).

regem-melech_2408.name: Regem-melech
regem-melech_2408.about: Friend of the king, one of the two messengers sent by the exiled Jews to Jerusalem in the time of Darius (Zech. 7:2) to make inquiries at the temple.

rehabiah_2409.name: Rehabiah
rehabiah_2409.about: Enlargement of the Lord, the son of Eliezer, and grandson of Moses (1 Chr. 23:17; 24:21).

rehob_2410.name: Rehob
rehob_2410.about: The father of Hadadezer, king of Tobah (2 Sam. 8:3, 12).

rehoboam_2412.name: Rehoboam
rehoboam_2412.about: He enlarges the people, the successor of Solomon on the throne, and apparently his only son. He was the son of Naamah “the Ammonitess,” some well-known Ammonitish princess (1 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 12:13). He was forty-one years old when he ascended the throne, and he reigned seventeen years (B.C. 975-958).

rehum_2413.name: Rehum
rehum_2413.about: One of “the children of the province” who returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:2); the same as “Nehum” (Neh. 7:7).

rehum_2414.name: Rehum
rehum_2414.about: The “chancellor” of Artaxerxes, who sought to stir him up against the Jews (Ezra 4:8-24) and prevent the rebuilding of the walls and the temple of Jerusalem.

rei_2417.name: Rei
rei_2417.about: Friendly, one who maintained true allegiance to king David (1 Kings 1:8) when Adonijah rebelled.

rekem_2418.name: Rekem
rekem_2418.about: One of the five Midianite kings whom the Israelites destroyed (Num. 31:8).

rekem_2419.name: Rekem
rekem_2419.about: One of the sons of Hebron (1 Chr. 2:43, 44).

remaliah_2420.name: Remaliah
remaliah_2420.about: Adorned by the Lord, the father of Pekah, who conspired successfully against Pekahiah (2 Kings 15:25, 27, 30, 32, 37; Isa. 7:1, 4, 5, 9; 8:6).

rephael_2421.name: Rephael
rephael_2421.about: Healed of God, one of Shemaiah’s sons. He and his brethren, on account of their “strength for service,” formed one of the divisions of the temple porters (1 Chr. 26:7, 8).

reuben_2429.name: Reuben
reuben_2429.about: Behold a son!, the eldest son of Jacob and Leah (Gen. 29:32). His sinful conduct, referred to in Gen. 35:22, brought down upon him his dying father’s malediction (48:4). He showed kindness to Joseph, and was the means of saving his life when his other brothers would have put him to death (37:21, 22). It was he also who pledged his life and the life of his sons when Jacob was unwilling to let Benjamin go down into Egypt.

reuel_2430.name: Reuel
reuel_2430.about: A son of Esau and Bashemath (Gen. 36:4, 10; 1 Chr. 1:35).

rezin_2435.name: Rezin
rezin_2435.about: Firm; a prince, a king of Syria, who joined Pekah (q.v.) in an invasion of the kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 15:37; 16:5-9; Isa. 7:1-8). Ahaz induced Tiglath-pileser III. to attack Damascus, and this caused Rezin to withdraw for the purpose of defending his own kingdom. Damascus was taken, and Rezin was slain in battle by the Assyrian king, and his people carried into captivity, B.C. 732 (2 Kings 16:9).

rezon_2437.name: Rezon
rezon_2437.about: Prince, son of Eliadah. Abandoning the service of Hadadezer, the king of Zobah, on the occasion of his being defeated by David, he became the “captain over a band” of marauders, and took Damascus, and became king of Syria (1 Kings 11:23-25; 2 Sam. 8:3-8). For centuries after this the Syrians were the foes of Israel. He “became an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon.”

rhesa_2438.name: Rhesa
rhesa_2438.about: Affection, son of Zorobabel, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:27).

rhoda_2439.name: Rhoda
rhoda_2439.about: A rose, the damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark. She came to hearken when Peter knocked at the door of the gate (Acts 12:12-15).

rimmon_2441.name: Rimmon
rimmon_2441.about: A man of Beeroth (2 Sam. 4:2), one of the four Gibeonite cities. (See Josh. 9:17.)

riphath_2443.name: Riphath
riphath_2443.about: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

rizpah_2444.name: Rizpah
rizpah_2444.about: Coal; hot stone, the daughter of Aiah, and one of Saul’s concubines. She was the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth (2 Sam. 3:7; 21:8, 10, 11). It happened that a grievous famine, which lasted for three years, fell upon the land during the earlier half of David’s reign at Jerusalem.

romamti-ezer_2446.name: Romamti-ezer
romamti-ezer_2446.about: Elevation of help, one of the sons of Heman, “the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn.” He was head of the “four-and-twentieth” course of singers (1 Chr. 25:4, 31).

ruth_2450.name: Ruth
ruth_2450.about: A friend, a Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, whose father, Elimelech, had settled in the land of Moab. On the death of Elimelech and Mahlon, Naomi came with Ruth, her daughter-in-law, who refused to leave her, to Bethlehem, the old home from which Elimelech had migrated. There she had a rich relative, Boaz, to whom Ruth was eventually married. She became the mother of Obed, the grandfather of David.

sabtah_2451.name: Sabtah
sabtah_2451.about: Rest, the third son of Cush (Gen. 10:7; 1 Chr. 1:9).

sacar_2453.name: Sacar
sacar_2453.about: A son of Obed-edom the Gittite, and a temple porter (1 Chr. 26:4).

sadoc_2454.name: Sadoc
sadoc_2454.about: Just, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Matt. 1:14).

salah_2455.name: Salah
salah_2455.about: A shoot, a descendant of Arphaxed (Luke 3:35, 36); called also Shelah (1 Chr. 1:18, 24).

salathiel_2457.name: Salathiel
salathiel_2457.about: Whom I asked of God, the son of Jeconiah (Matt. 1:12; 1 Chr. 3:17); also called the son of Neri (Luke 3:27). The probable explanation of the apparent discrepancy is that he was the son of Neri, the descendant of Nathan, and thus heir to the throne of David on the death of Jeconiah (comp. Jer. 22:30).

salmon_2463.name: Salmon
salmon_2463.about: Shady; or Zalmon (q.v.), a hill covered with dark forests, south of Shechem, from which Abimelech and his men gathered wood to burn that city (Judg. 9:48). In Ps. 68:14 the change from war to peace is likened to snow on the dark mountain, as some interpret the expression. Others suppose the words here mean that the bones of the slain left unburied covered the land, so that it seemed to be white as if covered with snow.

salome_2464.name: Salome
salome_2464.about: The wife of Zebedee and mother of James and John (Mat. 27:56), and probably the sister of Mary, the mother of our Lord (John 19:25). She sought for her sons places of honour in Christ’s kingdom (Matt. 20:20, 21; comp. 19:28). She witnessed the crucifixion (Mark 15:40), and was present with the other women at the sepulchre (Matt. 27:56).

samgar-nebo_2466.name: Samgar-nebo
samgar-nebo_2466.about: Be gracious, O Nebo! or a cup-bearer of Nebo, probably the title of Nergal-sharezer, one of the princes of Babylon (Jer. 39:3).

samson_2468.name: Samson
samson_2468.about: Of the sun, the son of Manoah, born at Zorah. The narrative of his life is given in Judg. 13-16. He was a “Nazarite unto God” from his birth, the first Nazarite mentioned in Scripture (Judg. 13:3-5; comp. Num. 6:1-21). The first recorded event of his life was his marriage with a Philistine woman of Timnath (Judg. 14:1-5).

samuel_2469.name: Samuel
samuel_2469.about: Heard of God. The peculiar circumstances connected with his birth are recorded in 1 Sam. 1:20. Hannah, one of the two wives of Elkanah, who came up to Shiloh to worship before the Lord, earnestly prayed to God that she might become the mother of a son. Her prayer was graciously granted; and after the child was weaned she brought him to Shiloh nd consecrated him to the Lord as a perpetual Nazarite (1:23-2:11).

sanballat_2470.name: Sanballat
sanballat_2470.about: Held some place of authority in Samaria when Nehemiah went up to Jerusalem to rebuild its ruined walls. He vainly attempted to hinder this work (Neh. 2:10, 19; 4:1-12; 6). His daughter became the wife of one of the sons of Joiada, a son of the high priest, much to the grief of Nehemiah (13:28).

sapphira_2472.name: Sapphira
sapphira_2472.about: Beautiful, the wife of Ananias (q.v.). She was a partner in his guilt and also in his punishment (Acts 5:1-11).

sarah_2473.name: Sarah
sarah_2473.about: Princess, the wife and at the same time the half-sister of Abraham (Gen. 11:29; 20:12). This name was given to her at the time that it was announced to Abraham that she should be the mother of the promised child. Her story is from her marriage identified with that of the patriarch till the time of her death.

satan_2476.name: Satan
satan_2476.about: Adversary; accuser. When used as a proper name, the Hebrew word so rendered has the article “the adversary” (Job 1:6-12; 2:1-7). In the New Testament it is used as interchangeable with Diabolos, or the devil, and is so used more than thirty times.

saul_2478.name: Saul
saul_2478.about: The son of Kish (probably his only son, and a child of prayer, “asked for”), of the tribe of Benjamin, the first king of the Jewish nation. The singular providential circumstances connected with his election as king are recorded in 1 Sam. 8-10. His father’s she-asses had strayed, and Saul was sent with a servant to seek for them.

sceva_2480.name: Sceva
sceva_2480.about: An implement, a Jew, chief of the priests at Ephesus (Acts 19:13-16); i.e., the head of one of the twenty-four courses of the house of Levi. He had seven sons, who “took upon them to call over them which had evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus,” in imitation of Paul. They tried their method of exorcism on a fierce demoniac, and failed.

seba_2481.name: Seba
seba_2481.about: One of the sons of Cush (Gen. 10:7).

secundus_2482.name: Secundus
secundus_2482.about: Second, a Christian of Thessalonica who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4).

segub_2483.name: Segub
segub_2483.about: The youngest son of Hiel the Bethelite. His death is recorded in 1 Kings 16:34 (comp. Josh. 6:26).

seir_2485.name: Seir
seir_2485.about: A Horite; one of the “dukes” of Edom (Gen. 36:20-30).

semei_2488.name: Semei
semei_2488.about: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

sennacherib_2489.name: Sennacherib
sennacherib_2489.about: Sin (the god) sends many brothers, son of Sargon, whom he succeeded on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 705), in the 23rd year of Hezekiah. “Like the Persian Xerxes, he was weak and vainglorious, cowardly under reverse, and cruel and boastful in success.” He first set himself to break up the powerful combination of princes who were in league against him. Among these was Hezekiah, who had entered into an alliance with Egypt against Assyria.

seorim_2491.name: Seorim
seorim_2491.about: Barley, the chief of the forth priestly course (1 Chr. 24:8).

serah_2492.name: Serah
serah_2492.about: Abundance; princess, the daughter of Asher and grand-daughter of Jacob (Gen. 46:17); called also Sarah (Num. 26:46; R.V., “Serah”).

seraiah_2498.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2498.about: A priest of the days of Jehoiakim (Neh. 12:1, 12).

seraiah_2500.name: Seraiah
seraiah_2500.about: The son of Neriah. When Zedekiah made a journey to Babylon to do homage to Nebuchadnezzar, Seraiah had charge of the royal gifts to be presented on that occasion. Jeremiah took advantage of the occasion, and sent with Seraiah a word of cheer to the exiles in Babylon, and an announcement of the doom in store for that guilty city.

sered_2501.name: Sered
sered_2501.about: Fear, one of the sons of Zebulun (Gen. 46:14).

sergius_2502.name: Sergius Paulus
sergius_2502.about: A “prudent man” (R.V., “man of understanding”), the deputy (R.V., “proconsul”) of Cyprus (Acts 13:6-13). He became a convert to Christianity under Paul, who visited this island on his first mission to the heathen. A remarkable memorial of this proconsul was recently (1887) discovered at Rome.

serug_2503.name: Serug
serug_2503.about: Branch, the father of Nahor (Gen. 11:20-23); called Saruch in Luke 3:35.

seth_2504.name: Seth
seth_2504.about: Appointed; a substitute, the third son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4:25; 5:3). His mother gave him this name, “for God,” said she, “hath appointed me [i.e., compensated me with] another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.”

sethur_2505.name: Sethur
sethur_2505.about: Hidden, one of the spies sent to search the Promised Land. He was of the tribe of Asher (Num. 13:13).

shaashgaz_2508.name: Shaashgaz
shaashgaz_2508.about: Servant of the beautiful, a chief eunuch in the second house of the harem of king Ahasuerus (Esther 2:14).

shadrach_1398.name: Shadrach
shadrach_1398.about: Aku’s command, the Chaldean name given to Hananiah, one of the Hebrew youths whom Nebuchadnezzar carried captive to Babylon (Dan. 1:6, 7; 3:12-30). He and his two companions refused to bow down before the image which Nebuchadnezzar had set up on the plains of Dura. Their conduct filled the king with the greatest fury, and he commanded them to be cast into the burning fiery furnace.

shallum_2514.name: Shallum
shallum_2514.about: The son of Jabesh, otherwise unknown. He “conspired against Zachariah, and smote him before the people, and slew him, and reigned in his stead” (2 Kings 15:10). He reigned only “a month of days in Samaria” (15:13, marg.). Menahem rose up against Shallum and put him to death (2 Kings 15:14, 15, 17), and became king in his stead.

shallum_2515.name: Shallum
shallum_2515.about: Keeper of the temple vestments in the reign of Josiah (2 Kings 22:14).

shallum_2517.name: Shallum
shallum_2517.about: One of the posterity of Judah (1 Chr. 2:40, 41).

shallum_2520.name: Shallum
shallum_2520.about: A keeper of the gate in the reign of David (1 Chr. 9:17).

shallum_2525.name: Shallum
shallum_2525.about: The uncle of the prophet Jeremiah (Jer. 32:7).

shalmaneser_2529.name: Shalmaneser
shalmaneser_2529.about: An Assyrian king (Hos. 10:14), identified with Shalmaneser II. (Sayce) or IV. (Lenormant), the successor of Pul on the throne of Assyria (B.C. 728). He made war against Hoshea, the king of Israel, whom he subdued and compelled to pay an annual tribute. Hoshea, however, soon after rebelled against his Assyrian conquerer.

shamer_2725.name: Shamer
shamer_2725.about: A man of Asher (1 Chr. 7:32); called also Shamer (34).

shamgar_2534.name: Shamgar
shamgar_2534.about: The Philistines from the maritime plain had made incursions into the Hebrew upland for the purposes of plunder, when one of this name, the son of Anath, otherwise unknown, headed a rising for the purpose of freeing the land from this oppression. He repelled the invasion, slaying 600 men with an “ox goad” (q.v.). The goad was a formidable sharpointed instrument, sometimes ten feet long.

shamir_2536.name: Shamir
shamir_2536.about: One of the sons of Michah (1 Chr. 24:24).

shammah_2539.name: Shammah
shammah_2539.about: One of David’s three mighty men (2 Sam. 23:11, 12).

shammah_2540.name: Shammah
shammah_2540.about: One of David’s mighties (2 Sam. 23:25); called also Shammoth (1 Chr. 11:27) and Shamhuth (27:8).

shammah_2700.name: Shammah
shammah_2700.about: One of the sons of Jesse (1 Sam. 16:9). He is also called Shimeah (2 Sam. 13:3) and Shimma (1 Chr. 2:13).

shammua_2545.name: Shammua
shammua_2545.about: One of the spies sent out by Moses to search the land (Num. 13:4). He represented the tribe of Reuben.

shammua_2547.name: Shammua
shammua_2547.about: One of David’s sons by Bathsheba (1 Chr. 3:5); called also Shammua (14:4).

shaphan_2550.name: Shaphan
shaphan_2550.about: A coney, a scribe or secretary of king Josiah (2 Kings 22:3-7). He consulted Huldah concerning the newly-discovered copy of the law which was delivered to him by Hilkiah the priest (8-14). His grandson Gedaliah was governor of Judea (25:22).

shaphat_2552.name: Shaphat
shaphat_2552.about: One of the spies. He represented the tribe of Simeon (Num. 13:5).

shaphat_2556.name: Shaphat
shaphat_2556.about: One of David’s chief herdsmen (1 Chr. 27:29).

sharar_2558.name: Sharar
sharar_2558.about: One of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:35); called also Sharar (2 Sam. 23:33).

sharezer_2559.name: Sharezer
sharezer_2559.about: (god) protect the king!, a son of Sennacherib, king of Assyria. He and his brother Adrammelech murdered their father, and then fled into the land of Armenia (2 Kings 19:37).

shaul_2477.name: Shaul
shaul_2477.about: A king of Edom (Gen. 36:37, 38); called Shaul in 1 Chr. 1:48.

shavsha_2493.name: Shavsha
shavsha_2493.about: (“Seraiah,” 2 Sam. 8:17; “Shisha,” 1 Kings 4:3), one of David’s secretaries (1 Chr. 18:16).

shealtiel_2456.name: Shealtiel
shealtiel_2456.about: Asked for of God, father of Zerubbabel (Ezra 3:2, 8; Neh. 12:1).

sheba_2567.name: Sheba (son of Raamah)
sheba_2567.about: Heb. shebha, the son of Raamah (Gen. 10:7), whose descendants settled with those of Dedan on the Persian Gulf.

sheba_2568.name: Sheba (son of Joktan)
sheba_2568.about: Heb. id. A son of Joktan (Gen. 10:28), probably the founder of the Sabeans.

sheba_2569.name: Sheba
sheba_2569.about: Heb. id. A son of Jokshan, who was a son of Abraham by Keturah (Gen. 25:3).

sheba_2570.name: Sheba
sheba_2570.about: Heb. id. A “son of Bichri,” of the family of Becher, the son of Benjamin, and thus of the stem from which Saul was descended (2 Sam. 20:1-22). When David was returning to Jerusalem after the defeat of Absalom, a strife arose between the ten tribes and the tribe of Judah, because the latter took the lead in bringing back the king.

shebaniah_2572.name: Shebaniah
shebaniah_2572.about: A Levite appointed to blow the trumpet before the ark of God (1 Chr. 15:24).

shebaniah_2574.name: Shebaniah
shebaniah_2574.about: A priest who returned from the Captivity with Zerubbabel (Neh. 12:3; marg., or Shebaniah).

shebna_2577.name: Shebna
shebna_2577.about: Tender youth, “treasurer” over the house in the reign of Hezekiah, i.e., comptroller or governor of the palace. On account of his pride he was ejected from his office, and Eliakim was promoted to it (Isa. 22:15-25). He appears to have been the leader of the party who favoured an alliance with Egypt against Assyria.

shecaniah_2581.name: Shecaniah
shecaniah_2581.about: A priest to whom the tenth lot came forth when David divided the priests (1 Chr. 24:11).

shecaniah_2582.name: Shecaniah
shecaniah_2582.about: One of the priests who were set “to give to their brethren by courses” of the daily portion (2 Chr. 31:15). Shechani’ah, id.

shechaniah_2583.name: Shechaniah
shechaniah_2583.about: A priest whose sons are mentioned in 1 Chr. 3:21, 22.

shechaniah_2586.name: Shechaniah
shechaniah_2586.about: The father of Shemaiah, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:29).

shechem_2588.name: Shechem
shechem_2588.about: The son of Hamor the Hivite (Gen. 33:19; 34).

shelemiah_2600.name: Shelemiah
shelemiah_2600.about: Father of one of those who accused Jeremiah to Zedekiah (Jer. 37:3; 38:1).

shelemiah_2601.name: Shelemiah
shelemiah_2601.about: Father of a captain of the ward (Jer. 37:13).

shem_2613.name: Shem
shem_2613.about: A name; renown, the first mentioned of the sons of Noah (Gen. 5:32; 6:10). He was probably the eldest of Noah’s sons. The words “brother of Japheth the elder” in Gen. 10:21 are more correctly rendered “the elder brother of Japheth,” as in the Revised Version. Shem’s name is generally mentioned first in the list of Noah’s sons. He and his wife were saved in the ark (7:13). Noah foretold his preeminence over Canaan (9:23-27).

shema_2617.name: Shema
shema_2617.about: One who stood by Ezra when he read the law (Neh. 8:4).

shemaah_2618.name: Shemaah
shemaah_2618.about: Rumour, a Benjamite whose sons “came to David to Ziklag” (1 Chr. 12:3).

shemaiah_2619.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2619.about: A prophet in the reign of Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:22-24).

shemaiah_2625.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2625.about: A Levite in the time of David, who with 200 of his brethren took part in the bringing up of the ark from Obed-edom to Hebron (1 Chr. 15:8).

shemaiah_2627.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2627.about: The eldest son of Obed-edom (1 Chr. 26:4-8).

shemaiah_2628.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2628.about: One of the Levites whom Jehoshaphat appointed to teach the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

shemaiah_2630.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2630.about: A Levite appointed to “distribute the oblations of the Lord” (2 Chr. 31:15).

shemaiah_2637.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2637.about: A false prophet who hindered the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Neh. 6:10).

shemaiah_2642.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2642.about: The father of Urijah the prophet (Jer. 26:20).

shemaiah_2643.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2643.about: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah (Jer. 29:24-32).

shemaiah_2644.name: Shemaiah
shemaiah_2644.about: The father of a prince in the reign of Jehoiakim (Jer. 36:12).

shemariah_2645.name: Shemariah
shemariah_2645.about: One who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

shemeber_2648.name: Shemeber
shemeber_2648.about: Soaring on high, the king of Zeboiim, who joined with the other kings in casting off the yoke of Chedorlaomer. After having been reconquered by him, he was rescued by Abraham (Gen. 14:2).

shemiramoth_2651.name: Shemiramoth
shemiramoth_2651.about: A Levite in David’s time (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

shemiramoth_2652.name: Shemiramoth
shemiramoth_2652.about: A Levite in the reign of Jehoshaphat (2 Chr. 17:8).

shemuel_2653.name: Shemuel
shemuel_2653.about: The son of Ammihud. He represented Simeon in the division of the land (Num. 34:20).

shemuel_2654.name: Shemuel
shemuel_2654.about: A prince of the tribe of Issachar (1 Chr. 7:2).

shephatiah_2658.name: Shephatiah
shephatiah_2658.about: A Benjamite who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

shephatiah_2659.name: Shephatiah
shephatiah_2659.about: A Simeonite prince in David’s time (1 Chr. 27:16).

shephatiah_2664.name: Shephatiah
shephatiah_2664.about: One of the princes who urged the putting of Jeremiah to death (Jer. 38:1-4).

sheresh_2669.name: Sheresh
sheresh_2669.about: Root, a descendant of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:16).

sherezer_2670.name: Sherezer
sherezer_2670.about: One of the messengers whom the children of the Captivity sent to Jerusalem “to pray for them before the Lord” (Zech. 7:2).

shethar_2673.name: Shethar
shethar_2673.about: A star, a prince at the court of Ahasuerus (Esther 1:14).

shethar-boznai_2674.name: Shethar-boznai
shethar-boznai_2674.about: Star of splendour, a Persian officer who vainly attempted to hinder the rebuilding of the temple (Ezra 5:3, 6; 6:6, 13).

shimea_2680.name: Shimea
shimea_2680.about: A Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 6:30).

shimea_2681.name: Shimea
shimea_2681.about: Another Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:39).

shimeah_2682.name: Shimeah
shimeah_2682.about: A Benjamite, a descendant of Gibeon (1 Chr. 8:32); called also Shimeam (9:38).

shimei_691.name: Shimei
shimei_691.about: A Levite of the family of Gershon (1 Chr. 6:42).

shimei_2684.name: Shimei
shimei_2684.about: A Benjamite of the house of Saul, who stoned and cursed David when he reached Bahurim in his flight from Jerusalem on the occasion of the rebellion of Absalom (2 Sam. 16:5-13).

shimei_2685.name: Shimei
shimei_2685.about: One of David’s mighty men who refused to acknowledge Adonijah as David’s successor (1 Kings 1:8). He is probably the same person who is called elsewhere (4:18) “the son of Elah.”

shimei_2686.name: Shimei
shimei_2686.about: A son of Pedaiah, the brother of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:19).

shimei_2690.name: Shimei
shimei_2690.about: A Ramathite who was “over the vineyards” of David (1 Chr. 27:27).

shimei_2691.name: Shimei
shimei_2691.about: One of the sons of Heman, who assisted in the purification of the temple (2 Chr. 29:14).

shimri_2704.name: Shimri
shimri_2704.about: The father of one of the “valiant men” of David’s armies (1 Chr. 11:45).

shimri_2705.name: Shimri
shimri_2705.about: Assisted at the purification of the temple in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

shimrith_2724.name: Shimrith
shimrith_2724.about: The mother of Jehozabad, who murdered Joash (2 Kings 12:21); called also Shimrith, a Moabitess (2 Chr. 24:26).

shimron_2706.name: Shimron
shimron_2706.about: Watchman, the fourth son of Issachar (Gen. 46:13; 1 Chr. 7:1; R.V., correctly, “Shimron”).

shimshai_2707.name: Shimshai
shimshai_2707.about: The shining one, or sunny, the secretary of Rehum the chancellor, who took part in opposing the rebuilding of the temple after the Captivity (Ezra 4:8, 9, 17-23).

shinab_2708.name: Shinab
shinab_2708.about: Cooling, the king of Adamah, in the valley of Siddim, who with his confederates was conquered by Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

shiphrah_2710.name: Shiphrah
shiphrah_2710.about: Beauty, one of the Egyptian midwives (Ex. 1:15).

shiphtan_2711.name: Shiphtan
shiphtan_2711.about: Judicial, an Ephraimite prince at the time of the division of Canaan (Num. 34:24).

shishak_2712.name: Shishak
shishak_2712.about: '=Sheshonk I., king of Egypt. His reign was one of great national success, and a record of his wars and conquests adorns the portico of what are called the “Bubastite kings” at Karnak, the ancient Thebes. Among these conquests is a record of that of Judea. In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign Shishak came up against the kingdom of Judah with a powerful army. He took the fenced cities and came to Jerusalem.

shobab_2715.name: Shobab
shobab_2715.about: One of David’s sons by Bathseheba (2 Sam. 5:14).

shobab_2716.name: Shobab
shobab_2716.about: One of the sons of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:18), the son of Hezron.

shobach_2717.name: Shobach
shobach_2717.about: Poured out, the “captain of the host of Hadarezer” when he mustered his vassals and tributaries from beyond “the river Euphrates” (2 Sam. 10:15-18); called also Shophach (1 Chr. 19:16).

shobal_2719.name: Shobal
shobal_2719.about: The second son of Seir the Horite; one of the Horite “dukes” (Gen. 36:20).

shobal_2720.name: Shobal
shobal_2720.about: One of the sons of Caleb, and a descendant of Hur (1 Chr. 2:50, 52; 4:1, 2).

shobi_2722.name: Shobi
shobi_2722.about: Captor, son of Nahash of Rabbah, the Ammonite. He showed kindness to David when he fled from Jerusalem to Mahanaim (2 Sam. 17:27).

shua_2726.name: Shua
shua_2726.about: A daughter of Heber the Asherite (1 Chr. 7:32).

shuah_2727.name: Shuah
shuah_2727.about: One of Abraham’s sons by Keturah (Gen. 25:2; Chr. 1:32).

shuah_2728.name: Shuah
shuah_2728.about: A Canaanite whose daughter was married to Judah (1 Chr. 2:3).

shubael_2579.name: Shubael
shubael_2579.about: One of the descendants of Gershom, who had charge of the temple treasures in the time of David (1 Chr. 23:16; 26:24).

shubael_2580.name: Shubael
shubael_2580.about: One of the sons of Heman; one of those whose duty it was to “lift up the horn” in the temple service (1 Chr. 25:4, 5); called also Shubael (ver. 20).

sibbechai_2737.name: Sibbechai
sibbechai_2737.about: The Lord sustains, one of David’s heroes (1 Chr. 11:29), general of the eighth division of the army (27:11). He slew the giant Saph in the battle of Gob (2 Sam. 21:18; R.V., “Sibbechai”). Called also Mebunnai (23:27).

sihon_2739.name: Sihon
sihon_2739.about: Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them. The Israelites went forth against him to battle, and gained a complete victory.

silas_2740.name: Silas
silas_2740.about: Wood, a prominent member of the church at Jerusalem; also called Silvanus. He and Judas, surnamed Barsabas, were chosen by the church there to accompany Paul and Barnabas on their return to Antioch from the council of the apostles and elders (Acts 15:22), as bearers of the decree adopted by the council. He assisted Paul there in his evangelistic labours, and was also chosen by him to be his companion on his second missionary tour (Acts 16:19-24).

simeon_2741.name: Simeon
simeon_2741.about: The second son of Jacob by Leah (Gen. 29:33). He was associated with Levi in the terrible act of vengeance against Hamor and the Shechemites (34:25, 26). He was detained by Joseph in Egypt as a hostage (42:24). His father, when dying, pronounced a malediction against him (49:5-7). The words in the Authorized Version (49:6), “they digged down a wall,” ought to be, as correctly rendered in the Revised Version, “they houghed an ox.”

simeon_2743.name: Simeon
simeon_2743.about: One of the ancestors of Joseph (Luke 3:30).

simeon_2744.name: Simeon
simeon_2744.about: Surnamed Niger, i.e., “black,” perhaps from his dark complexion, a teacher of some distinction in the church of Antioch (Acts 13:1-3). It has been supposed that this was the Simon of Cyrene who bore Christ’s cross. Note the number of nationalities represented in the church at Antioch.

simon_2746.name: Simon Zelotes
simon_2746.about: One of the twelve apostles, called the Canaanite (Matt. 10:4; Mark 3:18). This word “Canaanite” does not mean a native of Canaan, but is derived from the Syriac word Kanean or Kaneniah, which was the name of a Jewish sect.

simon_2747.name: Simon
simon_2747.about: One of the brothers of our Lord (Matt. 13:55; Mark 6:3).

simon_2748.name: Simon
simon_2748.about: A leper of Bethany, in whose house Mary anointed our Lord’s head with ointment “as he sat at meat” (Matt. 26:6-13; Mark 14:3-9).

simon_2749.name: Simon
simon_2749.about: A Jew of Cyrene, in North Africa, then a province of Libya. A hundred thousand Jews from Palestine had been settled in this province by Ptolemy Soter (B.C. 323-285), where by this time they had greatly increased in number. They had a synagogue in Jerusalem for such of their number as went thither to the annual feasts.

simon_2752.name: Simon the Sorcerer
simon_2752.about: A sorcerer of great repute for his magical arts among the Samaritans (Acts 8:9-11). He afterwards became a professed convert to the faith under the preaching of Philip the deacon and evangelist (12, 13). His profession was, however, soon found to be hollow. His conduct called forth from Peter a stern rebuke (8:18-23). From this moment he disappears from the Church’s history.

simon_2753.name: Simon the Tanner
simon_2753.about: A Christian at Joppa, a tanner by trade, with whom Peter on one occasion lodged (Acts 9:43).

simri_2754.name: Simri
simri_2754.about: Watchman, a Levite of the family of Merari (1 Chr. 26:10).

sinite_2755.name: Sinite
sinite_2755.about: An inhabitant of Sin, near Arka (Gen. 10:17; 1 Chr. 1:15).

sippai_2471.name: Sippai
sippai_2471.about: Extension, the son of the giant whom Sibbechai slew (2 Sam. 21:18); called also Sippai (1 Chr. 20:4).

sisera_2757.name: Sisera (army captain)
sisera_2757.about: The captain of Jabin’s army (Judg. 4:2), which was routed and destroyed by the army of Barak on the plain of Esdraelon. After all was lost he fled to the settlement of Heber the Kenite in the plain of Zaanaim. Jael, Heber’s wife, received him into her tent with apparent hospitality, and “gave him butter” (i.e., lebben, or curdled milk) “in a lordly dish.” Having drunk the refreshing beverage, he lay down, and soon sank into the sleep of the weary.

sisera_2758.name: Sisera
sisera_2758.about: The ancestor of some of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:53; Neh. 7:55).

so_2760.name: So
so_2760.about: (Nubian, Sabako), an Ethiopian king who brought Egypt under his sway. He was bribed by Hoshea to help him against the Assyrian monarch Shalmaneser (2 Kings 17:4). This was a return to the policy that had been successful in the reign of Jeroboam I.

solomon_2762.name: Solomon
solomon_2762.about: Peaceful, (Heb. Shelomoh), David’s second son by Bathsheba, i.e., the first after their legal marriage (2 Sam. 12). He was probably born about B.C. 1035 (1 Chr. 22:5; 29:1). He succeeded his father on the throne in early manhood, probably about sixteen or eighteen years of age. Nathan, to whom his education was intrusted, called him Jedidiah, i.e., “beloved of the Lord” (2 Sam. 12:24, 25).

sopater_2770.name: Sopater
sopater_2770.about: The father who saves, probably the same as Sosipater, a kinsman of Paul (Rom. 16:21), a Christian of the city of Berea who accompanied Paul into Asia (Acts 20:4-6).

sosthenes_2772.name: Sosthenes
sosthenes_2772.about: Safe in strength, the chief ruler of the synagogue at Corinth, who was seized and beaten by the mob in the presence of Gallio, the Roman governor, when he refused to proceed against Paul at the instigation of the Jews (Acts 18:12-17). The motives of this assault against Sosthenes are not recorded, nor is it mentioned whether it was made by Greeks or Romans.

stachys_2774.name: Stachys
stachys_2774.about: Spike; an ear of corn, a convert at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:9).

stephanas_2801.name: Stephanas
stephanas_2801.about: Crown, a member of the church at Corinth, whose family were among those the apostle had baptized (1 Cor. 1:16; 16:15, 17). He has been supposed by some to have been the “jailer of Philippi” (comp. Acts 16:33). The First Epistle to the Corinthians was written from Philippi some six years after the jailer’s conversion, and he was with the apostle there at that time.

stephen_2802.name: Stephen
stephen_2802.about: One of the seven deacons, who became a preacher of the gospel. He was the first Christian martyr. His personal character and history are recorded in Acts 6. “He fell asleep” with a prayer for his persecutors on his lips (7:60). Devout men carried him to his grave (8:2). It was at the feet of the young Pharisee, Saul of Tarsus, that those who stoned him laid their clothes (comp. Deut. 17:5-7) before they began their cruel work.

susanna_2804.name: Susanna
susanna_2804.about: Lily, with other pious women, ministered to Jesus (Luke 8:3).

susi_2805.name: Susi
susi_2805.about: The father of Gaddi, who was one of the twelve spies (Num. 13:11).

syntyche_2806.name: Syntyche
syntyche_2806.about: Fortunate; affable, a female member of the church at Philippi, whom Paul beseeches to be of one mind with Euodias (Phil. 4:2, 3).

tabbaoth_2807.name: Tabbaoth
tabbaoth_2807.about: Impressions; rings, “the children of,” returned from the Captivity (Ezra 2:43).

tabeal_2808.name: Tabeal
tabeal_2808.about: Goodness of God, the father of one whom the kings of Syria and Samaria in vain attempted to place on the throne of Ahaz (Isa. 7:6).

tabeel_2809.name: Tabeel
tabeel_2809.about: A Persian governor of Samaria, who joined others in the attempt to prevent the rebuilding of Jerusalem (Ezra 4:7).

tabrimon_2811.name: Tabrimon
tabrimon_2811.about: Good is Rimmon, the father of Benhadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

tahpenes_2817.name: Tahpenes
tahpenes_2817.about: The wife of Pharaoh, who gave her sister in marriage to Hadad the Edomite (1 Kings 11:19, 20).

talmai_2818.name: Talmai
talmai_2818.about: One of the Anakim of Hebron, who were slain by the men of Judah under Caleb (Num. 13:22; Josh. 15:14; Judg. 1:10).

talmai_2819.name: Talmai
talmai_2819.about: A king of Geshur, to whom Absalom fled after he had put Amnon to death (2 Sam. 3:3; 13:37). His daughter, Maachah, was one of David’s wives, and the mother of Absalom (1 Chr. 3:2).

tamar_2821.name: Tamar
tamar_2821.about: The daughter-in-law of Judah, to whose eldest son, Er, she was married (Gen. 38:6). After her husband’s death, she was married to Onan, his brother (8), and on his death, Judah promised to her that his third son, Shelah, would become her husband. This promise was not fulfilled, and hence Tamar’s revenge and Judah’s great guilt (38:12-30).

tamar_2822.name: Tamar
tamar_2822.about: A daughter of David (2 Sam. 13:1-32; 1 Chr. 3:9), whom Amnon shamefully outraged and afterwards “hated exceedingly,” thereby illustrating the law of human nature noticed even by the heathen, “Proprium humani ingenii est odisse quem laeseris”, i.e., “It is the property of human nature to hate one whom you have injured.”

tanhumeth_2824.name: Tanhumeth
tanhumeth_2824.about: Consolation, a Netophathite; one of the captains who supported Gedaliah (2 Kings 25:23; Jer. 40:8).

tarshish_2828.name: Tarshish (son of Javan)
tarshish_2828.about: One of the “sons” of Javan (Gen. 10:4; 1 Chr. 1:7).

tartan_2830.name: Tartan
tartan_2830.about: One of Sennacherib’s messengers to Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17).

tatnai_2831.name: Tatnai
tatnai_2831.about: Gift, a Persian governor (Heb. pehah, i.e., “satrap;” modern “pasha”) “on this side the river”, i.e., of the whole tract on the west of the Euphrates. This Hebrew title pehah is given to governors of provinces generally. It is given to Nehemiah (5:14) and to Zerubbabel (Hag. 1:1). It is sometimes translated “captain” (1 Kings 20:24; Dan. 3:2, 3), sometimes also “deputy” (Esther 8:9; 9:3).

temeni_2840.name: Temeni
temeni_2840.about: One of the sons of Ashur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chr. 4:6).

terah_2841.name: Terah
terah_2841.about: The wanderer; loiterer, for some unknown reason emigrated with his family from his native mountains in the north to the plains of Mesopotamia. He had three sons, Haran, Nahor, and Abraham, and one daughter, Sarah. He settled in “Ur of the Chaldees,” where his son Haran died, leaving behind him his son Lot. Nahor settled at Haran, a place on the way to Ur.

teresh_2842.name: Teresh
teresh_2842.about: Severe, a eunuch or chamberlain in the palace of Ahasuerus, who conspired with another to murder him. The plot was detected by Mordecai, and the conspirators were put to death (Esther 2:21; 6:2).

tertullus_2844.name: Tertullus
tertullus_2844.about: A modification of “Tertius;” a Roman advocate, whom the Jews employed to state their case against Paul in the presence of Felix (Acts 24:1-9). The charges he adduced against the apostle were, “First, that he created disturbances among the Romans throughout the empire, an offence against the Roman government (crimen majestatis).

thahash_2845.name: Thahash
thahash_2845.about: A badger, a son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother (Gen. 22:24).

the_giant_in_gath_2848.name: the giant in Gath
the_giant_in_gath_2848.about: Heb. ‘Anakim (Deut. 2:10, 11, 21; Josh. 11:21, 22; 14:12, 15; called “sons of Anak,” Num. 13:33; “children of Anak,” 13:22; Josh. 15:14), a nomad race of giants descended from Arba (Josh. 14:15), the father of Anak, that dwelt in the south of Palestine near Hebron (Gen. 23:2; Josh. 15:13). They were a Cushite tribe of the same race as the Philistines and the Egyptian shepherd kings. David on several occasions encountered them (2 Sam. 21:15-22).

theophilus_2849.name: Theophilus
theophilus_2849.about: Lover of God, a Christian, probably a Roman, to whom Luke dedicated both his Gospel (Luke 1:3) and the Acts of the Apostles (1:1). Nothing beyond this is known of him. From the fact that Luke applies to him the title “most excellent”, the same title Paul uses in addressing Felix (Acts 23:26; 24:3) and Festus (26:25), it has been concluded that Theophilus was a person of rank, perhaps a Roman officer.

theudas_2850.name: Theudas
theudas_2850.about: Thanksgiving, referred to by Gamaliel in his speech before the council at Jerusalem (Acts 5:36). He headed an insurrection against the Roman authority. Beyond this nothing is known of him.

thomas_2851.name: Thomas
thomas_2851.about: Twin, one of the twelve (Matt. 10:3; Mark 3:18, etc.). He was also called Didymus (John 11:16; 20:24), which is the Greek equivalent of the Hebrew name. All we know regarding him is recorded in the fourth Gospel (John 11:15, 16; 14:4, 5; 20:24, 25, 26-29).

tiberius_2852.name: Tiberius
tiberius_2852.about: I.e., as known in Roman history, Tiberius Claudius Nero, only mentioned in Luke 3:1. He was the stepson of Augustus, whom he succeeded on the throne, A.D. 14. He was noted for his vicious and infamous life. In the fifteenth year of his reign John the Baptist entered on his public ministry, and under him also our Lord taught and suffered. He died A.D. 37.

tibni_2853.name: Tibni
tibni_2853.about: Building of Jehovah, the son of Ginath, a man of some position, whom a considerable number of the people chose as monarch. For the period of four years he contended for the throne with Omri (1 Kings 16:21, 22), who at length gained the mastery, and became sole monarch of Israel.

tidal_2854.name: Tidal
tidal_2854.about: (in the LXX. called “Thorgal”), styled the “king of nations” (Gen. 14:1-9). Mentioned as Tudkhula on Arioch’s brick (see facing page 139). Goyyim, translated “nations,” is the country called Gutium, east of Tigris and north of Elam.

tilgath-pilneser_2376.name: Tilgath-pilneser
tilgath-pilneser_2376.about: An Assyrian king. It has been a question whether he was identical with Tiglath-pileser III. (q.v.), or was his predecessor. The weight of evidence is certainly in favour of their identity. Pul was the throne-name he bore in Babylonia as king of Babylon, and Tiglath-pileser the throne-name he bore as king of Assyria. He was the founder of what is called the second Assyrian empire. He consolidated and organized his conquests on a large scale.

timaeus_2858.name: Timaeus
timaeus_2858.about: Defiled, the father of blind Bartimaeus (Mark 10:46).

timon_2862.name: Timon
timon_2862.about: Honouring, one of the seven deacons at Jerusalem (Acts 6:5). Nothing further is known of him.

timotheus_2863.name: Timotheus
timotheus_2863.about: Honouring God, a young disciple who was Paul’s companion in many of his journeyings. His mother, Eunice, and his grandmother, Lois, are mentioned as eminent for their piety (2 Tim. 1:5). We know nothing of his father but that he was a Greek (Acts 16:1).

tiras_2864.name: Tiras
tiras_2864.about: The youngest of the sons of Japheth (Gen. 10:2; 1 Chr. 1:5).

tirhakah_2865.name: Tirhakah
tirhakah_2865.about: The last king of Egypt of the Ethiopian (the fifteenth) dynasty. He was the brother-in-law of So (q.v.). He probably ascended the throne about B.C. 692, having been previously king of Ethiopia (2 Kings 19:9; Isa. 37:9), which with Egypt now formed one nation. He was a great warrior, and but little is known of him.

tirzah_2868.name: Tirzah
tirzah_2868.about: The youngest of Zelophehad’s five daughters (Num. 26:33; Josh. 17:3).

titus_2869.name: Titus
titus_2869.about: Honourable, was with Paul and Barnabas at Antioch, and accompanied them to the council at Jerusalem (Gal. 2:1-3; Acts 15:2), although his name nowhere occurs in the Acts of the Apostles. He appears to have been a Gentile, and to have been chiefly engaged in ministering to Gentiles; for Paul sternly refused to have him circumcised, inasmuch as in his case the cause of gospel liberty was at stake.

tobadonijah_2870.name: Tobadonijah
tobadonijah_2870.about: Good is Jehovah, my Lord, a Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat to instruct the people of Judah in the law (2 Chr. 17:8).

tobiah_2872.name: Tobiah
tobiah_2872.about: Pleasing to Jehovah, the “servant,” the “Ammonite,” who joined with those who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Exile (Neh. 2:10). He was a man of great influence, which he exerted in opposition to the Jews, and “sent letters” to Nehemiah “to put him in fear” (Neh. 6:17-19).

tobijah_2873.name: Tobijah
tobijah_2873.about: Id., a Levite sent out through Judah by Jehoshaphat to teach the people (2 Chr. 17:8).

togarmah_2875.name: Togarmah
togarmah_2875.about: A son of Gomer, and grandson of Japheth (Gen. 10:3).

toi_2877.name: Toi
toi_2877.about: A king of Hamath, who sent “Joram his son unto King David to salute him,” when he “heard that David had smitten all the host of Hadadezer” (2 Sam. 8:9, 10). Called Tou (1 Chr. 18:9, 10).

tola_2879.name: Tola
tola_2879.about: A judge of the tribe of Issachar who “judged” Israel twenty-three years (Judg. 10:1, 2), when he died, and was buried in Shamir. He was succeeded by Jair.

trophimus_2880.name: Trophimus
trophimus_2880.about: A foster-child, an Ephesian who accompanied Paul during a part of his third missionary journey (Acts 20:4; 21:29). He was with Paul in Jerusalem, and the Jews, supposing that the apostle had brought him with him into the temple, raised a tumult which resulted in Paul’s imprisonment. (See TEMPLE, HEROD’S.) In writing to Timothy, the apostle says, “Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick” (2 Tim. 4:20).

tubal-cain_2884.name: Tubal-cain
tubal-cain_2884.about: The son of Lamech and Zillah, “an instructor of every artificer in brass and iron” (Gen. 4:22; R.V., “the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and iron”).

tychicus_2885.name: Tychicus
tychicus_2885.about: Chance, an Asiatic Christian, a “faithful minister in the Lord” (Eph. 6:21, 22), who, with Trophimus, accompanied Paul on a part of his journey from Macedonia to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4). He is alluded to also in Col. 4:7, Titus 3:12, and 2 Tim. 4:12 as having been with Paul at Rome, whence he sent him to Ephesus, probably for the purpose of building up and encouraging the church there.

tyrannus_2886.name: Tyrannus
tyrannus_2886.about: Prince, a Greek rhetorician, in whose “school” at Ephesus Paul disputed daily for the space of two years with those who came to him (Acts 19:9). Some have supposed that he was a Jew, and that his “school” was a private synagogue.

ucal_2887.name: Ucal
ucal_2887.about: The name of a person to whom Agur’s words are addressed (Prov. 30:1).

unni_2891.name: Unni
unni_2891.about: A Levite whom David appointed to take part in bringing the ark up to Jerusalem from the house of Obed-edom by playing the psaltery on that occasion (1 Chr. 15:18, 20).

unni_2892.name: Unni
unni_2892.about: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel from the Captivity (Neh. 12:9).

uriah_2898.name: Uriah
uriah_2898.about: A Hittite, the husband of Bathsheba, whom David first seduced, and then after Uriah’s death married. He was one of the band of David’s “mighty men.” The sad story of the curel wrongs inflicted upon him by David and of his mournful death are simply told in the sacred record (2 Sam. 11:2-12:26).

uriel_2900.name: Uriel
uriel_2900.about: A Kohathite ancestor of the prophet Samuel (1 Chr. 6:36).

uriel_2901.name: Uriel
uriel_2901.about: The chief of the Kohathites at the time when the ark was brought up to Jerusalem (1 Chr. 15:5, 11).

uriel_2902.name: Uriel
uriel_2902.about: The father of Michaiah, one of Rehoboam’s wives, and mother of Abijah (2 Chr. 13:2).

urijah_2899.name: Urijah
urijah_2899.about: The father of Meremoth, mentioned in Ezra 8:33.

urijah_2903.name: Urijah
urijah_2903.about: A high priest in the time of Ahaz (2 Kings 16:10-16), at whose bidding he constructed an idolatrous altar like one the king had seen at Damascus, to be set up instead of the brazen altar.

urijah_2904.name: Urijah
urijah_2904.about: One of the priests who stood at the right hand of Ezra’s pulpit when he read and expounded the law (Neh. 8:4).

urijah_2905.name: Urijah
urijah_2905.about: A prophet of Kirjath-jearim in the reign of Jehoiakim, king of Judah (Jer. 26:20-23). He fled into Egypt from the cruelty of the king, but having been brought back he was beheaded and his body “cast into the graves of the common people.”

uz_2908.name: Uz (son of Aram)
uz_2908.about: The son of Aram, and grandson of Shem (Gen. 10:23; 1 Chr. 1:17).

uz_2909.name: Uz (son of Dishan)
uz_2909.about: One of the Horite “dukes” in the land of Edom (Gen. 36:28).

uzal_2911.name: Uzal
uzal_2911.about: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan (Gen. 10:27; 1 Chr. 1:21), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

uzzah_2916.name: Uzzah
uzzah_2916.about: Strength, a son of Abinadab, in whose house the men of Kirjath-jearim placed the ark when it was brought back from the land of the Philistines (1 Sam. 7:1). He with his brother Ahio drove the cart on which the ark was placed when David sought to bring it up to Jerusalem. When the oxen stumbled, Uzzah, in direct violation of the divine law (Num. 4:15), put forth his hand to steady the ark, and was immediately smitten unto death.

uzzi_2917.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2917.about: The son of Bukki, and a descendant of Aaron (1 Chr. 6:5, 51; Ezra 7:4).

uzzi_2919.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2919.about: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

uzzi_2920.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2920.about: A Benjamite, a chief in the tribe (1 Chr. 9:8).

uzzi_2921.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2921.about: A son of Bani. He had the oversight of the Levites after the return from captivity (Neh. 11:22).

uzzi_2922.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2922.about: The head of the house of Jedaiah, one of “the chief of the priests” (Neh. 12:19).

uzzi_2923.name: Uzzi
uzzi_2923.about: A priest who assisted in the dedication of the walls of Jerusalem (Neh. 12:42).

uzziah_375.name: Uzziah
uzziah_375.about: One of Amaziah’s sons, whom the people made king of Judah in his father’s stead (2 Kings 14:21; 2 Chr. 26:1). His long reign of about fifty-two years was “the most prosperous excepting that of Jehosaphat since the time of Solomon.” He was a vigorous and able ruler, and “his name spread abroad, even to the entering in of Egypt” (2 Chr. 26:8, 14).

uzziah_2926.name: Uzziah
uzziah_2926.about: The father of Jehonathan, one of David’s overseers (1 Chr. 27:25).

uzziel_2929.name: Uzziel
uzziel_2929.about: One of the sons of Kohath, and uncle of Aaron (Ex. 6:18; Lev. 10:4).

uzziel_2931.name: Uzziel
uzziel_2931.about: A son of Bela, and grandson of Benjamin (1 Chr. 7:7).

uzziel_2932.name: Uzziel
uzziel_2932.about: One of the sons of Heman (1 Chr. 25:4); called also Azareel (18).

vajezatha_2935.name: Vajezatha
vajezatha_2935.about: Purity; worthy of honour, one of Haman’s sons, whom the Jews slew in the palace of Shushan (Esther 9:9).

vashti_2937.name: Vashti
vashti_2937.about: Beautiful, the queen of Ahasuerus, who was deposed from her royal dignity because she refused to obey the king when he desired her to appear in the banqueting hall of Shushan the palace (Esther 1:10-12).

zabad_1746.name: Zabad
zabad_1746.about: The son of Shemath. He conspired against Joash, king of Judah, and slew him (2 Chr. 24:25, 26). He is called also Jozachar (2 Kings 12:21).

zabad_2947.name: Zabad
zabad_2947.about: One of David’s valiant men (1 Chr. 11:41), the descendant of Ahlai, of the “children of Sheshan” (2:31).

zabbai_2952.name: Zabbai
zabbai_2952.about: The father of Baruch, who “earnestly repaired” part of the wall of Jerusalem (Neh. 3:20; marg., “Zaccai”).

zabdi_2954.name: Zabdi
zabdi_2954.about: An ancestor of Achan (Josh. 7:1, 17, 18). He is probably the “Zimri” of 1 Chr. 2:6.

zabdi_2956.name: Zabdi
